:::

There is no best-case analog close enough to carry the bull case, and that absence is a finding: no mega-cap franchise in the register has re-rated upward from 40x without an acceleration in reported growth. What the three cautionary cases teach is a decision rule rather than a forecast: when the entry multiple is the main contributor to expected return, the growth rate has to be demonstrated before the multiple is paid. Apple at 40.0x on 8.1% consensus EPS growth is a milder version of the same configuration — 37.3x price-to-free-cash-flow against Microsoft's 51x — but the mechanism is identical, and half of Apple's last five years of return came from the multiple rather than from earnings [S154, S155].

The strongest counter-case is that the quality deserves the multiple. Apple's trailing free cash flow of $136,683M is 1.71 times Microsoft and Alphabet combined, its 2.68% cash yield grows at 8% a year, and at an 8.0% required return the reverse DCF needs only 5.3% perpetual growth, which the 8.9% five-year free-cash-flow compound has already cleared. A long-only fund that owns the S&P 500 already holds 7.25% Apple through the index; the active decision is only whether to hold more than the benchmark, and at 36.5x forward earnings the answer is no until the price or the growth changes [S97, S93].

### The price at which the case turns

The case turns at a price, and it is lower than the valuation section's original band. On $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS, 30-34x gives $273-$309, so nothing above $309 should be bought and $287 is no longer the entry point. The decision tree has three branches: watch now at zero position until the FY2026 fourth-quarter print on 2026-11-02 and the December-2026 quarter; buy a starter at or below $309 if gross margin holds at 48% or better excluding refunds with Services growth in double digits; pass if memory takes gross margin below 47% or a final remedy removes commission. Confidence is high that the current price has no margin of safety and medium on the level of fair value, because the WACC moves the discounted value from $153 to $230. Open diligence: does the FY2026 10-K disclose intangible lives and the licensing counterparty, and does the December quarter hold gross margin near 48% with Services growth in double digits once the tariff refund drops out? The fastest falsifier is evidence that the AI cycle is producing units rather than features, which arrives with the December quarter [S7]."}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ESG评估 ESG Assessment (esg, revision 3 by Regulatory Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,864 characters)
Apple's ESG exposure is a platform-regulation problem, not a carbon or governance one: seven jurisdictions target the 75.4%-gross-margin Services pool — $109.2bn of FY2025 sales and $82.3bn of gross profit, 42.2% of the total — while fines to date (€500m EU, €150m France, $15.5m Korea) are less than 0.2% of $416.2bn of net sales and the remedies can permanently lower the highest-margin revenue Apple has. [S5, S134, S137, S136]

### The EU has established the principle; the size is still open

On 2025-04-23 the European Commission fined Apple €500m for breaching the DMA's anti-steering obligation and ordered the restrictions removed within 60 days; a separate Article 6(4) case on developer contract terms, opened 2024-06-24, remains unresolved with a statutory ceiling of 10% of worldwide net sales ($41.6bn). The fine is a rounding error, but the principle is durable: the General Court rejected Apple's challenge to its gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08. The cash question is the EU link-out commission. [S6, S134, S135]

### The US is the largest and slowest remedy risk

The DOJ and 15 states plus DC sued Apple for monopolization on 2024-03-21 in New Jersey seeking equitable relief; the motion to dismiss failed and by July 2026 the parties were in early settlement talks, with discovery to late May 2027 and no trial date. In Epic v. Apple the district court found contempt on 2025-04-30 and barred fees on out-of-app purchases; the Ninth Circuit on 2025-12-11 allowed some link-out commission and the Supreme Court agreed to review the contempt standard on 2026-06-30. Google search remedies finalised in December 2025 also threaten distribution payments inside Services, of undisclosed size. [S6, S62, S138]

### Enforcement is fragmenting; privacy is now an antitrust issue

The UK CMA designated Apple with strategic market status on 2025-10-22 and by 2026-10-20 was consulting on steering and NFC conduct requirements. Korea's communications regulator fined Apple KRW 20.81bn ($15.5m) on 2026-10-28 and ordered payment links and revised commissions, ruling a 26% fee on third-party billing evaded the 30% norm. Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act took effect on 2025-12-18, and 48 Chinese developers complained to SAMR on 2026-06-23. France's competition authority fined Apple €150m on 2025-03-31 over App Tracking Transparency, treating a privacy feature as abuse of dominance. The pattern is convergence of the global take rate toward the mid-teens, not one catastrophic penalty. [S132, S136, S140, S139, S141, S137]

### Environmental, labour and governance risks are not the discount drivers

Apple's 2025 emissions were more than 60% below 2015 and flat versus 2024, against a 2030 target of a 75% cut before carbon removals balance the remainder; removal volumes and costs are undisclosed, so the claim is only partially verified. Manufacturing remains concentrated in China, India and Vietnam, and the 10-K flags supplier industrial-accident risk; India's production-linked incentive has shifted capacity — cumulative iPhone exports passed $50bn by December 2025 and reached ₹2 lakh crore in FY2026 — but this is subsidy-supported diversification, not a structural cost advantage. Governance is cleaner than the sector: one share class, an independent chair in Art Levinson and eight directors; the 2026 proxy discloses no material related-party transactions beyond a former operating chief's family member earning above $120,000, and Tim Cook's 2025 target pay was $59m with 92% support on the 2025 say-on-pay vote. The live issues are succession (Cook is 65) and political exposure: shareholders rejected a "China Entanglement Audit" proposal on 2026-02-24. There is no dual-class discount. [S144, S145, S146, S143, S5, S52, S100]

### Policy is two different risks: sunk tax and reversible trade

The policy matrix separates sunk tax from reversible trade. State Aid is finished cash — the ECJ confirmed the Commission's 2016 decision on 2024-09-10 — a precedent risk, not an open liability. Tariffs are the opposite: the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple is claiming refunds, the Section 232 semiconductor review imposed no tariffs on Apple's products on 2026-01-14, but Section 301 actions remain live. Price trade policy as gross-margin volatility, not permanent impairment. [S6]

### What the investor should price

Separate the fine from the remedy. Fines to date are immaterial, and even a maximum DMA fine would be a single charge. The durable exposure is the commission pool: the matrix shows what a cut in Services gross profit would do to operating income. That argues for a haircut to Services earnings, not for avoiding the stock. Confidence is medium because Apple does not disclose App Store revenue or take rates, and the DOJ and EU timetables have slipped repeatedly.

### Diligence questions

Five questions would change the assessment: what share of Services revenue and gross profit is App Store commission revenue by region; what commission Apple collects on US and EU link-outs; whether Article 6(4) brings periodic penalties or structural separation; the annual value of Google search-distribution payments; and the contracted volume and cost of carbon removals behind Apple 2030. The first two sit outside the public filing set; a PACER data request has been filed. If App Store commission revenue is below a tenth of Services gross profit, regulation is a sentiment issue; if a quarter or more, an earnings issue.

Apple scores 5.7 out of 10, and the score is a verdict on price rather than on quality. The business earns a 9 and the ecosystem an 8, but valuation earns a 2 and regulatory exposure a 4, and those two dimensions carry 30% of the weight against a 36.5x forward multiple that the market has already paid. The composite is the weighted average of the table below; quality justifies a premium multiple, not the size of the premium the shares now carry [S93].

The quality scores are not in dispute. A franchise that converts a quarter of its revenue into gross profit and funds its buybacks from operations rather than from the balance sheet deserves a premium to the market, and the four-peer median is pulled down by a memory maker whose earnings multiple is lowest exactly when its earnings peak. But the premium now paid is at a cyclical high in gross margin and at the top of a five-year re-rating, so the table separates the franchise, which is the strongest in mega-cap technology, from the entry price, which is not.

### The recommendation and what changes it

The rating is Watchlist with a zero position, a 12-24 month horizon and medium evidence confidence. It changes in three directions. Downside: the bear case already carries a 40% weight at $224 (-35.8%); at 26x on bear EPS of $8.00 the value is $208 (-40%), and a final EU structural remedy that removes commission makes the bear the base at $270. Upside: at an 8.0% required return the same cash flows support $259-$330, so a ten-year yield below 4% would move the rating to Hold and raise the valuation score to 4. Operating: a December-2026 quarter with gross margin at 48% or better excluding refunds and Services growth in double digits would justify a starter position inside the band. None of the three is in evidence today [S7, S10].

### Position sizing and the regime

Position sizing is where the negative expected return becomes an instruction. The Kelly fraction, with its inputs in the table below, is negative because the probability-weighted outcome sits below the current price, so the optimal bet is zero. A long-only fund that wants the name would cap it at the weight in the table once the entry conditions are met, because the downside is a multiple event rather than a solvency event: net cash and the services annuity survive every stress in the risk matrix.

The index is near a record with volatility mid-range and credit spreads tight, yet technology is being rotated out and the ten-year yield stands near its cycle high, so a cash yield well below it has no valuation cushion. ### Next diligence and the conditions to invest

Three actions come before any purchase. First, read the FY2026 10-K due with the 2026-11-02 results for the intangible note — lives, counterparty and the $5,075M current portion that implies $0.16 of FY2027 amortisation — and for the fourth-quarter buyback pace. The buyer, the channel and the loss reasons are spread thin: section 1 gives the 40% direct / 60% indirect split and nothing more; no section states who authorises an upgrade decision in enterprise or government, how the carrier subsidy and trade-in mechanic prices the upgrade, or what a buyer who rejected the iPhone bought instead and at what price. Section 5 explains share shifts at market level but not at the point of sale.

arguments.notes: Questions I would ask the owner in committee. (1) Selling: Apple's hardest sale is not capability but the price ladder — the iPhone 18 Pro at $1,199 enters a memory-cost cycle with lukewarm pre-orders (S151), so what evidence is there that the installed base will pay the increment rather than hold devices one more year? The upgrade cycle length is the single unmeasured variable and Apple does not disclose it. (2) Budget owner: on consumer hardware the buyer and the payer are the same person, so the real gate is the carrier's trade-in subsidy and the instalment plan; in enterprise and government the buyer is an IT procurement function where Apple's share is not disclosed anywhere in the report. (3) Sales cycle: consumer is same-day, enterprise is a refresh cycle; the report never says which share of revenue is which, and that gap matters because the enterprise tail is what makes a hardware decline slow rather than sharp. (4) Why adoption is not faster: the installed base grew 6.4% against 16.1% revenue growth — the report explains this as monetisation per device, which is right, but it does not ask whether a base growing at 6.4% can carry 8-10% revenue growth once the price lever runs out. (5) Lost deals: the Huawei case in China is the documented loss and the report covers it well; the undocumented losses — India below $400, Europe mid-market — are asserted from share data rather than from buyer evidence. None of these is a Critical gap for a Watchlist verdict, but they are what a partner would press on if the recommendation moved to a buy.

arguments.notes: Stress arithmetic. Gross margin: 504 x 1% = $5.04bn; after tax $4.25bn; /14.6bn shares = $0.29-0.30 EPS. A 300bp miss removes $0.87-0.90, 9.4% of the $9.56 consensus, taking base value at 34x from $325 to $294 and at 26x to $225. Google payment: $20bn x 0.844 / 14.6 = $1.16 a share; half is $0.58; so a 50% cut takes FY2027 EPS to $8.98 and 34x value to $305, and a full loss to $8.40 and $286. Services: a 1,000bp cut on half of the $149bn commission-bearing pool is $7.45bn of gross profit, $0.43 a share. All three together with a 300bp margin miss give $7.67 and $261 at 34x, which is a 25% downside on a base multiple — that is the number the report should show as its compound bear. Peer-set sensitivity: applying 21.3x (three US peers) to TTM EPS gives $186 and 18.1x gives $158, so the conclusion does not depend on including Samsung; the own-history 31.1x average gives $271; every multiple method lands below $300 and none above $348.91. Reverse DCF: at 9.5% the required ten-year FCF compound is 15%, at 8.0% the perpetual rate is 5.3%, and the fair WACC at 3.5% terminal growth is 6.8% — a 1.6% equity risk premium at 1.1 beta, which no long-only mandate underwrites. Thirty per cent worse on the bear case (EPS $6.02) gives $157 at 26x and still no solvency stress on $62,173M of net cash. The thesis survives every adverse stress by construction, because it is a no-position call; what it is not robust to is the opposite tail — a ten-year yield below 4% with the multiple held at 40x, which the report identifies and quantifies at $330-$404 and which is why the rating is Watchlist rather than Avoid.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 3 by Lead Analyst, 8,919 characters)
Apple passes the first three tests of the thesis and fails the fourth, which is the only one that decides a purchase at today's price. The need is real and measured: more than 2.5 billion active devices generated $364,357M of revenue in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone at $196,515M and Services at $91,728M, and the group turned 49.1% of that revenue into gross profit and $136,683M of trailing revenue into free cash flow at 1.06 times net income on capex of 2.2% of sales. The capability is defensible: silicon-OS co-design, an in-house modem, four FDA clearances and 65% of the $600-plus handset tier are not replicable within a product cycle. The economics scale: Services earns a 76% gross margin on a quarter of revenue and needs no new distribution. What fails is the price. At $348.91 the buyer pays 40.0x trailing earnings, 32.5x EV/EBIT and 36.5x FY2027E EPS against a four-peer median of 18.1x and an S&P 500 forward multiple of 18.59x, for a company whose consensus EPS growth decelerates to 8.1% in FY2027 [S6].

### The disagreement is about what produced 2026

Our difference with consensus is about the durability of the current growth rate, not about quality. The 43-analyst consensus target of $332.39 sits 4.7% below the close, and Sell plus Strong Sell ratings rose from one to six between May and October 2026 while the shares gained 28.6%, so the sell side is behind the price rather than bearish on the franchise. We agree with the quality call and disagree that 2026 revealed a second growth engine: global shipments fall 16.7% while ASPs rise 27.6%, so growth is price and mix; Apple's share gain came partly from Android vendors retreating under memory costs; and 2 points of the June-quarter 50.1% gross margin were one-off tariff refunds. The edge is narrow and it is about price rather than insight — if the ten-year yield falls below 4%, the same cash flows support a materially higher value and the caution weakens [S93].

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 20% | AI replacement cycle extends; the foldable iPhone Duo opens a new price tier; Services holds double-digit growth with advertising and cloud replacing lost commission; gross margin near 49%; multiple stays at 40x | $404, +15.8% before the 0.31% dividend; 40x FY2027E EPS of $10.10 | December-quarter unit growth above 5%; Duo pre-orders; Services above 13% | S6, S93 |
| Base | 40% | Revenue growth decelerates to 10.3% and EPS to 8.1%; gross margin normalises to 48% as refunds wash out; regulation trims rather than removes commission; multiple drifts to the FY2025 year-end 34x | $325, -6.9%; 34x FY2027E EPS of $9.56 | FY2026 results on 2026-11-02; December-quarter margin near 48% excluding refunds | S93, S6 |
| Bear | 40% | Memory costs compress hardware margin; the App Store take rate settles toward the mid-teens and the Google payments are curtailed; FY2027 EPS $8.60; multiple mean-reverts to the FY2023 26x | $224, -35.8%; 26x FY2027E EPS of $8.60 | Gross margin below 47% like-for-like; a final EU remedy; a 2027 renewal below $20bn | S134, S147, S93 |
| Probability-weighted | 100% | 20% bull, 40% base, 40% bear | $300, -14.0%; $294 if bear EPS is $8.00 | — | S6, S93 |
:::

The weights changed from the original 25/45/30, and it is the report's most important correction. The bear's three drivers are dated events already in motion — memory contracts repricing handsets, EU commission terms live since 2026-10-01, and a Google default payment on annual, non-exclusive terms under cross-appeal — while the bull's driver, an AI replacement cycle, has no unit evidence. That moves the weighted outcome from $314 to $300. At $348.91 the arithmetic gives an 8.4% annual return only if the multiple holds at 40x, below the 9.5% required return, so the buyer is paying for the bull case and receiving the base case [S6, S93].

### What has to be true

| Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gross margin holds at or above 48% excluding tariff refunds through FY2027 | medium-low | A December-2026 quarter below 47% like-for-like, or iPhone 18 price increases that do not stick | Each 100bp is $5.0bn of operating income, $0.30 of EPS and 3.1% of base-case net income | Mobile DRAM and NAND contract prices; Samsung's memory-division margin | S6, S148 |
| The App Store take rate settles at 15-26% and the Google payments survive in some form | medium | A final EU Article 6(4) structural remedy, or a US order terminating the search payments | A 10% cut in Services gross profit is $8.2bn, 6.2% of operating income | Article 6(4) decision; the Supreme Court's Epic ruling; DOJ settlement terms | S134, S147 |
| Services grows at double digits and Greater China share holds near 18% | medium | Services growth below 8% for two quarters, or China unit share below 15% | A 300bp Services shortfall is 2.2% of operating income; China is 17.8% of nine-month revenue | Quarterly Services growth; IDC China share for Q4 2026 | S6, S80 |
| The exit multiple is 34x FY2027E EPS rather than 40x | medium | A ten-year Treasury materially below 4%, or FY2028 consensus EPS above $11 | Ten points of multiple move the two-year total return by 30 percentage points | Ten-year yield; sell-side target dispersion | S93, S10 |
| The buyback continues at 1.6% of shares a year and Q4 lands near $113.3bn of revenue and $1.96 of EPS | medium-high | A May 2027 authorisation materially below $100bn, or a September-quarter miss | Halving the buyback removes 0.8 points of annual EPS growth | The 2026-11-02 print; the May 2027 authorisation | S93, S5 |

### The analogs say the multiple, not the business, decides

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft | cautionary | 1999-2012 | Free cash flow per share tripled from $1.15 to $3.45 while the share price fell 54% from $58.38 to $26.71 and $100 became $51 with dividends reinvested; the P/FCF multiple went from 51x to 8x | S154 |
| Cisco | cautionary | 2000-2025 | The split-adjusted record of $80.06 set on 2000-03-27 was not exceeded until 2025-12-10, a 25-year round trip, while revenue kept growing | S155 |
| Apple | cautionary | 2005-2014 | Apple's own P/E fell from 45.25x to 12.46x while earnings grew, so a low-teens multiple is in this company's history | S156 |
:::

There is no best-case analog close enough to carry the bull case, and that absence is a finding: no mega-cap franchise in the register has re-rated upward from 40x without an acceleration in reported growth. What the three cautionary cases teach is a decision rule rather than a forecast: when the entry multiple is the main contributor to expected return, the growth rate has to be demonstrated before the multiple is paid. Apple at 40.0x on 8.1% consensus EPS growth is a milder version of the same configuration — 37.3x price-to-free-cash-flow against Microsoft's 51x — but the mechanism is identical, and half of Apple's last five years of return came from the multiple rather than from earnings [S154, S155].

The strongest counter-case is that the quality deserves the multiple. Apple's trailing free cash flow of $136,683M is 1.71 times Microsoft and Alphabet combined, its 2.68% cash yield grows at 8% a year, and at an 8.0% required return the reverse DCF needs only 5.3% perpetual growth, which the 8.9% five-year free-cash-flow compound has already cleared. A long-only fund that owns the S&P 500 already holds 7.25% Apple through the index; the active decision is only whether to hold more than the benchmark, and at 36.5x forward earnings the answer is no until the price or the growth changes [S97, S93].

### The price at which the case turns

The case turns at a price, and it is lower than the valuation section's original band. On $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS, 30-34x gives $273-$309, so nothing above $309 should be bought and $287 is no longer the entry point. The decision tree has three branches: watch now at zero position until the FY2026 fourth-quarter print on 2026-11-02 and the December-2026 quarter; buy a starter at or below $309 if gross margin holds at 48% or better excluding refunds with Services growth in double digits; pass if memory takes gross margin below 47% or a final remedy removes commission. Confidence is high that the current price has no margin of safety and medium on the level of fair value, because the WACC moves the discounted value from $153 to $230. Open diligence: does the FY2026 10-K disclose intangible lives and the licensing counterparty, and does the December quarter hold gross margin near 48% with Services growth in double digits once the tariff refund drops out? The quality scores are not in dispute. But the premium now paid is at a cyclical high in gross margin and at the top of a five-year re-rating, so the table separates the franchise, which is the strongest in mega-cap technology, from the entry price, which is not.

### The recommendation and what changes it

The rating is Watchlist with a zero position, a 12-24 month horizon and medium evidence confidence. It changes in three directions. Downside: the bear case already carries a 40% weight at $224 (-35.8%); at 26x on bear EPS of $8.00 the value is $208 (-40%), and a final EU structural remedy that removes commission makes the bear the base at $270. Apple's risk is not a broken franchise but three repricings arriving together — the memory inside its phones, the two services cash flows it does not disclose, and the discount rate — and the valuation prices only the third. Nine-month FY2026 revenue of $364,357M and a 49.1% gross margin describe a cyclical high, which is when a 40.0x trailing multiple has least room. I keep the recommendation and change the weights: bear from 30% to 40%, bull from 25% to 20%, because the bull's central assumption, an AI-driven replacement cycle, has no unit evidence while the bear's drivers are dated events already in motion. That moves the weighted outcome from $314 to $300, and to $294 if bear EPS is $8.00 rather than $8.60; the entry band should fall from $287-$325 to $273-$309 on $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS. Memory is the likeliest single driver at 65% probability: mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% quarter on quarter for LPDDR5X and 70-75% for LPDDR4X in the second quarter of 2026, average DRAM content still rises to 8.5GB a handset in 2026, and the July 2026 10-Q says component costs may materially negatively impact gross margin and revenue. Every 100bp of gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, $0.30 of EPS and 3.1% of base-case net income, so a 300bp miss costs $0.90, or 9.4% of the $9.56 consensus. The pass-through test is already running: the iPhone 18 Pro opened at $1,199 and pre-order wait times were "lukewarm", with GF Securities' Jeff Pu cutting production estimates in the week of 2026-09-15. Price defends the margin and price suppresses the units, so the two levers cannot both work at full strength; a December-2026 quarter below 47% gross margin like-for-like settles it. ### Services is named but not sized

Google's payment to be Safari's default has been reported at $20bn a year since the 2022 trial record; Apple discloses neither the sum nor its margin, so the figure is unverified by the company. At $20bn it is 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109,158M and 12.9% of trailing operating income of $154,859M. The US remedy kept the payments lawful, banned exclusivity and moved contracts to annual renegotiation; Google filed its defence of the Safari agreement by 2026-05-22 and the remedy is under cross-appeal. Half of it is $0.56 of EPS, 5.9% of consensus. The App Store: $149bn of the $1.4trn ecosystem is commission-bearing digital goods, and Apple's EU terms from August 2026 charge 5% on transactions outside the store and 20% on external payment links from 2026-10-01, against a 15% US proposal. A 1,000bp cut on half that pool is another $0.42. Together $0.98 — 10.3% of $9.56, the whole of the bear case's EPS haircut before memory, China or the renminbi. [S147, S150, S81]

It applies a defensible multiple to a haircut two services items exhaust and leaves nothing for the cost shock already contracted. Refinancing is the stress that does not bind on $62,173M of net cash. Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, but the amortisation that never appears as a line item is visible on the balance sheet: the current portion of intangible assets, net rose to $5,075M from $2,208M, putting $2.9bn more amortisation into the next twelve months — 55bp of FY2027 revenue, $0.16 of EPS, 1.7% of consensus. Gross intangibles of $38,220M grew $13,270M in nine months while other purchase obligations rose $14.5bn to $29.3bn, so the item is a contracted cash cost as well as an accrual; paid over three years it is $4.8bn a year, 3.5% of trailing free cash flow. That is why 1.06x conversion is arithmetically sound and economically incomplete: had the $13,270M been cash, conversion was 0.96x. Inventories rose 94% to $11,092M, and the discount model deducts $13.7bn of stock compensation but not the $17.7bn annualised intangible purchases — which flatters value. [S6, S47]

### 40x needs a discount rate no long-only fund can underwrite

On the valuation's cash flows and 3.5% terminal growth, $348.91 is fair at a WACC near 6.8% — an equity risk premium of 1.6% over a 4.99% Treasury at a 1.1 beta. At 8.0% the value is $259, at 8.5% $233, at 9.5% $183; a 150bp fall in the ten-year to 3.5% still leaves $233, so 40x needs a required return below 7%. Two supports are weaker than the conclusion: the 18.1x peer median includes Samsung at 12.9x, a memory maker whose P/E is lowest exactly when its earnings peak, and the three US peers alone give 21.3x, so the premium is 88% rather than 122%. The $158 peer value and $183 DCF are below any multiple a premium franchise trades at, leaving the reverse DCF — 6.8% perpetual growth at 9.5% — as the argument to carry into committee. The buyback is not value-destructive because 2.5% compares badly with a 4.99% coupon; it is value-destructive because the price exceeds the valuation's own intrinsic value, and management agrees: repurchases fell 12.0% to $62,094M in nine months and no insider bought a share in the twelve months to 2026-10-29 while $208.0m was sold. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 创始人与核心团队 Founding Team & Key Personnel (team, revision 5 by Company Analyst, 8,919 characters)
Apple's capital-allocation record is exceptional and its 2025-2026 product execution is not: the company returned $73.9bn, 63% of operating cash flow, in nine months while growing revenue 16%, but that growth needed a 33% rise in R&D and a $13.3bn build in gross intangibles, and the CEO, COO, CFO and general counsel all changed inside twenty months. John Ternus, 50 when appointed, became chief executive and a director on 2026-09-01; Tim Cook, 65, moved to executive chair after fifteen years as CEO; Sabih Khan, 58, has been chief operating officer since 2025-07-25 and joined Apple in August 1995; Kevan Parekh has been chief financial officer since January 2025; Deirdre O'Brien is a senior vice president; Jennifer Newstead became general counsel on 2026-03-01. The six named executive officers in the 2026 proxy — Cook, Kate Adams, Khan, Luca Maestri, O'Brien and Parekh — include no AI or machine-learning title, so the function's leadership is not disclosed through Section 16 or proxy channels [S54, S52].

The succession is continuity by design, and that is the point to price. Ternus holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Pennsylvania and worked as a mechanical engineer at Virtual Research Systems before joining Apple's product design team in 2001; he became a vice president of hardware engineering in 2013 and joined the executive team in 2021, and the company credits him with the iPad and AirPods introductions and 3D-printed titanium work in Apple Watch Ultra. Apple has done this before: Cook, an Auburn industrial engineer with a Duke MBA and a Fuqua scholarship, was an operations executive promoted from within in 2011 and leaves an installed base above 2.5 billion active devices in more than 200 countries, Services grown 28% to $109.2bn between FY2023 and FY2025, and 8 hardware launches in FY2025 alone — iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, Watch Series 11, Watch SE 3, Watch Ultra 3 and AirPods Pro 3. Independent reporting says the same from outside — a well-liked product engineer expected to make "small touches" rather than a disruptive break, and explicitly not the product visionary type, against a record including Vision Pro, delayed Siri work and a criticised Liquid Glass redesign. Continuity protects the cash engine; it supplies no evidence of a new product cycle [S112, S111, S87].

Capital allocation is where this team earns its premium, and the peer contrast is stark. In nine months of FY2026 Apple returned $73.9bn — $62.1bn of repurchases and $11.8bn of dividends — equal to 63% of $117.0bn of operating cash flow, while spending $6.8bn, or 1.9% of revenue, on capital expenditure; FY2025 was $89.3bn of repurchases plus $15.4bn of dividends under a $100bn authorisation, dividend raised to $0.26 then $0.27. Microsoft chose the opposite trade in FY2026, funding $139.5bn of investing outflows from $182.9bn of operating cash flow and lifting capital spending by $51.4bn for AI capacity. Apple's returns on capital are high because it owns almost no compute [S6, S5, S50].

The spending pattern says the company knows it is behind. Research and development went from $29,915m in FY2023 to $31,370m in FY2024 and $34,550m in FY2025, then reached $34,035m in nine months of FY2026, up 33% year on year and 9.3% of revenue, with management attributing it to AI infrastructure and headcount. In the same nine months gross intangible assets rose to $38,220m from $24,950m and other purchase obligations to $29.3bn from $14.8bn. Apple is buying capability as well as building it; the filing discloses neither the counterparty nor the exclusivity, and operating margin held at 33.6% only because gross margin rose 2.3 percentage points. A licensing commitment of that size is a permanent transfer of margin to an unnamed party, so it belongs in the valuation work as an assumption rather than a footnote [S6, S5].

Pay and board composition reinforce the status quo. Cook's 2025 target equity was $50m with 75% performance-based, his base salary has not changed since 2016, his total target compensation sits in the 80th to 90th percentile of the primary peer group, and 2021-granted performance RSUs vested at 187% of target on 2024-10-01, or 477,301 shares, on relative total shareholder return against the S&P 500; he has already met the age-65, ten-year condition for retirement vesting. After the transition the board has nine directors aged 51 to 77, including Levinson (75, since 2000), Sugar (77, since 2010), Jung (67, since 2008) and Wagner (64, since 2014), with Wanda Austin (2024) the only new independent since 2021. Relative-TSR scorecards pay for beating the index, a target reachable through buybacks and margin management without a new product cycle, and oversight of the AI transition sits with a board whose members have finance, consumer-brand and aerospace backgrounds rather than AI operating experience [S52, S54].

Insider behaviour gives no support to the price. Over the twelve months to 2026-10-29 there were 46 sale transactions of 687,127 shares for $208.0m, 43 under Rule 10b5-1 plans, and no purchases; Art Levinson sold $86.7m, Cook $80.4m, O'Brien $23.1m and Ternus $8.5m on 2026-10-02. Plans mute the sales; the signal is no discretionary purchase between $300 and $345. The counter-case is about product rather than people: independent reporting describes an unresolved AI gap versus OpenAI, a memory shortage squeezing margins and product misfires, while the same filings show 16% revenue growth and 22% iPhone growth, so the team is executing the current cycle well and the next one is unproven. Confidence is high on the record and low on the forward judgement. Four checks matter: Ternus's pay metrics, the executive who owns AI, the licensing counterparty, and whether the board adds an operating AI director [S41, S87].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 发展方向与战略 Development Strategy (strategy, revision 2 by Product Analyst, 8,679 characters)
Apple's strategy is a defence that is working, but it is a defence. Services at a 75.4% gross margin, a premium multi-launch product cadence and Indian assembly are turning a maturing hardware franchise into a higher-margin, less tariff-exposed annuity — while the two forces that set the ceiling, competition law in Brussels and Washington and the cost of renting intelligence from Google, are outside management's control [S115]. The plan protects cash generation; it does not restore growth.

### Services carry the margin, and the law is repricing them

Services reached $109,158m in FY2025, up 13.5% from $96,169m, at a 75.4% gross margin against 73.9% a year earlier, and grew 14% to $91,728m in the nine months to 2026-06-27 with a 75.6% margin in the June quarter. Because Apple books only its commission on third-party App Store sales, on a net basis, a dollar of services revenue carries 75 cents of gross profit against a consolidated gross margin of 46.9% in FY2025 and 50.1% in Q3 FY2026, so every point of mix shift raises group profitability without a single extra iPhone sold. That engine is now being repriced by courts and regulators rather than by competitors. On 2025-04-30 the California District Court found Apple in violation of the 2021 Epic injunction and barred it from imposing any commission on purchases made outside an app, referring the matter to the U.S. Attorney for possible criminal contempt, with the Ninth Circuit hearing Apple's expedited appeal in October 2025; in Europe the Commission fined Apple €500m on 2025-04-23 and its Article 6(4) investigation into Apple's contract terms remains open, carrying potential fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales; and the Department of Justice's antitrust suit, filed on 2024-03-21, seeks equitable relief over the same conduct [S5]. Because Apple has already introduced alternative fee structures and external purchase links in the EU, some revenue migrates rather than vanishing, but the direction is one-way: from commission, which scales with third-party commerce and costs nothing, to advertising, subscriptions and device price, which Apple must earn back every year.

### Manufacturing diversification is real but partial

India assembled 23% of global iPhone output in 2025, up from 14% in 2024, and is projected to reach 28% in 2026, while China's share fell from 83% to 74% [S119, S6]. That is the fastest supply-chain shift in Apple's history and it is being paid for twice: duplicated tooling and lower ramp yields on one side, dependence on Chinese components on the other, since Indian final assembly still imports much of what it screws together. Scale is the offset. Apple secured components for 80 million new-model phones for the second half of 2026 and plans more than 220 million units of production in 2026, which lets it pre-buy memory while Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo cut targets below 100 million units each, and inventories rose to $11,092m from $5,718m in nine months. Tariff policy remains live: the U.S. Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple has applied for refunds, while Section 301 duties and the Section 232 semiconductor investigation continue.

### China: revenue up, units down, share up

Greater China revenue rose 22% to $18,816m in Q3 FY2026 and 30% to $64,839m in nine months, after falling 4% in FY2025 and 8% in FY2024. The unit picture is different: China's smartphone market fell 15.4% year on year in Q3 2026, Apple's shipments fell 4.3%, its share rose to 17.8% from 15.8%, and Huawei grew 17.3% to 21.1% [S5, S122]. Apple is therefore monetising a shrinking market through mix and price rather than winning volume — defensible while the installed base upgrades to Pro and foldable models, fragile if Huawei's domestic supply chain keeps improving or price elasticity bites. The "China share loss" bear case was right about the trend through FY2025 and wrong about 2026 so far.

### Capital allocation is the strategy's quiet centre

Apple spent $6,799m on property, plant and equipment in nine months, 1.9% of revenue, while raising R&D 33% to $34,035m: the AI build is an operating cost, not a capital programme. That leaves cash for shareholders — $10.0bn of accelerated share repurchases entered in May 2026 and a $0.27 quarterly dividend — against $146.5bn of cash and marketable securities and $82.3bn of term debt at 2026-06-27. Net income rose 27% and diluted EPS 29% in the June quarter, so buybacks added 1.6 points of per-share growth [S6, S47]. The risk is not leverage but under-investment: buying capability from Google protects the margin while leaving Apple without owned compute or models, and gross intangibles rising from $24,950m to $38,220m in nine months suggests more value is being purchased than built.

### Resources fit the plan, with one exception

The organisation changed at the top on 2026-09-01, when John Ternus moved from Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering to CEO and Tim Cook became Executive Chair. A hardware engineer running a hardware-led strategy is continuity, and the first launch under him came in on schedule [S54]. The exception is political capital: the decisions that matter most over the next three years — the DMA Article 6(4) remedy, the Ninth Circuit appeal and the DOJ case — are legal negotiations in which a product engineer has less experience than the chair he replaced.

### Partners and dependencies

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google | Gemini models and cloud for the next Apple Foundation Models | 2026-01-12, multi-year, non-exclusive | Active; powers "Siri AI" | S115 |

| Memory suppliers | DRAM and NAND; talks reported with CXMT and YMTC for China sales | 2026-07, reported | Negotiating, unconfirmed by Apple | S113 |

### What must be true within twelve months

Four tests decide whether this is a durable annuity or a melting ice cube. Gross margin must hold near the mid-forties once the tariff refund washes out of the comparison while memory costs rise; the December 2026 quarter is the first clean read. Services growth must stay in double digits with advertising and cloud replacing any commission lost to the Epic order and the DMA — a mix the company has not had to prove for a full year. The iPhone Duo must sell into its planned volume, because a miss would confirm that premium pricing has reached the limit of what the installed base will pay. And no adverse final remedy should land in Brussels or at the Ninth Circuit that removes commission revenue retroactively. The signposts are concrete: the December-quarter margin, the advertising-versus-App-Store split in the FY2026 10-K, any disclosed size for the Gemini contract, IDC's China share for Q4 2026 and the Article 6(4) decision.

For a long-only watchlist the conclusion is that Apple's strategy earns ownership of the cash flow rather than payment for growth: the services annuity justifies a premium multiple while growth holds in double digits, the buyback compounds per-share value, and the plan creates no new growth engine before 2028. What the record cannot settle is the economics of the AI arrangement — the fee, the term and whether Apple retains query data — and the value of the health and finance adjacencies, neither of which is broken out; Apple discloses no services sub-segment revenue, so the durability of the margin engine has to be inferred from aggregate growth. Confidence in the direction of the strategy is high and in its durability medium, because the plan is well funded and well executed but its two binding constraints are a regulator and a competitor."}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 发展方向与战略 Development Strategy (strategy, revision 2 by Product Analyst, 8,679 characters)
Apple's strategy is a defence that is working, but it is a defence. Services at a 75.4% gross margin, a premium multi-launch product cadence and Indian assembly are turning a maturing hardware franchise into a higher-margin, less tariff-exposed annuity — while the two forces that set the ceiling, competition law in Brussels and Washington and the cost of renting intelligence from Google, are outside management's control [S115]. The plan protects cash generation; it does not restore growth.

### Services carry the margin, and the law is repricing them

Services reached $109,158m in FY2025, up 13.5% from $96,169m, at a 75.4% gross margin against 73.9% a year earlier, and grew 14% to $91,728m in the nine months to 2026-06-27 with a 75.6% margin in the June quarter. Because Apple books only its commission on third-party App Store sales, on a net basis, a dollar of services revenue carries 75 cents of gross profit against a consolidated gross margin of 46.9% in FY2025 and 50.1% in Q3 FY2026, so every point of mix shift raises group profitability without a single extra iPhone sold. That engine is now being repriced by courts and regulators rather than by competitors. On 2025-04-30 the California District Court found Apple in violation of the 2021 Epic injunction and barred it from imposing any commission on purchases made outside an app, referring the matter to the U.S. Attorney for possible criminal contempt, with the Ninth Circuit hearing Apple's expedited appeal in October 2025; in Europe the Commission fined Apple €500m on 2025-04-23 and its Article 6(4) investigation into Apple's contract terms remains open, carrying potential fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales; and the Department of Justice's antitrust suit, filed on 2024-03-21, seeks equitable relief over the same conduct [S5]. Because Apple has already introduced alternative fee structures and external purchase links in the EU, some revenue migrates rather than vanishing, but the direction is one-way: from commission, which scales with third-party commerce and costs nothing, to advertising, subscriptions and device price, which Apple must earn back every year.

### Manufacturing diversification is real but partial

India assembled 23% of global iPhone output in 2025, up from 14% in 2024, and is projected to reach 28% in 2026, while China's share fell from 83% to 74% [S119, S6]. That is the fastest supply-chain shift in Apple's history and it is being paid for twice: duplicated tooling and lower ramp yields on one side, dependence on Chinese components on the other, since Indian final assembly still imports much of what it screws together. Scale is the offset. Apple secured components for 80 million new-model phones for the second half of 2026 and plans more than 220 million units of production in 2026, which lets it pre-buy memory while Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo cut targets below 100 million units each, and inventories rose to $11,092m from $5,718m in nine months. Tariff policy remains live: the U.S. Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple has applied for refunds, while Section 301 duties and the Section 232 semiconductor investigation continue.

### China: revenue up, units down, share up

Greater China revenue rose 22% to $18,816m in Q3 FY2026 and 30% to $64,839m in nine months, after falling 4% in FY2025 and 8% in FY2024. The unit picture is different: China's smartphone market fell 15.4% year on year in Q3 2026, Apple's shipments fell 4.3%, its share rose to 17.8% from 15.8%, and Huawei grew 17.3% to 21.1% [S5, S122]. Apple is therefore monetising a shrinking market through mix and price rather than winning volume — defensible while the installed base upgrades to Pro and foldable models, fragile if Huawei's domestic supply chain keeps improving or price elasticity bites. The "China share loss" bear case was right about the trend through FY2025 and wrong about 2026 so far.

### Capital allocation is the strategy's quiet centre

Apple spent $6,799m on property, plant and equipment in nine months, 1.9% of revenue, while raising R&D 33% to $34,035m: the AI build is an operating cost, not a capital programme. That leaves cash for shareholders — $10.0bn of accelerated share repurchases entered in May 2026 and a $0.27 quarterly dividend — against $146.5bn of cash and marketable securities and $82.3bn of term debt at 2026-06-27. Net income rose 27% and diluted EPS 29% in the June quarter, so buybacks added 1.6 points of per-share growth [S6, S47]. The risk is not leverage but under-investment: buying capability from Google protects the margin while leaving Apple without owned compute or models, and gross intangibles rising from $24,950m to $38,220m in nine months suggests more value is being purchased than built.

### Resources fit the plan, with one exception

The organisation changed at the top on 2026-09-01, when John Ternus moved from Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering to CEO and Tim Cook became Executive Chair. A hardware engineer running a hardware-led strategy is continuity, and the first launch under him came in on schedule [S54]. The exception is political capital: the decisions that matter most over the next three years — the DMA Article 6(4) remedy, the Ninth Circuit appeal and the DOJ case — are legal negotiations in which a product engineer has less experience than the chair he replaced.

### What must be true within twelve months

Four tests decide whether this is a durable annuity or a melting ice cube. Gross margin must hold near the mid-forties once the tariff refund washes out of the comparison while memory costs rise; the December 2026 quarter is the first clean read. Services growth must stay in double digits with advertising and cloud replacing any commission lost to the Epic order and the DMA — a mix the company has not had to prove for a full year. The iPhone Duo must sell into its planned volume, because a miss would confirm that premium pricing has reached the limit of what the installed base will pay. And no adverse final remedy should land in Brussels or at the Ninth Circuit that removes commission revenue retroactively. The signposts are concrete: the December-quarter margin, the advertising-versus-App-Store split in the FY2026 10-K, any disclosed size for the Gemini contract, IDC's China share for Q4 2026 and the Article 6(4) decision.

For a long-only watchlist the conclusion is that Apple's strategy earns ownership of the cash flow rather than payment for growth: the services annuity justifies a premium multiple while growth holds in double digits, the buyback compounds per-share value, and the plan creates no new growth engine before 2028. What the record cannot settle is the economics of the AI arrangement — the fee, the term and whether Apple retains query data — and the value of the health and finance adjacencies, neither of which is broken out; Apple discloses no services sub-segment revenue, so the durability of the margin engine has to be inferred from aggregate growth. {"url":"https://www.tomsguide.com/phones/iphones/iphone-18-pro-benchmarks-apple-just-built-the-most-powerful-phones-weve-ever-seen","title":"iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max benchmarks: These are the fastest phones we've ever tested","text":"(Image credit: Tom's Guide)

Apple made a lot of bold claims about the A20 Pro chipset that's powering the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple promised that these phones are faster and more efficient, while offering big improvements to graphics and AI processing. But how much of a difference do these new chips actually make?The A20 Pro changes things up this year, having been built with a 2nm design that offers much better transistor density than the 3nm A19 Pro from last year. On top of that Apple promises that the 6-core CPU has a pair of "super cores" that are 20% faster, plus an additional four efficiency cores. The seven-core GPU is supposed to offer 40% improved graphics, while Apple had added a second neural engine to double the new chip's AI processing power.We've been testing both new phones for our iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max review, and the benchmarking tests paint a very good picture for Apple's latest flagship. In fact, based on benchmark scores, there's been a huge performance leap that puts the likes of iPhone 17 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra to shame.If you're looking for a phone with the best performance and graphics prowess, Apple should top your shopping list. Though, it would be nice if the AI processing power was a little higher. Here's what we learned after testing the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.A20 Pro: Overall Performance

(Image credit: Tom's Guide)Every time we review a phone, we run Geekbench's benchmarking tests to gauge the overall CPU performance and how different devices compare to their contemporaries. In the case of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, we did the latest Geekbench 7 benchmark, and the older Geekbench 6 tests.

As you can see, both tests showed a massive improvement in both single- and multi-core testing. The iPhone 18 Pro came out of Geekbench 6 testing with a respective 4,735 and 12,800 in single and multi-core testing.Meanwhile Geekbench 7 saw the phone record scores of 4,022 and 11,543. The iPhone 18 Pro Max scored similarly, with Geekbench 6 scores of 4,741 / 12,789 and Geekbench 7 scores of 4,025 / 11,525Sign up to the Tom's iGuide weekly newsletter with coverage on everything from product launches to software updates, this is your go-to source for the latest updates on all the best Apple content.That's a huge improvement compared to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. Both phones came out with similar scores in both iterations of Geekbench benchmarking, with iPhone 17 Pro recording scores of 3,834/ 9,988 in Geekbench 6 and 3,138 / 8,692 with Geekbench 7. Meanwhile, the iPhone 17 Pro Max finished testing with 3,871 / 9,968 from Geekbench 6 and 3,285 / 8,999 from Geekbench 7.As for Apple's biggest rival, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, that came out with a score of 3,785 / 11,563 for Geekbench 6 and 3,149 / 10,612 with Geekbench 7. That sits in the middle of the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, and while this means Apple has Samsung beat at the moment, things may change with the release of the Galaxy S27 Ultra and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 for Galaxy chipsetA20 Pro: Graphics Performance

(Image credit: Tom's Guide)Graphics performance is often where Apple chips lag behind the Snapdragon flagship, but this year the A20 Pro has pushed well beyond what Samsung's flagship phone has to offer. In fact, considering the S26 Ultra was almost neck and neck with the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, the fact that the A20 Pro has jumped so far ahead is pretty impressive.

Alongside average frame rates of 46.4fps and 46.6fps.A20 Pro: AI performance

(Image credit: Tom's Guide)Geekbench's AI test gives us an idea of how good a phone is at overall AI processing through its Neural Engine. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## 财务分析 Financial Analysis (financials, revision 3 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,648 characters)
Apple's statements show a business that converts almost all of its profit into cash on capex that is trivial for a company of its size, but the fiscal 2026 margin rests on a tariff refund the company itself calls one-off and on an intangible build the 10-Q does not explain, so the current margin is a peak to discount rather than a run-rate to capitalise.

### Growth re-accelerated, and the tax line explains two years of noise

Nine-month FY2026 revenue rose 16.1% to $364,357M and operating income 21.7% to $122,432M, lifting the operating margin to 33.6% from 32.0% in FY2025 and 29.8% in FY2023. That acceleration sits beside a FY2023-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 4.2%, so it is a cycle, not a trend. Two accounting items explain most of the reported profit volatility either side of it: the $10.2bn one-time State Aid charge in FY2024 pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% and cut net income to $93,736M, while the June 2026 quarter's 50.1% gross margin included 2 percentage points of tariff refunds, the company's own approximation, and $0.11 of the $2.02 diluted EPS. Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, so there is no non-GAAP reconciliation to police; the reported line is the only line, and the normalisation is the reader's job. What is not accounting is the cost trend: R&D rose 32.5% to $34,035M in nine months and stock-based compensation was 2.9% of revenue, so the operating margin is being defended with pricing and mix rather than operating leverage [S5, S6, S47].

### Cash conversion is better than the FY2025 ratio suggests

FY2025's 0.88x free-cash-flow conversion is the one ratio a screen will flag, and it is an artefact. The $15.8bn Irish State Aid settlement was still in escrow at 2024-09-28 and was paid during FY2025, so cash taxes for the nine months to 2025-06-28 were $37,332M against $26,555M a year later; adjust for it and FY2025 conversion is 1.0x. In nine months to 2026-06-27, operating cash flow of $116,996M exceeded net income by $15,532M and working capital was a net $2.9bn drag rather than a source of cash, with an $8,316M receivables release and $5,671M of vendor receivables offset by a $16,266M build in other assets and a $5,461M inventory build. The structural reason conversion is high is the negative cash cycle — receivables 24.5 days, payables 98.3 days — and the structural reason it beats peers is capex: $10,041M trailing against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet, which leaves Apple's free cash flow at 1.71 times the two combined [S47, S5, S11, S13].

### The balance sheet is a net-cash position with one unexplained line

At 2026-06-27 Apple held $146,517M of cash and marketable securities against $84,344M of debt, for net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M at the FY2025 year-end. Term-debt maturities are $12,393M in 2026, $10,078M in 2027 and $9,300M in 2028, covered by maturities in the securities portfolio, and the company earns net interest income (+$670M in nine months), so coverage does not bind. Commitments are modest: $4,752M of unconditional purchase obligations due in 2026, lease liabilities of $13.7bn, deferred revenue of $14.9bn (64% current) and $23.2bn of gross unrecognised tax benefits, of which $10.6bn would hit the tax rate if recognised. The line that needs explaining is intangibles: gross intangibles rose $13,270M to $38,220M in nine months with $5,075M already current, and there is no acquisition line in investing cash flow, so this is licensed or purchased capability rather than a bought business, and its amortisation is not yet in the margin. The diligence question that follows: what are those intangibles, over what life are they amortised, and does the expense arrive in FY2027 [S6, S5]?

### Returns are extraordinary, but the reported ROIC is arithmetic, not economics

Return on assets is 36.1% on the trailing twelve months and return on equity 148.8%, both far above Microsoft's 20.1% and 30.6% and lifted by a shrinking equity base. The computed ROIC of 320.6% is meaningless: buybacks of $263,210M in FY2023-FY2025 shrank invested capital to near zero, so the denominator, not the numerator, produces the number. On $100.4bn of net operating assets the after-tax return is 128%, and on total assets 33% — a wide premium to an estimated 9-10% cost of capital built on a 4.99% ten-year Treasury yield, and the honest statement is that Apple earns $128.1bn of after-tax operating profit on $100.4bn of operating capital. Against Microsoft's 35.2% and Alphabet's 30.1% TTM ROIC the comparison is not like-for-like, because those two now carry the data-centre capital Apple does not; that is the trade an investor is making — higher returns on lighter capital, in exchange for depending on partners for AI capacity. The capital-allocation version of the same point: trailing buybacks of $82,226M plus $15,640M of dividends absorbed 72% of free cash flow and retired 1.6% of diluted shares, lifting nine-month EPS growth to 22.4% against 20.0% net income growth; but at $348.91 on 2026-10-29, or 40.0 times trailing EPS, each buyback dollar retires stock at a 2.5% earnings yield while the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, so it is per-share engineering with a below-risk-free return, covered 1.4 times by free cash flow and already slowing — $62,094M in nine months against $70,579M [S7, S10, S11, S13, S47].

### Base, upside and downside: gross margin is the variable that moves the outcome

On a base case of $504bn of FY2027 revenue (+6% on an estimated FY2026 of $475bn), a 48.0% gross margin and 15.6% operating expense, operating income is $163.3bn (32.4%) and EPS $9.30; an upside case of 10% revenue growth with a 49.5% margin gives $10.24, and a downside of a 2% revenue decline with a 45.0% margin gives $7.58. Every 100bp on gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, 3.1% of base-case net income; 100bp on the tax rate is $1.6bn, 1.2%. Gross margin dominates, and it is the line management has already flagged: memory and storage costs that price increases "may not" offset. That is the variable to underwrite — whether Apple can hold a 48% margin when Samsung is earning 55% on the components inside its phones [S59, S60].

arguments.markdown:
Apple passes the first three tests of the thesis and fails the fourth, which is the only one that decides a purchase at today's price. The need is real: more than 2.5 billion active devices generated $364,357M of revenue in nine months of FY2026, with a 49.1% gross margin and $136,683M of trailing free cash flow at 1.06x net income on capex of 2.2% of sales. The capability is defensible: silicon-OS co-design, an in-house modem, four FDA clearances and 65% of the $600-plus handset tier are not replicable within a product cycle. The economics scale: Services earns a 76% gross margin on a quarter of revenue and needs no new distribution. What fails is the price. At $348.91 the buyer pays 40.0x trailing earnings, 32.5x EV/EBIT and 36.5x FY2027E EPS against a four-peer median of 18.1x and an S&P 500 forward multiple of 18.59x on 2026-10-29, for a company whose consensus EPS growth decelerates to 8.1% in FY2027 [S6].

### The disagreement is about what produced 2026

Our difference with consensus is about the durability of the current growth rate, not about quality. The 43-analyst consensus target of $332.39 sits 4.7% below the close, and Sell plus Strong Sell ratings rose from one to six between May and October 2026 while the shares gained 28.6%: the sell side is behind the price, not bearish on the franchise. We agree with the quality call and disagree that 2026 revealed a second growth engine: global shipments fall 16.7% while ASPs rise 27.6%, so growth is price and mix; Apple's share gain came partly from Android vendors retreating under memory costs; and 2 points of the June-quarter 50.1% gross margin were one-off tariff refunds. The edge is narrow and about price rather than insight: below a 4% ten-year yield, the same cash flows support a higher value and the caution weakens [S93].

The 20/40/40 weighting rests on three dated drivers rather than on a narrative. Memory contracts are repricing handsets now: mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% quarter on quarter for LPDDR5X in Q2 2026, and inventory is up 94% to $11,092M. The EU's new commission card has been live since 2026-10-01, with the Article 6(4) case still open. And the Google default payment, reported at $20bn a year and 12.9% of trailing operating income, now runs on annual, non-exclusive terms under cross-appeal. Against that, the bull case needs an AI replacement cycle in units, and the December-2026 quarter is the first place it could show; the filings carry features, not volume. Three dated downside mechanisms against one undated upside is why base and bear carry 40% each and the bull 20%, and why the weighted outcome is $300, 14.0% below the price [S148, S134, S147, S6].

### The analogs say the multiple, not the business, decides

There is no best-case analog close enough to carry the bull case, and that absence is a finding: no mega-cap franchise in the register has re-rated upward from 40x without an acceleration in reported growth. The three cautionary cases teach a decision rule rather than a forecast: when the entry multiple is the main contributor to expected return, growth has to be demonstrated before the multiple is paid. Apple at 40.0x on 8.1% consensus EPS growth is a milder version of the same configuration — 37.3x price-to-free-cash-flow against Microsoft's 51x — but the mechanism is identical, and half of Apple's last five years of return came from the multiple rather than from earnings [S154, S155].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's risk is not a broken franchise but three repricings arriving together — the memory inside its phones, the two services cash flows it does not disclose, and the discount rate — and the valuation prices only the third. Nine-month FY2026 revenue of $364,357M and a 49.1% gross margin describe a cyclical high, which is when a 40.0x trailing multiple has least room. The probability-weighted outcome is $300 on a 20/40/40 bull/base/bear split, because three dated drivers are already in motion: memory contracts repricing handsets, the EU commission terms live since 2026-10-01, and the Google default payment on annual, non-exclusive terms under cross-appeal. The bull's AI-driven replacement cycle has no unit evidence to set against them. The entry band is $273-$300 — 30x to 33x the $9.10 blended FY2027 EPS (60% × $9.56 + 40% × $8.42), capped at the $300 expected value because 34x on $9.10, $309, sits above it. Memory is the likeliest single driver at 65% probability: mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% quarter on quarter for LPDDR5X and 70-75% for LPDDR4X in the second quarter of 2026, average DRAM content still rises to 8.5GB a handset in 2026, and the July 2026 10-Q says component costs may materially negatively impact gross margin and revenue. Every 100bp of gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, $0.30 of EPS and 3.1% of base-case net income, so a 300bp miss costs $0.90, or 9.4% of the $9.56 consensus. The pass-through test is already running: the iPhone 18 Pro opened at $1,199 and pre-order wait times were "lukewarm", with GF Securities' Jeff Pu cutting production estimates in the week of 2026-09-15. Price defends the margin and price suppresses the units, so the two levers cannot both work at full strength; a December-2026 quarter below 47% gross margin like-for-like settles it. [S6, S81, S147, S148, S151]

### Services is named but not sized

Google's payment to be Safari's default has been reported at $20bn a year since the 2022 trial record; Apple discloses neither the sum nor its margin, so the figure is unverified by the company. At $20bn it is 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109,158M and 12.9% of trailing operating income of $154,859M. The US remedy kept the payments lawful, banned exclusivity and moved contracts to annual renegotiation; Google filed its defence of the Safari agreement by 2026-05-22 and the remedy is under cross-appeal. Half of it is $0.56 of EPS, 5.9% of consensus. The App Store: $149bn of the $1.4trn ecosystem is commission-bearing digital goods, and Apple's EU terms from August 2026 charge 5% on transactions outside the store and 20% on external payment links from 2026-10-01, against a 15% US proposal. A 1,000bp cut on half that pool is another $0.42. Together $0.98 — 10.3% of $9.56, the whole of the bear case's EPS haircut before memory, China or the renminbi. [S147, S150, S81]

### The bear case is too narrow, not too harsh

It applies a defensible multiple to a haircut two services items exhaust and leaves nothing for the cost shock already contracted. Refinancing is the stress that does not bind on $62,173M of net cash. A 30% free-cash-flow cut takes the discounted value to $128, which no committee should believe for a franchise earning 76% margins on a quarter of revenue, so the honest form of that stress is EPS minus 17% at 26x, or $206. Policy is priced the same way rather than listed: the €500m fine of 2025-04-23 showed the Commission will fine, the Article 6(4) case carries a statutory cap near $41.6bn of FY2025 revenue, the General Court upheld gatekeeper status on 2026-07-08, and Korea fined Apple and Google a combined $47.6m on 2026-10-28 — cash small beside the precedent that the commission is contestable. [S93, S47, S134, S136]

### The FY2027 charge the 10-Q hides in the current portion

Earnings are clean in the narrow sense and the margin is not. Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, but the amortisation that never appears as a line item is visible on the balance sheet: the current portion of intangible assets, net rose to $5,075M from $2,208M, putting $2.9bn more amortisation into the next twelve months — 55bp of FY2027 revenue, $0.16 of EPS, 1.7% of consensus. Gross intangibles of $38,220M grew $13,270M in nine months while other purchase obligations rose $14.5bn to $29.3bn, so the item is a contracted cash cost as well as an accrual; paid over three years it is $4.8bn a year, 3.5% of trailing free cash flow. That is why 1.06x conversion is arithmetically sound and economically incomplete: had the $13,270M been cash, conversion was 0.96x. Inventories rose 94% to $11,092M, and the discount model deducts $13.7bn of stock compensation but not the $17.7bn annualised intangible purchases — which flatters value. [S6, S47]

### 40x needs a discount rate no long-only fund can underwrite

On the valuation's cash flows and 3.5% terminal growth, $348.91 is fair at a WACC near 6.8% — an equity risk premium of 1.6% over a 4.99% Treasury at a 1.1 beta. At 8.0% the value is $259, at 8.5% $233, at 9.5% $183; a 150bp fall in the ten-year to 3.5% still leaves $233, so 40x needs a required return below 7%. Two supports are weaker than the conclusion: the 18.1x peer median includes Samsung at 12.9x, a memory maker whose P/E is lowest exactly when its earnings peak, and the three US peers alone give 21.3x, so the premium is 88% rather than 122%. The $158 peer value and $183 DCF are below any multiple a premium franchise trades at, leaving the reverse DCF — 6.8% perpetual growth at 9.5% — as the argument to carry into committee. The buyback is not value-destructive because 2.5% compares badly with a 4.99% coupon; it is value-destructive because the price exceeds the valuation's own intrinsic value, and management agrees: repurchases fell 12.0% to $62,094M in nine months and no insider bought a share in the twelve months to 2026-10-29 while $208.0m was sold. [S93, S10, S41]

**The thesis breaks if the Google default payment is repriced, because the base case carries it in full.** At $20bn a year it is 12.9% of trailing operating income, Apple does not disclose it, and it now renews annually under a non-exclusive contract both parties are still appealing. A cut to $10bn takes $0.56 of FY2027 EPS; a full loss takes $1.13, turning the $9.56 base into $8.43 and the $325 base value into $287 at the same 34x — so the price today would be capitalising a payment the court has already held unlawful in its exclusive form. Open question: the 2027 renewal price is unknowable from public filings, and only the contract itself would settle it. [S147, S149]
:::

Two questions stay open and both are answerable before any purchase: what the fiscal 2026 annual report, due within days of the fourth-quarter results, discloses about intangible lives and counterparty, and whether the December quarter holds gross margin near the base case with Services growth in double digits once the tariff refund drops out. Until the first is answered the services exposure is an estimate, so the weights carry medium confidence and the bear weight could be raised further; no position at the current price survives the weighting, and the upper end of any entry band should be treated as a ceiling rather than a target.

### Services is named but not sized

Google's payment to be Safari's default has been reported at $20bn a year since the 2022 trial record; Apple discloses neither the sum nor its margin, so the figure is unverified by the company. At $20bn it is 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109,158M and 12.9% of trailing operating income of $154,859M. The US remedy kept the payments lawful, banned exclusivity and moved contracts to annual renegotiation; Google filed its defence of the Safari agreement by 2026-05-22 and the remedy is under cross-appeal. Half of it is $0.56 of EPS, 5.9% of consensus. The App Store: $149bn of the $1.4trn ecosystem is commission-bearing digital goods, and Apple's EU terms from August 2026 charge 5% on transactions outside the store and 20% on external payment links from 2026-10-01, against a 15% US proposal. A 1,000bp cut on half that pool is another $0.42. Together $0.98 — 10.3% of $9.56, the whole of the bear case's EPS haircut before memory, China or the renminbi. [S147, S150, S81]

It applies a defensible multiple to a haircut two services items exhaust and leaves nothing for the cost shock already contracted. Refinancing is the stress that does not bind on $62,173M of net cash. A 30% free-cash-flow cut takes the discounted value to $128, which no committee should believe for a franchise earning 76% margins on a quarter of revenue, so the honest form of that stress is EPS minus 17% at 26x, or $206. Policy is priced the same way rather than listed: the €500m fine of 2025-04-23 showed the Commission will fine, the Article 6(4) case carries a statutory cap near $41.6bn of FY2025 revenue, the General Court upheld gatekeeper status on 2026-07-08, and Korea fined Apple and Google a combined $47.6m on 2026-10-28 — cash small beside the precedent that the commission is contestable. [S93, S47, S134, S136]

### The FY2027 charge the 10-Q hides in the current portion

Earnings are clean in the narrow sense and the margin is not. Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, but the amortisation that never appears as a line item is visible on the balance sheet: the current portion of intangible assets, net rose to $5,075M from $2,208M, putting $2.9bn more amortisation into the next twelve months — 55bp of FY2027 revenue, $0.16 of EPS, 1.7% of consensus. Gross intangibles of $38,220M grew $13,270M in nine months while other purchase obligations rose $14.5bn to $29.3bn, so the item is a contracted cash cost as well as an accrual; paid over three years it is $4.8bn a year, 3.5% of trailing free cash flow. That is why 1.06x conversion is arithmetically sound and economically incomplete: had the $13,270M been cash, conversion was 0.96x. Inventories rose 94% to $11,092M, and the discount model deducts $13.7bn of stock compensation but not the $17.7bn annualised intangible purchases — which flatters value. [S6, S47]

On the valuation's cash flows and 3.5% terminal growth, $348.91 is fair at a WACC near 6.8% — an equity risk premium of 1.6% over a 4.99% Treasury at a 1.1 beta. At 8.0% the value is $259, at 8.5% $233, at 9.5% $183; a 150bp fall in the ten-year to 3.5% still leaves $233, so 40x needs a required return below 7%. Two supports are weaker than the conclusion: the 18.1x peer median includes Samsung at 12.9x, a memory maker whose P/E is lowest exactly when its earnings peak, and the three US peers alone give 21.3x, so the premium is 88% rather than 122%. The $158 peer value and $183 DCF are below any multiple a premium franchise trades at, leaving the reverse DCF — 6.8% perpetual growth at 9.5% — as the argument to carry into committee. The buyback is not value-destructive because 2.5% compares badly with a 4.99% coupon; it is value-destructive because the price exceeds the valuation's own intrinsic value, and management agrees: repurchases fell 12.0% to $62,094M in nine months and no insider bought a share in the twelve months to 2026-10-29 while $208.0m was sold.
