sources.claims: 8-K text: Item 5.02 (Departure or Election of Directors and Officers; Compensatory Arrangements)

sources.title: Counterpoint Research: Premium Smartphone Share in Overall Market Hits H1 Record at 29%; Apple and Samsung Lead
sources.claims: Premium smartphones (wholesale ASP $600+) reached a record 29% of global smartphone unit sales in H1 2026, up from 25% in H1 2025; Apple held 65% of premium unit sales in H1 2026 with premium sales up 9% YoY; Apple and Samsung combined 84% of the premium segment, up from 82%; premium segment volumes grew about 5% YoY.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows the premium pool is growing as a share of a shrinking market, so Apple's exposure is to value rather than units; but the Counterpoint file was read only as a search extract, not opened in full.

sources.title: Counterpoint Research: Q2 2026 Global Smartphone Shipments (lowest Q2 since 2013)
sources.claims: Global smartphone shipments fell 11% YoY in Q2 2026 to the lowest second-quarter level since 2013 as the DRAM/NAND shortage intensified; Samsung reclaimed global leadership with 24% share and the strongest YoY growth among the top five.
sources.claims_weakened: The 11% decline differs from IDC's 7.4% for the same quarter, showing tracker disagreement of about 3.6pp on the unit decline; direction (sharp contraction, premium outperformance) is consistent.

sources.title: IDC: Global Smartphone Shipments Fall 7.4% in Q2 2026 as the Memory Crisis Splits the Market in Two (final Q2 2026 data and 2026 forecast)
sources.claims: Q2 2026 worldwide smartphone shipments 276.3M units, -7.4% YoY; Samsung 22.7%, Apple 20.2% (+14.9% YoY units, +3.9pp share), Xiaomi 11.3% (-26.4%), OPPO 10.5%, vivo 7.7%; Apple on track for record 22% annual share in 2026; 2026 forecast shipments -16.7% to just over 1bn units, ASP +27.6% to $581, market value +6.3% to $613bn; memory costs up nearly 300% YoY and over 65% of low-end BOM; foldables +12.6% with Apple entering in H2 2026; 173M sub-$100 phones shipped in 2025.
sources.claims_weakened: Undermines any view that smartphone unit demand is stable through 2026-27; shows Apple's FY2026 share gains partly reflect rivals' memory-driven price rises and Apple's early supply lock, not only product strength.

sources.title: IDC: Why Huawei and Apple Grew While China's Smartphone Market Fell Again in Q2 2026
sources.claims: China Q2 2026 shipments about 66M units, -4.3% YoY, fifth straight quarterly decline; Huawei 22.6% share (+19.4% YoY units), Apple 18.1% (+24.4% units, up from 13.9%), OPPO 16.0%, vivo 16.0%, Xiaomi 12.4% (-21.7%), Honor 11.3%; first-half 2026 China 134M units, -4.2%; "618" smartphone sales down close to 15% YoY; IDC expects China YoY decline to widen to about 20% in H2 2026 and a replacement-cycle recovery around 2028-2029; top six vendors hold about 96% of the market.
sources.claims_weakened: Contradicts the 2024-25 consensus of structural Apple share loss in China: Apple gained 4.2pp of China share in Q2 2026 while Huawei also gained; both won by holding prices as Android rivals raised them.

sources.title: Reuters: Apple changes fees for alternative app stores in EU
sources.claims: Apple changed its EU App Store business terms in August 2026 to resolve its DMA dispute with the European Commission: a 5% Core Technology Commission on digital transactions in apps distributed outside the App Store (alternative marketplaces or web), and a 20% commission where developers use external payment links, with the new terms effective October 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Confirms EU take-rate compression on the most contestable slice of App Store revenue; does not quantify the revenue at risk, and the effective date means FY2026 results will not show it.

sources.title: Huawei Investment & Holding Co. 2025 Annual Report
sources.claims: Huawei 2025 annual report: revenue CNY880.9bn (about $127.5bn), net profit CNY68bn, R&D CNY192.3bn equal to 21.8% of revenue, released 2026-03-31.
sources.claims_weakened: Huawei's group revenue is dominated by ICT infrastructure and cloud, so it does not size Huawei's handset business; the figures come from the search extract of the annual report page, not a full read of the report.

sources.title: Sensor Tower: State of Mobile 2026 — global in-app purchase revenue $167bn in 2025
sources.claims: Global consumer in-app purchase revenue reached $167bn in 2025, up 10.6% YoY, with non-gaming app spending exceeding games for the first time, driven by generative-AI apps (Sensor Tower State of Mobile 2026).
sources.claims_weakened: The $167bn figure covers App Store and Google Play consumer spend and excludes advertising, cloud and commerce, so it understates the services pool Apple monetises; Apple's commission take on that spend is not disclosed.

sources.title: European Commission: Commission finds Apple and Meta in breach of the Digital Markets Act
sources.claims: The European Commission found Apple in breach of the Digital Markets Act anti-steering obligation and fined it EUR 500 million (decision announced 2025-04-23, press release IP/25/1085); Meta was fined EUR 200 million in the same decision.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any view that App Store regulation is a tail risk only: a DMA fine of EUR 500m has already been imposed on Apple's Services business in Europe.

sources.title: Apple Investor Relations: FY 26 Fourth Quarter Results event page
sources.claims: Apple's FY2026 fourth-quarter results conference call is scheduled for Monday 2026-11-02 at 2:00 p.m. PT; therefore as of 2026-10-30 the latest reported period is the fiscal third quarter ended 2026-06-27 and no FY2026 full-year figures exist yet.
sources.claims_weakened: None; it defines the data cut-off used in this report.

sources.title: CNBC: Apple overhauls EU app store fees to resolve payments clash
sources.claims: Apple overhauled its EU App Store fee structure in August 2026 to comply with the Digital Markets Act, after the EUR 500m fine; the European Commission welcomed the changes while Epic Games criticised them.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the assumption that Apple can preserve App Store take rates in the EU unchanged; also shows Apple chose compliance over litigation on fees.

sources.title: Fortune: Apple's John Ternus era — can a low-key engineer win the AI race?
sources.claims: John Ternus became Apple CEO on 2026-09-01 with Tim Cook moving to executive chair; Ternus joined Apple's product design team, became VP Hardware Engineering in 2013 (Macs, iPads), joined the senior executive team in 2021, later took on iPhone and AirPods; age 51 as of 2026-08; Apple described as a $4.6 trillion company in late August 2026; independent reporting of the AI gap versus OpenAI, Siri misses, Vision Pro as a misfire, criticised Liquid Glass iOS redesign, foldable phone arriving years after Samsung, memory chip shortage squeezing margins, and analysts describing Ternus as a continuity insider rather than a product visionary (Gene Munster, Jean-Louis Gassée).
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the idea that the CEO handover is a strategic reset: reporting suggests continuity and an unresolved AI/product-momentum gap; also implies a market value near $4.6trn in late August 2026, below a ~$5.0trn reading in late October 2026.

sources.title: IDC wrist-worn device market Q1 2026 as reported by Telbb
sources.claims: IDC Q1 2026 global wrist-worn device shipments 47.05M units, +2.2% YoY: Huawei 20.2%, Apple and Xiaomi tied at 17%, Samsung 5.8% (units down 20.7% YoY), Garmin 5.1%.
sources.claims_weakened: Second-hand trade summary of IDC data, not IDC's release; the wrist-worn category mixes smartwatches with basic bands, which flatters Huawei and Xiaomi versus Apple's smartwatch-only position.

sources.title: StatCounter: Mobile operating system market share, worldwide and United States, 2026
sources.claims: StatCounter mobile OS share: iOS 30.81% vs Android 69.17% of worldwide mobile web page views in September 2026; iOS 58.35% vs Android 41.62% in the United States in June 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Web-traffic-based share overstates iOS in the US relative to installed base and is not revenue share; the figures come from search extracts of StatCounter's series, not a page opened in full.

sources.title: Gadgets360 report of IDC Worldwide Quarterly Personal Computing Device Tracker, Q2 2026
sources.claims: IDC Q2 2026 worldwide traditional PC shipments 68.2M units, -4.9% YoY (first decline after nine quarters of growth): Lenovo 24.4% share, HP 19.1%, Dell 13.6%, Apple 9.9%, with Apple shipments up about 10% YoY against a falling market.
sources.claims_weakened: Reported by trade media citing IDC rather than read from IDC's own release; Apple's 9.9% is unit share and understates its revenue share because Mac ASPs are far above the market average.

sources.title: Microsoft to acquire Activision Blizzard — $95.00 per share, $68.7 billion all-cash
sources.claims: Microsoft agreed to acquire Activision Blizzard for $95.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $68.7B inclusive of net cash; announced 2022-01-18 and closed 2023-10-12 (TechCrunch). The largest technology acquisition on record.
sources.claims_weakened: Sets the practical ceiling for strategic M&A: at $68.7B the largest tech deal ever is 1.35% of Apple's $5,029.9B enterprise value, so a takeover premium cannot be a return driver for an Apple holder.

sources.title: Apple Q4 2026 earnings set for November 2; John Ternus's first call as CEO
sources.claims: Apple will report fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on 2026-11-02, per its investor relations calendar; the call is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET. Corroborated by Apple's investor relations event page and by AppleInsider/MacObserver coverage of the same calendar update.
sources.claims_weakened: Nothing directly; it fixes the near-term catalyst date used in the exit and valuation sections.

sources.title: Apple (AAPL) stock forecast — consensus ratings, price targets and estimates (S&P Global poll of 43 analysts)
sources.claims: Consensus of 43 analysts polled by S&P Global: average 12-month target $332.39 (-4.73% vs the $348.91 close), median $337.50 (-3.27%), low $245 (-29.8%), high $405 (+16.1%); average rating Buy, with 18 Strong Buy, 6 Buy, 13 Hold, 3 Sell and 3 Strong Sell in October 2026. FY2026E revenue $477.64B (+14.77%), EPS $8.84 (+18.46%), net income $130.00B, gross margin 48.60%, operating income $156.51B, FCF $142.36B, dividend $1.07 per share; FY2027E revenue $526.79B (+10.29%) and EPS $9.56 (+8.14%). Recent targets: Evercore ISI $380 (Oct 29), Monness $355 (from $335, Oct 28), HSBC $366 (Oct 27), JPMorgan $360 (Oct 26), BofA $370 (from $380, Oct 26).
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any claim that the sell side sees meaningful upside from $348.91; also shows Sell/Strong Sell ratings rising from 1 to 6 between May and October 2026 while the stock rose.

sources.title: Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) P/E ratio history
sources.claims: Samsung Electronics' trailing P/E was 12.9x as of October 2026, against 18.2x at the end of 2025. Investing.com's LTM series shows 11.0x, so the peer figure is 11-13x rather than a single point.
sources.claims_weakened: Widens the peer gap: Apple's 40.0x TTM P/E is ~3.1x Samsung's 12.9x, so any "Apple is fairly valued against hardware peers" claim fails. Samsung's multiple is cyclical (memory), which limits how far the comparison carries.

sources.title: Apple newsroom: App Store ecosystem reaches $1.4 trillion in developer billings and sales (2025)
sources.claims: Apple-commissioned Analysis Group study: the global App Store ecosystem facilitated over $1.4 trillion in developer billings and sales in 2025, and for more than 90% of that activity developers paid Apple no commission.
sources.claims_weakened: Company-funded study; the $1.4tn is gross third-party commerce, not Apple revenue, and the commission-bearing digital-goods slice is not disclosed. Useful to size the ecosystem, not to value Apple's take.

sources.title: Business Standard report of IDC India smartphone tracker, Q2 2026
sources.claims: India Q2 2026 smartphone shipments 33.2M units, -11.1% YoY; first-half 2026 total 64.2M units, the lowest first half in five years; average selling price rose 14.4% to about INR 30,000; Samsung and Apple were the only major vendors to grow units and Apple led the market by value.
sources.claims_weakened: Reported by Business Standard citing IDC rather than read from IDC's release; India is small in Apple's revenue mix, so the share gains matter more for the long-dated growth story than for near-term earnings.

sources.title: Three stocks are now 21% of the S&P 500 — Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft
sources.claims: Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft together made up 21% of the S&P 500 by weight as of 2026-10-07, the highest concentration on record; a separate 2026-09-24 analysis puts Nvidia and Apple together above 15% of the index.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's individual index weight is not given in the retrieved text; the claim used in the report is only that Apple is one of the three constituents that together hold 21% of the index, so passive flows are a factor in its liquidity and in any index-driven selling.

sources.title: The biggest tech acquisitions of all time — MSFT/Activision $69B, Dell/EMC $67B, Broadcom/VMware $61B
sources.claims: Ranking of the largest technology acquisitions: Microsoft/Activision Blizzard ~$69B (closed 2023), Dell/EMC ~$67B (2016), Broadcom/VMware ~$61B (2023). Used only to establish the scale ceiling of strategic M&A against Apple's $5,029.9B enterprise value.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows no precedent transaction comes within two orders of magnitude of an Apple acquisition; also means the precedent multiples in this table are for companies an order of magnitude smaller, so they do not transfer to Apple's valuation.

sources.title: AAPL stock forecast — 44 analysts, median target $338 (range $245-$405)
sources.claims: 44 Wall Street analysts covering Apple have a median 12-month price target of $338, with estimates from $245 to $405 — consistent with the S&P Global poll's $337.50 median and $245-$405 range, so the consensus target sits at or slightly below the 2026-10-29 close of $348.91.
sources.claims_weakened: Reinforces that the stock trades at or above consensus rather than at a discount; no "upside to target" argument survives.

sources.title: Duke University Board of Trustees: Tim Cook B'88
sources.claims: Tim Cook earned an MBA from Duke University as a Fuqua Scholar and a Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering from Auburn University; he joined Apple in 1998, was COO before becoming CEO in August 2011, served as CEO from 2011 to 2026 and is now executive chair; during his tenure Apple reached an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices in more than 200 countries and territories, Services grew to a more than $100 billion business, the company transitioned to Apple-designed silicon, and its carbon footprint fell more than 60% below 2015 levels while revenue nearly doubled.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the reading that Cook's tenure was only financial engineering: the record includes category creation (Watch, AirPods, Vision Pro), the Apple silicon transition and an installed base of 2.5 billion devices.

sources.title: Apple Leadership: John Ternus
sources.claims: John Ternus is Apple's CEO and a board member; he joined Apple's product design team in 2001, became a vice president of hardware engineering in 2013 and joined the executive team in 2021 as senior vice president of Hardware Engineering; he was instrumental in introducing iPad and AirPods and multiple iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch generations, and led reliability, materials and repairability work including a recycled aluminium compound and 3D-printed titanium in Apple Watch Ultra; before Apple he was a mechanical engineer at Virtual Research Systems; he holds a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Pennsylvania.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any claim that Ternus lacks product-launch or materials-engineering depth; also shows a single degree and one pre-Apple employer, with no prior executive or P&L role outside Apple.

sources.title: CNBC/Nikkei Asia: Apple plans five new iPhones through 2027, foldable push, memory shortage
sources.claims: Nikkei Asia report (via CNBC, 2026-07-02): Apple plans at least five iPhone models between H2 2026 and H1 2027; suppliers told to prepare about 10 million foldable iPhones in 2026, up from 7-8 million; components secured for about 80 million new-model phones for H2 2026; 2026 iPhone production expected above 220 million units; AI-driven memory shortage raising costs, with Bloomberg reporting talks to source memory from CXMT and YMTC; Apple raised MacBook and iPad prices in late June 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the "no new form factors" critique of Apple; also documents input-cost and supply risk that offsets product-mix gains.

sources.title: MacRumors: Everything Apple announced at the September 2026 event
sources.claims: At its 2026-09-09 "Surprise and Shine" event Apple introduced iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, its first foldable iPhone ("iPhone Duo"), new Apple Watch models and AirPods 5.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens reports that the foldable had slipped to early 2027; confirms the foldable shipped in the September 2026 cycle.

sources.title: Reuters: Apple, Google strike Gemini deal for revamped Siri
sources.claims: Apple will use Google's Gemini models for its revamped Siri under a multi-year deal announced 2026-01-12; the rebuilt Siri was described as "coming later this year", i.e. still unshipped as of January 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any claim that Apple's in-house foundation models were ready to power a competitive assistant; establishes third-party model dependency at the core of Apple Intelligence.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: Apple debuts iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max (retrieved via search result)
sources.claims: Apple's 2026-09 newsroom release for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max: powered by the A20 Pro chip, variable aperture camera, improved battery life, and "Siri AI"; devices reached Apple Store locations on 2026-09-18.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows the AI assistant and the new SoC shipped together in the September 2026 cycle, narrowing the AI feature-gap critique for the newest hardware.

sources.title: iThinkDiff: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 vs A19 Pro benchmark comparison
sources.claims: Geekbench 6 single-core: Apple A19 Pro 4,019 versus Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 3,846; the Snapdragon part leads in some multi-threaded and graphics tests.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the assumption of a large Apple CPU lead: the single-core gap narrowed to about 4-5% in the 2025-2026 generation.

sources.title: European Commission: DMA interoperability specification decisions for Apple (IP/25/816)
sources.claims: On 2025-03-19 the European Commission adopted two specification decisions under the DMA setting out measures Apple must take to comply with its interoperability obligation for iOS and iPadOS (Article 6(7)).
sources.claims_weakened: Shows DMA obligations being converted into engineering-level requirements, which erodes Apple's control of ecosystem access points such as notifications, device pairing and app distribution.

sources.title: Moneycontrol: India to assemble 28% of global iPhones in 2026 (SAG estimates)
sources.claims: Industry estimates (Smart Analytics Global, reported by Moneycontrol): India assembled 23% of global iPhone output in 2025, up from 14% in 2024, and is projected to reach 28% in 2026; China's share fell to 74% in 2025 from 83% in 2024.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that Apple's manufacturing diversification is stalled; also shows China remains the majority assembly base (about 74% in 2025).

sources.title: Lawyer Monthly: Apple loses to EU Commission on DMA gatekeeper ruling (General Court, July 2026)
sources.claims: In July 2026 the EU General Court upheld Apple's designation as a DMA gatekeeper, dismissing its challenge over the App Store and iOS and rejecting its iMessage case as inadmissible.
sources.claims_weakened: Removes the litigation route to escaping DMA obligations in Europe; makes take-rate and interoperability concessions structural rather than temporary.

sources.title: US2023/0049811 - Hinges for Folding Display Devices (Apple Inc.)
sources.claims: Apple-assigned patent publication US2023/0049811 "Hinges for Folding Display Devices": a multi-link hinge with interdigitated fingers in a friction clutch and crescent-shaped pin slots to manage folding stress on a flexible display; corresponds to granted US 12,164,344.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows Apple protected foldable hinge mechanics years before the September 2026 iPhone Duo, so the foldable is not a reactive copy; also shows the IP is hinge-mechanical rather than AI-related.

sources.title: 9to5Mac/IDC: Apple gains ground as China smartphone shipments fall 15.4% in Q3 2026
sources.claims: IDC data reported 2026-10-13: China smartphone shipments fell 15.4% year on year in Q3 2026; Apple's shipments fell 4.3% but its share rose to 17.8% from 15.8%; Huawei grew 17.3% to a 21.1% share.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the "China share loss to Huawei" story for 2026: Apple gained share in a shrinking market even as Huawei stayed first; also shows the Chinese market itself contracting sharply.

sources.claims_weakened: Shows the foldable roadmap extends beyond the 2026 iPhone Duo, so the form-factor critique of Apple is weaker than the shipped-product catalogue alone suggests.

sources.title: UK Competition and Markets Authority: Apple's mobile platform case page (SMS designation and conduct requirements)
sources.claims: CMA designated Apple as having strategic market status in its mobile platform on 2025-10-22 (mobile OS, native app distribution, mobile browser and browser engine); final commitments on app review, ranking, data use and interoperable access published 2026-04-01; steering conduct-requirement consultation opened 2026-06-30 and NFC access conduct-requirement consultation on 2026-10-20.
sources.claims_weakened: UK interventions are proceeding step by step and have not yet imposed a take-rate cap or fine, so near-term cash impact is limited.

sources.title: EUR-Lex: Commission Decision C/2025/3348 (DMA case DMA.100109, Apple Article 5(4))
sources.claims: The Commission's non-compliance decision orders Apple under Article 29(5) DMA to bring the anti-steering non-compliance to an end within 60 calendar days of notification; the decision records the legal basis for fines and periodic penalty payments under Articles 30 and 31.
sources.claims_weakened: Confirms the immediate remedy is behavioral (steering/link-out), not a break-up or take-rate cap.

sources.title: European Commission press release IP/25/1085: Commission finds Apple and Meta in breach of the Digital Markets Act
sources.claims: European Commission fined Apple EUR 500 million on 2025-04-23 for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation (Article 5(4)); investigation opened 2024-03-25; separate Article 6(4) investigation opened 2024-06-24 into Apple's new contractual terms for third-party app developers and marketplaces.
sources.claims_weakened: Fine is small relative to Apple's FY2025 net sales of USD 416.2 billion; does not by itself establish material cash-flow damage.

sources.title: Ashurst Perkins Coie: EU General Court rejects Apple challenges to European Commission DMA designation decisions
sources.claims: On 2026-07-08 the EU General Court delivered judgment in three joint cases rejecting Apple's challenges to (1) its DMA gatekeeper designation for App Store, iOS and Safari and (2) the Commission's market investigation into the statutory presumption; this narrows Apple's appeal routes against DMA obligations.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple cannot expect judicial relief from DMA gatekeeper status in the near term; compliance costs are durable.

sources.title: Korea Times: Korea fines Google, Apple combined $47.6 mil. over in-app payment practices
sources.claims: Korea Media and Communications Commission on 2026-10-28 fined Apple KRW 20.81 billion (about USD 15.5 million) and Google KRW 42.9 billion over in-app payment practices; found a 26% commission on third-party billing plus conditions effectively forced developers onto in-house payments; ordered external payment links and revised commission structures within three months. First enforcement under the 2021 Telecommunications Business Act amendment.
sources.claims_weakened: Korean fine is immaterial to Apple's cash flow; the significance is the precedent that a 26% fee on third-party billing is treated as evasion.

sources.title: Autorité de la concurrence: Targeted advertising - fine of EUR 150,000,000 on Apple for ATT framework
sources.claims: France's Autorité de la concurrence fined Apple EUR 150 million for abusing a dominant position in iOS/iPadOS app distribution between April 2021 and July 2023 through the implementation of App Tracking Transparency; found ATT as implemented was neither necessary nor proportionate and penalised smaller publishers.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows Apple's privacy differentiator can itself create antitrust liability, but the fine is small (about 0.04% of FY2025 net sales).

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple and DOJ Hold Early Settlement Talks in iPhone Antitrust Case
sources.claims: Apple and DOJ held early settlement talks in the iPhone antitrust case in July 2026; Apple's motion to dismiss was denied; no trial scheduled and evidence-gathering scheduled to end late May 2027. Separately, a federal judge ordered Apple to pay an additional USD 184 million in interest on a USD 634 million Masimo patent judgment, taking the total to around USD 818 million (2026-10-06).
sources.claims_weakened: DOJ case may settle without structural remedies; timing slips into 2027 and beyond reduce near-term cash impact.

sources.title: Wolters Kluwer Competition Blog: Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act grows its guidelines
sources.claims: In March 2025 the JFTC designated Apple Inc., its Japanese subsidiary iTunes K.K. and Google as specified software operators under the Mobile Software Competition Act; the Act took full effect on 2025-12-18.
sources.claims_weakened: Designation is an ex-ante conduct regime, not a finding of violation; no Japanese fine against Apple has been imposed.

sources.title: Japan Fair Trade Commission: Approaches in the digital market (Mobile Software Competition Act)
sources.claims: Japan's Act on Promotion of Competition for Specified Smartphone Software (Mobile Software Competition Act, Act No. 58 of 2024) was passed on 2024-06-12 and promulgated 2024-06-19; the JFTC treats Apple as a specified software operator for its OS, app store and browser.
sources.claims_weakened: Japanese regime is narrower than the EU DMA (mobile OS, app stores, browsers, search) and emphasises dialogue-based enforcement, limiting near-term fine risk.

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple Faces New App Store Complaint From Chinese Developers
sources.claims: On 2026-06-23 a group of 48 China-based iOS developers filed an antitrust complaint with China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) alleging Apple abuses market dominance through App Store commission rates and restrictions on alternative distribution; the complaint asks SAMR to investigate and cites Apple's commitment to offer China its lowest App Store commission rate.
sources.claims_weakened: A complaint is not a formal investigation or finding; no SAMR action against Apple has been announced.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: Apple announces changes to iOS in Japan
sources.claims: Apple announced changes to iOS apps in Japan in December 2025 to comply with the Mobile Software Competition Act, covering alternative app marketplaces and payment processing for the Japanese storefront.
sources.claims_weakened: Compliance changes are company-designed and do not establish the effective commission level after alternatives are introduced.

sources.title: News18: PLI Scheme Success - India's iPhone exports cross Rs 2 lakh crore in 2025-26
sources.claims: India's iPhone exports reached a record INR 2 lakh crore (about USD 23 billion) in FY2026, the final year of the large-scale electronics PLI scheme, making Apple the country's single largest branded exporter.
sources.claims_weakened: Exports are gross values and do not show the fiscal incentive received or the share of global iPhone output; the PLI scheme's final-year structure limits future subsidy.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: Apple accelerates environmental progress with highest-ever recycled material (2026 Environmental Progress Report)
sources.claims: Apple's 2026 Environmental Progress Report (April 2026) states Apple's 2025 greenhouse-gas emissions were down more than 60% versus 2015 and held roughly constant versus 2024 despite revenue growth; Apple 2030 targets a 75% reduction versus 2015 before balancing remaining emissions with nature-based solutions.
sources.claims_weakened: The 2030 goal still requires roughly a further 15 percentage points of reduction plus carbon removals; the residual gap and use of offsets are the weakest part of the climate claim.

sources.title: The Planet Brief: Apple Environmental Progress Report 2026 - the 2030 emissions gap
sources.claims: Independent review of Apple's 2026 Environmental Progress Report concludes a gap remains between the over-60% emissions cut achieved and the 75% reduction required by Apple 2030, with residual emissions dependent on carbon removals; analysis checked 2026-08-08 against Apple's report and assurance statements.
sources.claims_weakened: Questions whether Apple's carbon-neutral claim is deliverable on offsets alone; supports treating the claim as unverified until removals are contracted and assured.

sources.title: Logistics Insider: Apple iPhone exports from India cross $50 billion under PLI scheme
sources.claims: Apple's cumulative iPhone exports from India crossed USD 50 billion under the smartphone production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme by December 2025, less than four years after Apple joined in FY2022, according to official data; three months of the five-year eligibility window remained.
sources.claims_weakened: PLI is a temporary incentive that expires; the figure measures exports, not value added or margin retained in India.

sources.title: The Verge: Google and Apple's $20 billion search deal survives US antitrust remedies ruling
sources.claims: The US District Court remedies ruling in United States v. Google allowed Google to keep paying partners such as Apple to be the default search engine, including the agreement reported at about $20 billion, but prohibited exclusive search distribution deals and allowed yearly renegotiation; structural relief (Chrome, Android divestiture) was rejected
sources.claims_weakened: The brief's formulation that the Google payment "survives": it survives only as a non-exclusive, annually renegotiable contract with a counterparty whose exclusivity premium has been removed, so the revenue is intact in the near term but its price is now reset every year — and the size (~$20bn) is a press estimate, not an Apple disclosure

sources.title: TrendForce: Mobile DRAM Contract Prices Continue Rising in 2Q26, Pressuring Smartphone Production
sources.claims: Mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% QoQ for LPDDR5X and 70-75% for LPDDR4X in 2Q26; several consecutive quarters of steep increases intensify handset cost burdens; brands are cutting 2026 production and may not meet contracted bit volumes; high-end configuration settles at 12GB with 16GB declining; average smartphone DRAM content still rises to 8.5GB in 2026 (+10%)
sources.claims_weakened: That Apple can hold a 48% gross margin through FY2027 on price alone: the component inside its phones rose 78-83% in a single quarter, and memory content per device still grows, so the cost line compounds rather than annualises; also weakens the thesis-table claim that the 2026 cycle was purely a cost shock that normalises, since TrendForce expects pressure "over the coming quarters"

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Google defends its Safari deal with Apple in antitrust ruling appeal
sources.claims: Google formally defended its Safari default agreement with Apple in its appeal of the remedies ruling, filed by 2026-05-22; Google argues the court wrongly treated the Safari agreement as exclusive when it merely set a default; both sides are appealing the remedy to the DC Circuit, so the annual-renewal terms remain under review
sources.claims_weakened: Any assumption that the search-payment remedy is settled law by 2026-10: the terms are live on appeal, and a DOJ win could tighten them further while a Google win could restore some value to the default position

sources.title: TechCrunch: Apple touts $1.4 trillion in App Store billings and sales, 90% without a commission
sources.claims: Apple's App Store generated $1.4 trillion of developer billings and sales in 2025, of which about $149 billion was digital goods and services on which Apple charges a 15-30% commission; the remaining 90% of ecosystem activity is commission-free
sources.claims_weakened: Any estimate that treats total App Store commerce as Apple revenue: the commission-bearing pool is roughly $149bn, so a 500bp cut in the effective take rate removes about $7.5bn of near-100%-margin revenue, about 5% of FY2025 operating income — material, but not existential on its own

sources.title: MacRumors: iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders off to a muted start, analyst says
sources.claims: Initial iPhone 18 Pro pre-order wait times were described as "lukewarm" by GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu, who trimmed his production estimates after launch on 2026-09-09; entry price reported at $1,199 for the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro and up to $2,499 for the 2TB Pro Max, with price cited as the main cause of the slower start
sources.claims_weakened: The bull case's AI-driven replacement cycle and the base case's 10.6% September-quarter revenue growth: if the price increases needed to pass through memory costs are already damping pre-order demand, then the FY2027 ASP-led revenue path and the 48% gross margin cannot both hold

sources.title: S&P 500 Forward P/E Ratio Today: 18.59x (2026-10-29)
sources.claims: The S&P 500 traded at a blended forward 12-month P/E of 18.59x on 2026-10-29, an earnings yield of 5.38%, the 26th percentile of the trailing five years.
sources.claims_weakened: Any reading of Apple's 36.5x FY2027E multiple as a market-level rather than company-specific premium: Apple trades at roughly twice the index's forward multiple.

sources.title: Microsoft During the Lost Decade
sources.claims: Microsoft free cash flow per share rose from $1.15 in 1999 to $3.45 in 2012 (+200%) while the share price fell 54% from $58.38 at end-1999 to $26.71 at end-2012; $100 invested at end-1999 was worth $51 at end-2012 with dividends reinvested. The cause was multiple compression from almost 51x free cash flow in 1999 to 8x in 2012.
sources.claims_weakened: The claim that fundamental growth protects a holder from an elevated entry multiple: Microsoft tripled free cash flow per share and still lost half the invested capital over thirteen years.

sources.title: Cisco's stock closes at record for first time since dot-com peak in 2000
sources.claims: Cisco set a split-adjusted record of $80.06 on 2000-03-27, the day it passed Microsoft as the most valuable listed company; it did not exceed that level until 2025-12-10, when it closed $80.25, a 25-year round trip. Revenue growth was 66% in 2000 against 7.5% in its most recent quarter, and its market capitalisation was $317bn on 2025-12-10 against $4.5trn for NVIDIA.
sources.claims_weakened: The belief that a hardware leader at a peak multiple is protected by continued revenue growth: Cisco's business kept growing while the share price took 25 years to regain its 2000 peak.

sources.title: Apple Inc. (AAPL) P/E Ratio Long-Term Trends
sources.claims: Apple's P/E ratio fell from 45.25 in 2005 to a low near 12.46 in 2014, showing that earnings growth outpaced the share price for years and that Apple's own history contains a severe multiple compression.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that Apple has always commanded a premium multiple and that 40x is its normal state: its own history includes a low-teens multiple on rising earnings.

sources.title: Beebom: Apple A20 Pro vs Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 — benchmarks and specs
sources.claims: Geekbench 6 on the outlet's own devices: A20 Pro (iPhone 18 Pro Max) 4,707 single-core / 12,598 multi-core vs Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 (iQOO 15) 3,588 / 10,207, i.e. +31% single and +23% multi. 3DMark Wild Life Extreme 20-loop stress test: A20 Pro 8,793 best loop, 7,032 lowest, 80% stability; Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 6,867 best, 1,715 lowest, 25% stability. Specs: TSMC N2 2nm, 6-core CPU at up to 4.93GHz, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engine (44 TOPS FP16), Apple C2 5G modem. Qualcomm's vendor-claimed Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 scores 4,257 / 12,710, within 11% single-core and level on multi-core.
sources.claims_weakened: Undercuts the claim of a structural Apple silicon lead: on the same Geekbench 6 build the single-core advantage is 31%, not the 4.5% implied by the older A19 Pro comparison, and the next Qualcomm generation closes it to about 11% on vendor numbers. Device-level comparison confounds silicon with chassis and cooling.

sources.title: Tom's Guide: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max benchmarks — fastest phones we've tested
sources.claims: Second independent outlet's own testing: Geekbench 6 iPhone 18 Pro 4,735 single-core / 12,800 multi-core and iPhone 18 Pro Max 4,741 / 12,789; Geekbench 7 4,022 / 11,543 on the Pro. Sustained graphics stability rose from 65.2% (iPhone 17 Pro) to 79.4% (iPhone 18 Pro Max). Geekbench AI 1.7: iPhone 18 Pro 69,245 vs Galaxy S26 Ultra 83,047, so Apple remains behind on AI throughput despite a second neural engine. 3DMark Solar Bay Unlimited 16,288 (Pro) and 17,850 (Pro Max) vs 12,984 on the S26 Ultra.
sources.claims_weakened: Confirms the A20 Pro CPU lead but contradicts a claim of AI leadership: on Geekbench AI the Qualcomm-powered Galaxy S26 Ultra scores about 20% higher. Shows benchmark scores move materially between Geekbench 6 and Geekbench 7 builds, so single-run comparisons are fragile.

sources.title: Google Patents: US12164344B2 Hinges for folding display devices (Apple Inc.)
sources.claims: US 12,164,344 B2 was granted on 2024-12-10 to Apple Inc. (original and current assignee), application US17/859,668 filed 2022-07-07, priority 2021-08-11, inventors Scott J Krahn, Adam T Garelli, Bradley J Hamel, Dinesh C Mathew, Hoon Sik Kim and others; status active, anticipated expiration 2042-07-07. Family includes EP4134784A1, KR20230024218A and CN115904004A. Claims cover a hinge of interdigitated fingers in a friction clutch with crescent-shaped slots.
sources.claims_weakened: Fixes the grant date and assignee left undisclosed in the application-publication source; also shows the foldable hinge IP is a 2021 invention with a 2042 expiry rather than a 2025-2026 filing.

sources.title: Counterpoint Research: Europe Smartphone Shipments Drop 10% YoY in Q2 2026 to Hit Three-year Low
sources.claims: European smartphone shipments fell 10% YoY to 35 million units in Q2 2026, the lowest second quarter since 2023; Apple matched Samsung at 34% share of the region's shipments (Counterpoint Q2 2026 Market Monitor, cited from the search extract because the article returned HTTP 403).
sources.claims_weakened: No European revenue or ASP is given in the extract; the 34% Apple share is not cross-checked against a second tracker and sits well above Apple's global unit share, so it may reflect a value or premium-weighted cut.

sources.title: MacRumors: iPhone Loyalty Rate Climbs to 87% as Switching to Android Slows
sources.claims: CIRP puts iPhone loyalty at 87% in Q1 2026, up from 84% a year earlier, with Android switchers at 12% of new US iPhone buyers versus 14% a year earlier.
sources.claims_weakened: Survey-based and US-only; loyalty measures repeat purchase among buyers, not retention across the whole installed base.

sources.title: IDC: Smart Glasses Growth Cools to 35% as Meta Doubles Down on Distribution
sources.claims: Global XR headset and glasses shipments rose 35.3% YoY in Q2 2026 after 130.2% in Q1; audio glasses were 70.3% of units and display glasses 14.3%; Meta held 68.7% share; IDC forecasts unit growth of 26.3% in 2026, 40.5% in 2027 and 26.4% in 2028, with Samsung and XREAL Android XR products due later in 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: The article gives no absolute units or revenue; the category is small against smartphone volumes, and today's glasses pair with a phone rather than replace one, so near-term substitution is an attach risk, not a handset-loss risk.

sources.title: Counterpoint Research: Market Monitor — OEM Shipment by Region and Countries, Q2 2026
sources.claims: Japan's smartphone market declined 1% YoY in Q2 2026 after two years of growth; the Middle East and Africa market fell 10% YoY (paywalled regional report page, retrieved as a search extract, HTTP 403).
sources.claims_weakened: No absolute unit or value figure for Japan, Asia-Pacific or any other region; the page is a paywalled report listing, so the figures cannot be checked.

sources.title: TechCrunch: OpenAI's first hardware device is reportedly a screenless speaker that can move
sources.claims: On 2026-07-14 Bloomberg-sourced reporting described OpenAI's first hardware product as a screen-free, movable AI companion speaker built with former Apple engineers and still in development; Apple sued OpenAI over trade secrets in July 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: No confirmed launch date, price or specification; nothing has shipped, so it takes no measurable revenue from Apple's pool yet, and the report rests on unnamed sources.

sources.title: CommandLinux: Android OEM market share statistics 2026, citing Omdia US smartphone shipments for Q1 2026
sources.claims: Omdia recorded US smartphone shipments of 33.4 million units in Q1 2026, down 3% YoY, with Motorola the only vendor in the ranking to grow (Moto G more than 70% of Motorola's quarterly shipments).
sources.claims_weakened: A secondary statistics compilation quoting Omdia; the primary tracker is paywalled and the period is Q1 2026, not the latest quarter.

sources.title: CIRP: How is the Android to iOS Pipeline?
sources.claims: 12% of new US iPhone buyers in the March 2026 quarter reported moving from an Android smartphone; the switching rate has held at 11-15% of new iPhone buyers in recent years (Consumer Intelligence Research Partners quarterly survey).

scope.decision: Whether Apple (AAPL) belongs on Meridian Capital's long-only watchlist: a Buy/Add/Hold/Reduce/Sell/Avoid rating with position sizing and the conditions that would move it on or off the watchlist.

spines.must_answer: Is the market mispricing Apple's future cash flow or risk — earnings quality, competitive position, valuation, catalysts and downside risk?
Is demand for Apple's hardware and services durable or promotion-driven — repeat purchase, installed-base behavior, channel economics and brand defensibility?
Does policy create a moat or catalyst for Apple, or a hidden constraint on growth, valuation and exit — US-China, App Store regulation, tariffs and export controls?

research_plan.industry_map: Consumer electronics and platform-services value chain: upstream semiconductors and components (TSMC leading-edge SoCs; memory, displays, cameras, RF from Korea, Japan and the US) → assembly and test (Foxconn, Luxshare and Tata in India; concentrated in China with an India ramp to 28% of iPhone assembly in 2026) → distribution (carriers, retailers, direct online; 40% direct and 60% indirect) → installed base of more than 2.5bn active devices → monetization through hardware plus services (App Store, iCloud, advertising, Apple Pay, subscriptions, licensing) → replacement and upgrade cycle. Decisive bottleneck: control of the silicon/OS/developer ecosystem at the premium end, which sustains pricing and the installed-base annuity; binding constraints are advanced-node supply, memory cost, China/India manufacturing geopolitics and platform-regulation limits on services take rates. Apple's place: the integrator with pricing power at the premium end and 65% of the $600-plus handset tier, monetizing the installed base through services at a 76% gross margin.
research_plan.geo_lens: Material. Home and revenue market: United States (largest revenue region); Greater China is the second-largest and most policy-exposed region at 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue ($64,839M); Europe, Japan and rest of Asia-Pacific secondary. Supply chain: assembly concentrated in China and India (India reached 23% of iPhone assembly in 2025, projected 28% in 2026, while China fell from 83% to 74%), leading-edge silicon from TSMC in Taiwan, memory and components from Korea, Japan and the US. Capital market and listing: Nasdaq; comparables are US mega-cap platforms and global handset makers. Report written from a US long-only investor's perspective.
research_plan.policy_lens: Material. Jurisdictions mapped: United States (DOJ antitrust case filed 2024-03-21, App Store remedy risk, the Epic contempt finding of 2025-04-30 and Supreme Court review agreed 2026-06-30, IEEPA tariffs struck down 2026-02-20, Section 232 semiconductor review with no Apple tariffs on 2026-01-14, Section 301 measures live), European Union (DMA Article 6(4) case with a 10% of worldwide sales cap, the €500m fine of 2025-04-23, the new fee card live 2026-10-01, General Court upholding gatekeeper status 2026-07-08), China (SAMR, 48 developers' complaint of 2026-06-23, data-security rules), India (production-linked incentives; ₹2 lakh crore of iPhone exports in FY2026), plus UK CMA strategic market status of 2025-10-22, Korea's KRW 20.81bn fine of 2026-10-28 and Japan's MSCA effective 2025-12-18. Policy affects App Store take rate, services margin, supply-chain geography and China demand; the report prices a regulatory haircut to services rather than a binary outcome.

US Department of Justice antitrust filings and PACER court dockets
European Commission competition/DMA decisions and non-compliance proceedings
UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) mobile ecosystems investigation
China SAMR and Ministry of Industry and Information Technology records
USPTO and EPO patent databases
US FTC and state attorneys general actions

gates: Confirm company identity, legal entity, geography, stage, and business model.
Decide whether the geographic market context lens is material; if yes, map home, revenue, expansion, supplier, comparable-company, capital, exit markets and the investor perspective.
Decide whether the policy and geopolitics lens is material; if yes, map jurisdictions and perspective.
Complete the profile requirements before drafting.
Build the source register with source type, date, confidence, claims and a link or file/page reference.
Use visible source IDs such as [S1] as citations in the report.
Complete the evidence matrix for all material sections before drafting.
Run the pre-draft evidence gate and fix failures.
Draft the report from evidence, not from outline memory.
Run the red-team pass and rewrite weak sections.
research_plan.hypothesis: Apple is a high-quality cash compounder whose installed base and services mix support durable free cash flow, but at $348.91 (40.0x trailing earnings, 32.5x EV/EBIT, 36.5x FY2027E against an 18.1x four-peer median) the price offers no margin of safety. The 2026 acceleration came from hardware mix, memory-driven competitor retreat and 2 points of one-off tariff refunds; the probability-weighted outcome is $300 (-14.0%) on a 20/40/40 distribution. View: Watchlist, zero position, conditional starter at $273-$309 on $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS, subject to a December-2026 quarter with gross margin at 48% or better excluding refunds and double-digit Services growth.
research_plan.author: Lead Analyst

items: Use web and data tools for fresh facts whenever a company, market, price, policy, filing, funding, or executive fact may have changed.
For each major section, record targeted search strings, opened sources, source IDs, and why the selected sources are decision-grade rather than merely convenient.
Use the server's checks for deterministic QA, extraction, citation checks and the delivery folder; do not rely on a one-shot narrative draft.
Do not generate repeated filler paragraphs such as per-section original-document priority, citation-anchor blocks, or repeated metric-card copy; each section must contain content-specific analysis.
Before drafting, write a section distinctness plan: the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, and best visual artifact for each section.
For each section, draft one final-report thesis sentence that directly analyzes the company; never copy internal plan labels or rubric language into the report.
Remove repeated visible scaffolds such as "Economic mechanism", "Comparison and benchmark", "Counter-evidence and risk" and "Investor implication"; keep the scaffold internal.
Use a verdict strip, compact decision cards, selected tables, and at most a few KPI strips; do not repeat the same card, grid or dashboard pattern in every section.
Before writing the executive briefing, summarize the non-consensus or consensus view and the exact evidence that changes the decision.
Treat OCR as a pipeline: inventory files, OCR scan- or slide-heavy material, and keep page, slide or table references for every extracted claim.
Check every page holding numbers, TAM, valuation, customers, clinical or regulatory claims, policy claims, financing terms or team credentials before relying on it.
Mark OCR-derived claims low confidence until checked or corroborated; use ranges for OCR-derived financial inputs.
Build a claim verification table for material company-provided claims: verified, partially verified, unverified, contradicted, or not publicly disclosed.

(AAPL, Nasdaq, listed) for a long-only watchlist decision in English; three spines chosen and the value chain, decisive bottleneck, geographic and policy lenses mapped; no client documents attached. Fourteen research sections are saved by the six analysts with evidence blocks and gates passed, 151+ sources are registered including SEC filings (S5, S6, S47), market data (S7, S8, S9, S10, S93) and regulator records (S134, S135, S136, S138).
