rows.belief: The pain Apple monetises is upgrade-cycle fatigue plus an assistant capability gap, not unmet demand: it extracts $194 of revenue and $65 of operating profit per active device per year from a base of more than 2.5 billion devices, so the customer need is replacement and services attach rather than new-category creation.
rows.evidence: 9M FY2026 revenue $364,357M, +16.1%, with iPhone +22.4% to $196,515M and Services +14.1% to $91,728M; more than 2.5bn active devices in the December 2025 quarter, up 150M year on year; services revenue of $48.9 per device a year against $43.7 in FY2025 [S5, S6, S58].
rows.counter_evidence: IDC has global shipments falling 16.7% in 2026 while ASP rises 27.6% to $581, so demand is being carried by price rather than units; the installed base grew 6.4% against 16.1% revenue growth, meaning most of the growth is monetisation and price, which has a ceiling [S79, S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A December-2026 quarter with revenue down year on year, or disclosure of iPhone unit volumes, would settle whether the 2026 cycle was pull-forward.

rows.belief: The moat is hardware and regulatory, not intelligence: silicon-OS co-design, an in-house modem and four FDA clearances are durable, while the assistant layer is rented — Apple Foundation Models run on Google Gemini under a multi-year agreement announced 2026-01-12.
rows.evidence: A19 Pro Geekbench 6 single-core 4,019 against 3,846 for Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, a 4.5% lead; granted hinge patent US 12,164,344 and application US2025/0120026A1 for the iPhone Duo; FDA clearances on 2024-09-12, 2024-09-13, 2025-09-11 and 2026-04-01 [S117, S121, S68, S115].
rows.counter_evidence: No assistant or foundation-model patent with an Apple assignee surfaced publicly, and the competitor that supplies the model also sells phones; the 4.5% silicon lead is within one generation of being matched, and no product-level margin is disclosed to prove the premium is earned by the silicon [S115, S117].
rows.confidence: high on the facts, medium on durability
rows.change: Evidence that Apple is training or deploying its own frontier model, or a measurable assistant capability gap in third-party testing, would move this either way.

rows.belief: 2026 is a cost-shock cycle, not a demand cycle: memory prices up nearly 300% erased the sub-$100 tier, premium mix rose to 29% of units and Apple took 65% of the $600+ tier, so the current growth rate is borrowed from rivals' price increases and will normalise.
rows.evidence: Premium tier 29% of unit sales in H1 2026 from 25%; Apple 65% of premium units and Apple plus Samsung 84%; Apple units +14.9% and Samsung +8.1% in a quarter the market fell 7.4% while Xiaomi fell 26.4% [S77, S79, S78].
rows.counter_evidence: IDC expects China's second-half decline to widen to 20% year on year, government subsidies faded in Q2 2026, and the Greater China rebound of 30% to $64,839M was partly renminbi strength rather than volume [S80, S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: Memory pricing normalising in 2027, or Android vendors holding prices, would remove the mechanism behind the share gain.

rows.belief: The installed-base annuity scales without new distribution: 40% direct and 60% indirect channels, services attach rising per device, and India assembly at 23% of iPhone output in 2025 heading to 28% in 2026 reduces tariff exposure without changing the route to market.
rows.evidence: Services $109,158M in FY2025 at a 75.4% gross margin and $91,728M in nine months of FY2026 at 75.6% in the June quarter; India assembly 23% in 2025 from 14% in 2024, projected 28% in 2026 while China fell from 83% to 74% [S5, S6, S119].
rows.counter_evidence: Services growth is a function of the take rate the courts now set, not of distribution reach; Apple discloses no India revenue (it sits inside Europe) and no services sub-segment split, so the scalability of the highest-margin line cannot be verified [S6, S56].
rows.confidence: high on the mechanism, medium on magnitude
rows.change: A services growth print below 8%, or disclosure that a majority of services growth is advertising rather than App Store, would change the scaling story.

rows.belief: Per-device economics are extraordinary and currently flattered: $95 of gross profit and $65 of operating profit per active device a year with a 32:1 lifetime-to-acquisition ratio, but roughly 2 points of the June-quarter 50.1% gross margin were one-off tariff refunds.
rows.evidence: Group gross margin 49.1% in 9M FY2026 against 46.9% in FY2025; operating margin 33.6%; $5.0bn of operating income per 100bp of gross margin, 3.1% of base-case net income; capex 2.2% of revenue [S5, S6, S47].
rows.counter_evidence: The 10-Q warns memory and storage costs will intensify and that price increases may not offset them; inventories rose 94% to $11,092M and $13,270M of gross intangibles were added with no acquisition in investing cash flow, so an amortisation charge is coming [S6, S47].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A December-quarter gross margin below 47% ex-refund would show the margin peak has passed.

rows.belief: Execution is strong and continuity is intact, but the top team is newly installed and its capital allocation has become the weak link: $82,226M of trailing buybacks at 40.0x earnings retire stock at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury.
rows.evidence: John Ternus became CEO on 2026-09-01 with Tim Cook as executive chair, and the iPhone 18 cycle shipped on schedule on 2026-09-09; R&D rose 32.5% to $34,035M; $438.6bn of buybacks and $75.0bn of dividends were paid from operating cash flow from 2021 to 2026 [S54, S6, S47, S114].
rows.counter_evidence: CEO, COO, CFO and general counsel all changed within twenty months; no insider bought a share in twelve months against $208.0m sold; the board spans ages 51-77 with one new independent since 2021, and the company has disclosed no plan to replace the buyback at a lower multiple [S52, S54].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A new buyback authorisation in May 2027 sized or priced differently, or insider buying, would change this.

rows.belief: There is no margin of safety at $348.91: 40.0x trailing earnings and 32.5x EV/EBIT against a four-peer median of 18.1x, with a DCF range of $153-$230 and a reverse DCF requiring 15% free-cash-flow growth for ten years at a 9.5% WACC.
rows.evidence: Price $348.91 at the NasdaqGS close on 2026-10-29, market cap $5,092.1B, EV $5,029.9B, trailing EPS $8.72, FCF $136.7B; above every fiscal year-end multiple since FY2022 (24.6x, 27.9x, 37.5x, 34.2x) [S7, S6, S93].
rows.counter_evidence: At an 8.0% required return the reverse DCF needs only 5.3% perpetual growth, which Apple's 8.9% five-year FCF compound has already cleared; a 2.7% FCF yield and 37.3x price-to-FCF beat Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta [S6, S93].
rows.confidence: high on the multiple, medium on fair value
rows.change: A sustained move in the ten-year yield below 4% would mechanically lift the defensible multiple.

rows.belief: Exit is the secondary market only: no acquirer can absorb a $5.0trn enterprise value — the largest technology deal ever is 1.35% of it — so total return comes from EPS growth, a 1.6% share shrink and a 0.31% dividend, and the trim discipline has to be tied to the multiple.
rows.evidence: 38.67M shares and $13.22B traded daily, so a $250M position is 1.9% of one day's value; $82.2B of trailing repurchases equal 1.6% of shares; the five-year 134.2% return decomposes into 55.4% EPS growth, 50.7% multiple expansion and 3.3% dividends [S7, S5, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: With 8.1% consensus FY2027 EPS growth plus the buyback and dividend, an 8.4% annual return is achievable with no re-rating, which is an acceptable long-only outcome and argues against trimming [S93].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A change in the buyback's size or pace, or an index-weight change, would alter the exit arithmetic.

rows.belief: The price is above intrinsic value on a 9.5% required return: base case $325 (-6.9%) and probability-weighted $314 (-9.9%), against a two-stage DCF of $183 and a sensitivity range of $153-$230.
rows.evidence: Consensus 12-month target $332.39 from 43 analysts, 4.7% below the close; Sell plus Strong Sell ratings rose from one in May 2026 to six in October 2026; 36.5x FY2027E P/E on $9.56 [S93, S7].
rows.counter_evidence: DCF output is dominated by the WACC assumption and terminal value is 56% of enterprise value; at 8.5% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth the model returns $230, so the discount rate rather than the cash flows decides the verdict [S93, S10].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: Either a de-rating to 30-34x forward earnings or an upward revision cycle above 10% revenue growth would close the gap.

rows.belief: Reported earnings are clean in the sense that Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, but FY2026's margin is a peak to normalise: about 2 points of the June-quarter gross margin were tariff refunds and $13,270M of intangibles appeared without an acquisition line or a disaggregating note.
rows.evidence: Q3 FY2026 gross margin 50.1% including roughly 2pp of refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; gross intangibles $38,220M, up from $24,950M, with $5,075M already current; unrecognised tax benefits $23.2bn, of which $10.6bn would hit the tax rate [S6, S47].
rows.counter_evidence: Trailing free cash flow of $136,683M at 1.06x net income supports the earnings, and the FY2025 0.88x conversion was the $15.8bn Irish State Aid payment rather than deteriorating economics [S47, S5].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: The FY2026 10-K's intangible note and the December-quarter margin would settle whether the peak is accounting or operating.

rows.belief: Conversion is structurally high and better than peers: 1.06x net income on capex of 2.2% of revenue leaves Apple's trailing free cash flow at 1.71 times Microsoft and Alphabet combined.
rows.evidence: Trailing operating cash flow $146,724M, capex $10,041M, FCF $136,683M; capex $10,041M against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet; cash conversion cycle -56.8 days on 98.3 days of payables [S47, S11, S13].
rows.counter_evidence: Working capital was a $2.9bn drag in nine months with a $16,266M build in other assets, and the negative cash cycle cannot extend much further without supplier pushback [S47].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A capital programme for owned AI compute would break the 2%-of-sales capex assumption on which the free-cash-flow case rests.

rows.belief: The balance sheet is strong but irrelevant to the call: $62,173M of net cash is 1.2% of a $5.02trn market value, so it cushions nothing in a de-rating and funds the buyback rather than a defence.
rows.evidence: Cash and marketable securities $146,517M against debt of $84,344M at 2026-06-27; term-debt maturities $12,393M in 2026, $10,078M in 2027 and $9,300M in 2028, covered by securities maturities; net interest income positive at $670M in nine months [S6, S47].
rows.counter_evidence: Commitments are rising — other purchase obligations up $14.5bn to $29.3bn, lease liabilities $13.7bn, deferred revenue $14.9bn — and the tax reserve of $23.2bn is a contingent draw [S6, S47].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A debt-funded acquisition of AI capacity, or a step-up in purchase obligations, would make the balance sheet a live variable.

rows.belief: Consensus is above the price in estimates but below it in targets, which is the signature of a stock that has outrun its models: FY2026 revenue $477.64B (+14.8%) and EPS $8.84, FY2027 $526.79B (+10.3%) and $9.56, against a $332.39 average target.
rows.evidence: Nine-month actuals imply a September quarter of $113.3B and $1.96 of EPS, or +10.6% and +6.5%, against +16.4% and +29% in the June quarter; Apple publishes no quantitative guidance [S93].
rows.counter_evidence: Estimates were revised up through 2026 and the June quarter beat the deceleration implied here, so the sell side has been behind the business rather than ahead of it [S93, S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: The 2026-11-02 print is the first hard test of whether consensus FY2027 of $526.79B is reachable.

rows.belief: The dated calendar is crowded and negatively skewed at 40x: FY2026 results on 2026-11-02 chaired for the first time by Ternus, the December quarter as the first clean read on margin ex-refund, the May 2027 buyback authorisation, the EU Article 6(4) decision and the US appellate and DOJ tracks.
rows.evidence: FQ4 FY2026 results scheduled 2026-11-02; buyback authorisations in May 2024 ($110B) and May 2025 ($100B); Epic contempt review granted by the Supreme Court on 2026-06-30; DOJ settlement talks reported July 2026 with discovery to May 2027 [S85, S5, S6, S62].
rows.counter_evidence: No signpost for Article 6(4) has been published since the case opened on 2024-06-24 and the DOJ timetable has slipped repeatedly, so timing risk cuts both ways [S6].
rows.confidence: high on dates, low on outcomes
rows.change: An earlier-than-expected EU decision or a DOJ settlement would reset the regulatory timeline.

rows.belief: Zero position today and a watchlist rating: no entry until 30-34x FY2027E earnings, or $287-$325, or evidence that FY2027 revenue growth holds above 10% with gross margin above 48% excluding refunds.
rows.evidence: Base case $325 and bear case $224 from a 26x multiple on $8.60 of EPS, a -35.8% downside; probability-weighted $314, -9.9%; a $250M position would be 1.9% of one day's traded value, so entry and exit costs are not the constraint [S93, S7].
rows.counter_evidence: A long-only fund that trimmed at 37.5x in fiscal 2024 missed the following 50%, and 8-10% annual compounding with no re-rating is a legitimate return for a low-turnover mandate [S93].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A market-wide de-rating or a genuine second growth engine would move the entry band rather than the discipline.

scenarios.driver: AI-device upgrade cycle extends and the foldable iPhone Duo opens a new price tier; Services holds double-digit growth with advertising and cloud replacing lost commission; gross margin holds near 49% despite memory costs; the multiple stays at 40x on FY2027E EPS of $10.10.
scenarios.evidence: June-quarter revenue rose 16.4% with double-digit growth in iPhone, Mac and Services and in every geographic segment; Greater China rebounded 22.4% to $18.8B; R&D rose 32.2% to $11.7B; Apple took 65% of the $600+ premium tier and raised unit share 3.9 points to 20.2% [S6, S47, S77, S79].
scenarios.outcome: $404 a share, +15.8% from $348.91 before the 0.31% dividend; 40x FY2027E EPS of $10.10.
scenarios.implication: Own it: the watchlist rating converts to an add only once delivered unit growth and a clean margin print justify the multiple; at this probability the expected contribution is +3.2% to the weighted return.

scenarios.driver: Growth decelerates to the consensus FY2027 figure of 10.3% revenue and 8.1% EPS, gross margin normalises to 48% once the tariff refunds wash out, regulation trims rather than removes commission, and the multiple drifts back to the FY2025 year-end 34x.
scenarios.evidence: Nine-month actuals imply a September quarter of $113.3B and $1.96 of EPS, +10.6% and +6.5%, against +16.4% and +29% in June; consensus FY2027 revenue $526.79B and EPS $9.56; the June-quarter 50.1% gross margin included 2 points of tariff refunds, so the underlying figure was 48.1% [S93, S6].
scenarios.implication: Hold on the watchlist with no position: the business compounds at 8-10% a year, but at $348.91 the buyer is paying for the bull case and receiving the base case.

scenarios.driver: Memory costs compress hardware gross margin while the App Store take rate settles toward the mid-teens and the Google payments are curtailed, so FY2027 EPS falls to $8.60 and the multiple mean-reverts to the FY2023 26x; Samsung converts memory profits into handset price competition and Huawei caps China share.
scenarios.evidence: The 10-Q warns memory and storage costs may not be offset by price increases; the EU's Article 6(4) case carries a 10% of sales cap and the €500m fine on 2025-04-23 established the principle; the General Court upheld gatekeeper status on 2026-07-08; Korean and UK regulators are converging on mid-teens commissions; the shares traded at $243.42 within the past year, 30.2% below today's close [S6, S134, S135, S136, S132, S7].
scenarios.outcome: $224 a share, -35.8% from $348.91; 26x FY2027E EPS of $8.60, and $208 if bear EPS is $8.00.
scenarios.implication: Avoid adding at any price above the entry band; the bear case is a 26x multiple on a smaller EPS, and the trigger to re-underwrite is a margin print below 47% or a final EU remedy that removes commission retroactively.

assumptions.assumption: Gross margin holds at or above 48% excluding tariff refunds through FY2027, against memory and storage costs the company says will intensify
assumptions.disproof: A December-2026 quarter gross margin below 47% on a like-for-like basis, or iPhone price increases that do not stick
assumptions.impact: Each 100bp of gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, 3.1% of base-case net income and $0.30 of EPS; a return to the FY2025 46.9% margin removes about 11% of FY2027 EPS
assumptions.early_warning: DRAM and NAND contract pricing, Samsung's memory-division margin, the spread between Apple's ASP and BOM cost

assumptions.assumption: The App Store take rate settles in a 15-26% band rather than collapsing, and Google search-distribution payments inside Services survive in some form
assumptions.disproof: A final EU Article 6(4) remedy imposing structural separation, or a US order terminating the search-distribution payments
assumptions.impact: A 10% cut in Services gross profit is $8.2bn, 6.2% of operating income; halving the reported $20bn Google payment is $0.56 of EPS, 5.9% of consensus
assumptions.early_warning: Article 6(4) decision, the Supreme Court's ruling on the Epic contempt standard, the DOJ settlement terms, the 2027 Google renewal

assumptions.assumption: Services grows at double digits (12.3% CAGR to $120.5bn trailing) and iPhone premium mix and China share hold near 18%
assumptions.disproof: Services growth below 8% for two quarters, or Greater China unit share back below 15% as IDC expects the second-half China market to fall 20%
assumptions.impact: A 300bp shortfall in Services growth removes roughly $3.6bn of 76%-margin revenue, about 2.2% of operating income; a China reversal hits 17.8% of nine-month revenue
assumptions.early_warning: Quarterly Services growth, IDC China share for Q4 2026, advertising and cloud revenue lines replacing lost commission

assumptions.assumption: The exit multiple is 34x FY2027E EPS of $9.56, i.e. the FY2025 year-end level rather than the current 40.0x
assumptions.disproof: A ten-year Treasury yield falling materially below 4%, or a re-acceleration that lifts consensus FY2028 EPS above $11
assumptions.impact: Ten points of exit multiple move two-year total return by about 30 percentage points: -10.7% at 30x, +1.2% at 34x, +18.9% at 40x
assumptions.early_warning: Ten-year yield and the equity-risk premium, the 50-day versus 200-day average, sell-side target dispersion

assumptions.assumption: The buyback continues at roughly 1.6% of shares a year and the FY2026 fourth quarter lands near consensus of $113.3bn of revenue and $1.96 of EPS
assumptions.disproof: A materially smaller May 2027 authorisation than the $100bn of May 2025, or a September-quarter revenue miss
assumptions.impact: Halving the buyback removes about 0.8 points of annual EPS growth; a 5% revenue miss on FY2027 consensus removes about $2.30 of EPS at a 48% gross margin
assumptions.early_warning: The 2026-11-02 print, the May 2027 authorisation, buyback pace in the FY2026 10-K

consensus.consensus: The market treats Apple as the highest-quality cash compounder in mega-cap technology and pays for it: 40.0x trailing earnings, above every fiscal year-end multiple since FY2022, on the view that Services mix, the buyback and a record premium share justify a permanent premium to Microsoft at 27.7x and Alphabet at 14.8x.
consensus.our_view: The quality is consensus and broadly correct; the edge is narrower and is about price rather than business. The share price capitalises a second growth engine - AI devices, Services, new categories - that no filing evidences, while the 2026 acceleration came from hardware mix, memory-driven competitor retreat and 2 points of one-off tariff refunds. At $348.91 the probability-weighted outcome is $300, -14.0%, so the thesis is not that Apple is a bad business but that it is a good business with no margin of safety; on quality the thesis is consensus, and the differentiated view is the multiple.
consensus.evidence: The 43-analyst consensus target of $332.39 sits 4.7% below the close and Sell plus Strong Sell ratings rose from one to six between May and October 2026 while the shares gained 28.6%; the reverse DCF needs 15% free-cash-flow growth for a decade at a 9.5% WACC, 2.7 times the 5.5% revenue compound from FY2021 to FY2026E; and half of the five-year 134.2% return came from multiple expansion rather than earnings [S93, S7, S6].
consensus.proof_event: The FY2026 fourth-quarter print on 2026-11-02 and the December-2026 quarter that follows it: if revenue grows more than 10% with gross margin above 48% excluding refunds, the consensus view is right and the multiple is defensible; if margin or growth disappoints, the de-rating case is proved.

one_question.question: What share of Services revenue and gross profit comes from App Store commissions and from Google's search-distribution payments - the two cash flows that the EU, US courts and the DOJ are directly repricing?
one_question.why: This single undisclosed number decides whether platform regulation is a sentiment issue or an earnings event. Services is $109.2bn of FY2025 revenue at a 75.4% gross margin, $82.3bn of gross profit and 42.2% of the total; a tenth of that pool lost to remedies is $8.2bn, 6.2% of operating income, which would move the bear case from a multiple event to an earnings event. If the exposed share is below a tenth of Services gross profit, the 40x multiple is a rate-and-growth argument and can be defended; if a quarter or more, the base case EPS of $9.56 is overstated and the entry band falls below $287. Apple does not disclose App Store revenue, take rates or the Google payment, so the answer has to come from the PACER exhibits already requested and from the Article 6(4) decision, and no analyst estimate in the register resolves it.

modules.analogs: "No best-case analog is close enough to carry the bull case. Cautionary analog one: Microsoft 1999-2012, where free cash flow per share tripled from $1.15 to $3.45 while the share price fell 54% and $100 became $51 with dividends reinvested, because the P/FCF multiple fell from 51x to 8x [S154]. Cautionary analog two: Cisco, which set a split-adjusted record of $80.06 on 2000-03-27 and did not exceed it until 2025-12-10, a 25-year round trip, while revenue kept growing [S155]. Own history: Apple's P/E fell from 45.25x in 2005 to about 12.46x in 2014 while earnings grew [S156]. The decision rule: when the entry multiple is the main contributor to expected return, the growth rate has to be demonstrated before the multiple is paid."
modules.capital_efficiency: "Capex of $10,041M trailing, 2.2% of revenue, against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet, gives trailing free cash flow of $136,683M at 1.06x net income and a capital-light model that funds $82,226M of buybacks and $15,640M of dividends from operations rather than from the balance sheet. The efficiency is real and is the base case's foundation. The cost is that the capability inputs are bought rather than built: R&D up 32.5% to $34,035M and $13,270M of gross intangibles added with no acquisition line, against a Gemini licence that converts model development into an operating expense. If AI becomes the upgrade reason rather than a feature, the 2%-of-sales capex line is the assumption that breaks first."
modules.position_sizing: "Listed, long-only: watchlist only, zero position at $348.91. The Kelly fraction at these inputs is negative (-1.62) because the probability-weighted return is -14.0% with a 0.44 upside-to-downside ratio, so the optimal bet is zero. A conditional starter is capped at 3-5% of the portfolio once the price is $273-$309 on $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS, a December-2026 gross margin prints at 48% or better excluding refunds, and Services growth is in double digits. The maximum loss to the bear case is -35.8% to $224, and the market regime (S&P 500 +12.8% YTD, VIX 17.20, ten-year 4.99%, technology rotating out) argues for patience rather than exposure."

answers.most_damaging_fact: The size and durability of Google's search-distribution payment. It is reported at $20bn a year (S147), equivalent to 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue and 12.9% of trailing operating income (S6), it is not disclosed by Apple, and the remedy that preserved it put the contract on annual, non-exclusive terms that both parties are appealing (S149). If the true figure is $12-14bn and the 2027 renewal clears lower, the base case's 48% gross margin and $9.56 EPS are overstated by 4-6%, the bear becomes the base, and the entry band falls below $273 — the lower bound the recommendation names. If instead the payment is intact and rising, the bear's principal earnings driver disappears and the 40% bear weight is too high. The second most damaging fact is the 4.99% ten-year yield (S10): on $111.0B of owner cash the model reaches $349 only at a 6.4% required return and $221 at 8.0%, so the verdict softens only if a long-only fund accepts a 1.3% premium over Treasuries.
answers.company_only_claims: Four positive claims rest on company material. The AI capability narrative — "all-new Siri AI" and the iPhone 18 Pro feature set — comes from Apple's newsroom (S116) and is not independently tested; the Gemini arrangement is corroborated by Reuters (S115) but its scope, fee and term are Apple's description. The $1.4trn App Store ecosystem is Apple's own framing (S95), and only $149bn of it is commission-bearing digital goods (S150). The 10 million foldable units planned for 2026 is a supplier plan reported by CNBC/Nikkei (S113), not an Apple disclosure, and the technology section presents it as the form-factor test. The attribution of the 30% Greater China rebound to renminbi strength and mix is management's explanation; the revenue is filed (S6) but the cause is unverified. By contrast, revenue, margins, buybacks, cash and the Microsoft and Alphabet capex comparisons are filing-verified (S5, S6, S47, S11, S13).
answers.generic_section: technology_product is the most generic. Its barrier table assigns difficulty scores of 8, 9, 7, 7 and 3, a composite of 7 and "3-4 years to replicate" with no method and no source, which is exactly the kind of unsourced scoring the rest of the report avoids. The silicon moat rests on one Geekbench 6 single-core run from a low-confidence blog (S117) showing a 4.5% lead, a gap inside normal run-to-run variance, and the section itself concedes that the benchmark cannot show sustained thermal performance. Its central judgement — that the moat is hardware and regulatory rather than intelligence — is probably right but needs a second independent benchmark, the Gemini fee and term, and the A20 Pro process node before a committee can lean on it. The exit section is second weakest: it is market data plus arithmetic, with no judgement about the buyer base.
answers.unpriced_risk: The services repricing is named in the thesis table but not carried into the recommendation's price. The bear case's 10% EPS haircut ($9.56 to $8.60) is fully consumed by the two services items — $0.56 from halving the Google payment and $0.42 from a 1,000bp cut on half the $149bn App Store pool — leaving nothing for a 300bp gross-margin miss worth $0.90, a 30% China decline worth $0.45, or the $0.16 FY2027 amortisation charge (S147, S150, S6). The entry band is $273-$300 on $9.10 of risk-adjusted EPS, capped at the $300 probability-weighted value, so no position should be contemplated above $300. The second unpriced item is the $14.5bn rise in other purchase obligations to $29.3bn, a contracted cash cost that the 8% free-cash-flow growth path ignores.
answers.first_challenge: A skeptical partner challenges the valuation's construction before its conclusion: the two-stage DCF deducts $13.7bn of stock compensation and $17.7bn of contracted intangible purchases as real cash costs, leaving $111.0B of owner cash against $142.36B of reported free cash, caps growth at 8% for five years then 4%, and lands on $158 — 55% below the price — so the number looks like an artefact of the growth path rather than a valuation. The same partner asks why the base case exits at 34x when it simultaneously assumes EPS growth decelerating to 8.1%, and why 40.0x is treated as a peak when the FY2024 and FY2025 year-ends were 37.5x and 34.2x (S7, S93). The answer has to be the reverse DCF — about 17% free-cash-flow growth a year for a decade at a 9.5% required return, or about 7.1% in perpetuity — not the $158 point estimate, and the section should say so before it is asked.
answers.downside_survival: The conclusion survives every listed-company stress; the entry band does not. Multiple compression from 40.0x to 26x on base EPS gives $249 (-28.7%), and on bear EPS of $8.00 gives $208 (-40%). Free cash flow 30% lower takes the DCF to $111 a share, which no committee should accept for a 76%-margin franchise, so the honest statement of that stress is EPS minus 17% at 26x, or $206. Refinancing does not bind: $62,173M of net cash, $12,393M of 2026 term maturities covered by maturing securities and positive net interest income (S6, S47). An inventory write-down of 20% on $11,092M costs $2.2bn pre-tax, $0.12 of EPS. Even a 50%-smaller premium tier, which would halve iPhone revenue, leaves Apple with net cash and a services annuity, so the bear case is a multiple event rather than a solvency event — which is why zero position at $348.91 is defensible and a short is not.
answers.ocr_claims: There are none: the register holds no OCR-derived sources, and every figure in the draft traces to a filing (S5, S6, S47), market data (S7, S10, S93) or an independent page retrieved in this run (S147, S148, S150, S151). The FDA clearances cited in the technology section are regulator records (S68, S71, S72, S67), not scanned documents. The only transcription risk worth flagging is that the $20bn Google payment is a press figure repeated across outlets rather than a disclosed number, which is why it is labelled unverified in the risk section rather than treated as a filing fact.

rows.finding: In the nine months to 2026-06-27 iPhone was 53.9% of net sales ($196,515M, +22.4% y/y) and Services 25.2% ($91,728M, +14.1%); the FY2025 mix was iPhone 50.4%, Services 26.2%, Mac 8.1%, iPad 6.7%, Wearables 8.6% ($416,161M total).
rows.mechanism: Hardware sell-in into an iPhone 17 upgrade cycle, plus a favourable FX swing in Europe and Greater China, outgrew the subscription-like services layer; mix therefore rotated back toward the more cyclical, lower-margin leg.
rows.benchmark: FY2023 mix of iPhone 52.3% and Services 22.2%; FY2023-FY2025 total revenue CAGR of 4.2% versus 9M FY2026 growth of 16.1%.
rows.weakens: The narrative that Apple is steadily becoming a services company: services' revenue share fell 1.0 point year on year and services' share of gross profit fell from 41.3% to 39.1%.
rows.implication: The durability of earnings depends on the hardware cycle more than the mix story implies, so the watchlist case must price a hardware downturn, not only a regulatory one.
rows.confidence: high - two primary filings (10-K FY2025, 8-K/10-Q FY2026) give the category table directly.
rows.follow_up: What were iPhone units and ASP in FY2026? Apple discloses net sales only, so unit volume must come from third-party shipment data.

rows.finding: Services earned a 76.3% gross margin in 9M FY2026 (75.4% in FY2025, 70.8% in FY2023) against 39.9% for Products, and Services supplied 42.2% of FY2025 gross profit on 26.2% of revenue.
rows.mechanism: The App Store commission, advertising, iCloud and licensing are recognised net of near-zero marginal cost on an installed base already paid for by hardware buyers, so incremental service revenue carries almost pure margin.
rows.benchmark: Blended gross margin of 67.9% at Microsoft FY2026 and 59.7% at Alphabet FY2025; Apple's blended 46.9% is the lowest of the three because hardware dominates revenue.
rows.weakens: The 76% services margin is a gross margin before the content, payment and cloud costs that sit in cost of sales; and the Services gross-profit share fell to 39.1% in FY2026 because hardware margins rose faster.
rows.implication: Services is the right asset to own for durability, but at 25% of revenue it cannot by itself offset a hardware margin shock of 100-200bp.
rows.confidence: high - segment gross margin is disclosed in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
rows.follow_up: How much of Services gross profit is App Store commission versus advertising and iCloud? Apple does not disaggregate services gross margin by line.

rows.finding: Apple's EU rate card from 2026-10-01 is 26% on App Store In-App Purchase (15% for small-business, mini-app and video programmes and for auto-renewing subscriptions after year one), 20% on in-app alternative payment, 15% on link-outs and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed outside the App Store; in the US Apple has proposed 5-15% on external-link purchases after a 2025 contempt finding, and the DOJ Section 2 case filed 2024-03-21 is unresolved but in reported settlement talks.
rows.mechanism: Regulators and courts, not Apple, now set the ceiling on the commission; each reduction moves a share of third-party developer revenue from Apple's 76%-margin services line to developers or payment processors.
rows.benchmark: The 30% standard In-App Purchase commission Apple charged before the DMA and Epic litigation (15% for small developers); Google Play has faced the same structural pressure, so this is an industry re-rating, not an Apple-specific one.
rows.weakens: The EU package is a settlement-style simplification agreed with the Commission, which reduces the tail risk of escalating fines; a 26% base rate is a 4-point cut, not the elimination of the toll.
rows.implication: Services growth from FY2027 must come from installed-base growth, advertising and cloud rather than take-rate increases, which caps the multiple the services stream can support.
rows.confidence: medium-high - the rate card is Apple's own disclosure; the US 5-15% proposal still needs court approval and the DOJ outcome is open.
rows.follow_up: What share of Services revenue is EU App Store commission? Apple does not disclose it, which is the largest single unknown in the services margin.

rows.finding: Per active device, annualising the nine months to 2026-06-27 across the disclosed base of more than 2.5bn active devices gives about $194 of revenue, $95 of gross profit (49.1%), $30 of R&D and SG&A, $65 of operating profit (33.6%), $3.6 of capex and $59 of free cash flow.
rows.mechanism: R&D and SG&A are largely fixed against a base that grows about 6% a year, so each added device and each added dollar of services revenue drops through at a high incremental margin; the operating structure breaks even at roughly $153bn of annual revenue, 31.5% of the current run-rate.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 per-device figures of $166 revenue, $78 gross profit, $53 operating profit and $40 free cash flow; the FY2026 step-up is 22% in gross profit per device on 16% revenue growth.
rows.weakens: The per-device figure is an average that hides a wide spread: an iPhone buyer generates several times the services revenue of an iPad or Mac buyer, and Apple does not disclose the split.
rows.implication: The fixed-cost operating leverage is real and large: a 10% revenue decline would still leave the company profitable, which supports a lower risk premium than a hardware cyclical normally earns.
rows.confidence: medium - built from disclosed statements and the disclosed installed base; the annualisation and the divisor are estimates.
rows.follow_up: How does services revenue per device differ between iPhone, iPad and Mac cohorts, and is the base still growing in the premium segments?

rows.finding: Samsung Electronics reported Q3 2026 revenue of KRW 195.3tn and operating profit of KRW 107.4tn, a 55.0% operating margin, on record memory earnings from HBM4, while IDC expects 2026 smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% and the industry ASP to rise 27.6% to $581.
rows.mechanism: A memory shortage transfers profit from device assemblers to component suppliers; Apple's response is price (iPhone revenue +22% on shipment growth in the low teens) and mix (Pro models), which works only while demand is inelastic.
rows.benchmark: Apple's Products gross margin of 39.9% in 9M FY2026 versus 36.9% a year earlier, a rise the company attributes to mix and tariff refunds but not to component costs, which it says will intensify.
rows.weakens: Apple's hardware margin rose rather than fell in FY2026, so the memory transfer has not yet hit reported numbers; tariff refunds and mix more than offset it.
rows.implication: The single largest threat to the model is a cost shock Apple cannot pass on; the Samsung margin is the clearest evidence of who is capturing the value in the 2026 handset stack.
rows.confidence: high on the reported margins; medium on the causal link to Apple's FY2027 margins.
rows.follow_up: What memory cost inflation is embedded in Apple's FY2027 purchase commitments and to what extent have iPhone 18 prices been raised to offset it?

rows.finding: Apple returned $73,872M to shareholders in 9M FY2026 ($62,094M buybacks, $11,778M dividends) against $110,197M of free cash flow, while R&D rose 32.5% to $34,035M and gross intangible assets rose $13,270M to $38,220M with no acquisition line in investing cash flow.
rows.mechanism: Apple funds capability through the income statement and licensed intangibles rather than owned data-centre capex, which keeps reported free cash flow intact while competitors absorb the AI build in capex.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft's TTM capex of $135,921M (39% of revenue) left TTM free cash flow of $59,957M, and Alphabet's $159,804M left $19,747M; Apple's $10,041M of capex left $136,683M.
rows.weakens: The capital-light model means Apple's access to AI capability depends on partners and licences it does not control, and the $13.3bn intangible build is unexplained in the 10-Q.
rows.implication: Buyback capacity is structurally protected, but the buyback slowed 12% year on year while R&D and intangibles rose, so the per-share compounding engine is being partly diverted.
rows.confidence: high on the cash figures; medium on what the intangibles represent.
rows.follow_up: What are the $13.3bn of gross intangibles added in FY2026, over what life are they amortised, and does the amortisation begin to pressure FY2027 operating margin?

plan.decision_question: How does Apple make money, and how durable are the economics of hardware plus services?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple taxes a 2.5-billion-device installed base twice — once at a 40% product gross margin and then for the life of each device at a 76% services margin — but in fiscal 2026 the profit acceleration came from the hardware leg that memory suppliers are now repricing, not from the software leg that regulators are repricing, so the durable half of the model is the smaller half of the growth.
plan.why_different: The market and product sections judge demand, share and capability; this section judges the revenue model and the arithmetic of a single device and a single service dollar, and it is the only section that prices the take rate as a regulated input rather than a competitive one.
plan.mechanism: Installed-base monetisation: hardware buys the device at roughly 40% gross margin and installs the base; services then earn 76% gross margin on that base with near-zero marginal cost. The moat is the switching cost of the base, the leak is that the take rate on third-party transactions is now set by courts and regulators, and the 2026 cost shock is that memory suppliers are taking the hardware margin back.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own history (FY2023-FY2025 mix and margins), Microsoft and Alphabet as high-margin software comparables, Samsung as the memory supplier now capturing the handset stack's profit, and the pre-DMA 30% App Store rate as the regulatory base rate.
plan.counter_evidence: iPhone concentration at 53.9% of 9M FY2026 revenue and rising; services take rates cut in the EU to a 26% base and proposed at 5-15% for US link-outs; memory costs flagged by Apple as intensifying while Samsung earns a 55% operating margin; and hardware, not services, produced 71% of the FY2026 incremental gross profit, so the durable leg is not the one that is growing.
plan.visual: Unit-economics table per active device (FY2025 versus annualised 9M FY2026) plus a pricing table of the App Store rate card by region and effective date.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, risks are manageable, well positioned, moat (unqualified), ecosystem flywheel, about/many/several with a number

business_model.author: Fundamentals Analyst
queries: Apple 10-K FY2025 Item 7 selling, general and administrative expense
Apple 10-K FY2025 advertising expense disclosure in the notes
Apple 10-Q nine months to 2026-06-27 revenue, gross profit and SG&A
Alphabet 10-Q Q3 2026 sales and marketing expense against nine-month revenue
Apple EU App Store commission schedule effective 2026-10-01 (26% / 20% / 15% / 5%)
Samsung Electronics Q3 2026 operating margin and memory pricing

rows.finding: Matched to the device life, four years of gross profit per active device ($78.1 x 4 = $312) against four years of SG&A per device ($11.0 x 4 = $44) gives 7.1:1 and payback in 6.8 months; on nine-month FY2026 annualised figures, $381 against $48 gives 8.0:1 and 6.0 months.
rows.mechanism: Apple's acquisition cost is spread over a four-year replacement cycle, so both numerator and denominator must cover the same life; only then is the multiple comparable with subscription or peer acquisition economics.
rows.benchmark: Alphabet spent 8.6% of revenue on sales and marketing alone in the nine months to 2025-09-30 ($24,813M on $289,007M), against Apple's 6.6% of FY2025 revenue on all SG&A, so Apple's acquisition cost is lean even before the G&A share is stripped out.
rows.weakens: SG&A includes corporate overhead, so 7.1:1 is a conservative floor rather than a measured S&M return; Apple discloses no sales-and-marketing line and no unit sales, so both inputs are estimates built on disclosed dollars and an assumed four-year life.
rows.implication: The hardware-plus-services model returns $7.1 of gross profit per $1 of acquisition cost over a device life - strong for hardware, but a quarter of the subscription-style multiple a one-year denominator would suggest, so price the annuity as bounded by the replacement cycle.
rows.confidence: medium-high: inputs disclosed, life and S&M split assumed
rows.follow_up: What share of Apple's SG&A is selling and marketing rather than corporate G&A, and does the 2.5bn active-device base reflect a four-year replacement cycle or a longer one?

rows.finding: Products supplied $22,629M of the $31,922M increase in nine-month FY2026 gross profit (71%), while Services carries the higher margin at 76.3% versus 39.9% for Products.
rows.mechanism: The FY2026 upgrade cycle lifts the lower-margin hardware leg fastest, so consolidated margin expansion is coming from price and mix in hardware rather than from mix shift into services.
rows.benchmark: FY2025, when Services supplied 77.6% of the $14,518M gross-profit increase - the opposite composition.
rows.weakens: Products gross margin also rose on Pro mix and FX, which may persist into FY2027 if ASPs hold.
rows.implication: Growth quality is lower than the 49.1% consolidated margin implies; the profit driver is the leg exposed to memory costs.
rows.confidence: high: both figures disclosed
rows.follow_up: What is iPhone unit growth versus ASP growth in the September 2026 quarter?

rows.finding: The EU App Store rate card effective 2026-10-01 sets 26% on in-app purchases (15% for reduced-rate programmes), 20% on alternative in-app payment, 15% on link-outs and a 5% Core Technology Commission, against the 30% standard charged before the DMA.
rows.mechanism: Regulators reset the take rate on the highest-margin slice of Services, so the services gross margin of 76.3% is no longer a company-set parameter.
rows.benchmark: US in-app purchase at 15-30% and a proposed 5-15% on external-link purchases after the April 2025 contempt order.
rows.weakens: EU commission is a small share of the $109bn Services line and Apple has offset rate cuts with new fees and higher subscriptions.
rows.implication: A 4-15 point cut on third-party digital transactions is a direct, permanent transfer from the 76%-margin line; the durability of services economics must be underwritten at a lower take rate, not the historical one.
rows.confidence: high on the rate card; low on the revenue at stake
rows.follow_up: What share of Services revenue is EU App Store commission, and what take rate does the DOJ settlement discussion imply for the US?

rows.finding: Samsung Electronics earned a 55.0% operating margin in Q3 2026 on record memory earnings, while Apple's nine-month operating margin was 33.6%.
rows.mechanism: Component suppliers capture the memory upcycle, so the same price Apple charges buys less gross profit per device unless it raises prices.
rows.benchmark: Apple's own 10-Q warning that memory and storage costs will intensify and that price increases may not offset them.
rows.weakens: Samsung's margin reflects memory alone; Apple's long-term supply agreements and prepayments can lag spot pricing.
rows.implication: The hardware gross margin that produced 71% of the profit increase is the line most exposed to a cost shock outside Apple's control.
rows.confidence: medium: Samsung figure independent, Apple exposure inferred from its own risk language
rows.follow_up: How much of FY2027 iPhone cost is locked under supply agreements, and what price increase has Apple already taken?

rows.finding: Trailing capex of $10,041M is 2.2% of revenue against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet, and buybacks of $62,094M in nine months plus $11,778M of dividends returned capital while R&D rose 32.5%.
rows.mechanism: A capital-light model converts profit into distributable cash, but the absence of owned AI infrastructure pushes the capacity requirement onto partners and licences - visible in the $13,270M intangible addition.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft and Alphabet capex at 39.2% and 33.9% of revenue on trailing figures.
rows.weakens: Capital intensity may be a competitive disadvantage in AI, not an advantage, if on-device features need model licensing Apple must pay for.
rows.implication: Free cash flow is structurally high, but the growth capex peers are booking now may reach Apple later through licence fees, intangible amortisation or partner pricing.
rows.confidence: high on the figures; medium on the interpretation
rows.follow_up: What are the $13,270M of intangibles, and over what life are they amortised?

plan.decision_question: How does Apple make money per device, and how durable are the economics of hardware plus services?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple taxes a 2.5-billion-device installed base twice - once at a 39.9% product gross margin when a device is sold, then for its life at a 76.3% services margin - but in fiscal 2026 the growth came from the hardware leg that memory suppliers are now repricing, not the software leg that regulators are repricing, so the durable half of the model is the smaller half of the growth.
plan.why_different: Section 7 reads the consolidated statements; this section builds the per-device unit P&L, the take rates and the matched-period acquisition multiple that explain where the consolidated numbers come from.
plan.mechanism: Installed-base annuity: hardware sale buys the customer, services monetises the base, and the acquisition multiple must be measured over the same four-year device life on both sides of the ratio.
plan.comparison_set: Alphabet's sales and marketing ratio, Samsung's memory margin, Microsoft and Alphabet capex intensity, and Apple's own FY2025 composition of gross-profit growth.
plan.counter_evidence: Both legs are repriced at once: memory costs compress hardware margin while the EU and US reset the App Store take rate; iPhone is 53.9% of sales and volumes are falling industry-wide.
plan.visual: Unit-economics table with matched-period LTV:CAC and payback, plus the pricing table.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, risks are manageable, well positioned; no 28:1 or 32:1 ratio; no one-year SG&A against a four-year LTV

financials.author: Fundamentals Analyst
queries: get_sec_financials AAPL, 5 years plus latest quarter and TTM (statements, ratios, working-capital days, returns)
get_sec_financials MSFT and GOOGL for peer margins, returns, capex and cash conversion
10-K FY2025 Item 8: State Aid Decision note, effective tax rate, unrecognized tax benefits, debt, leases, purchase obligations
10-Q 2026-06-27 Item 1: deferred revenue, intangibles, inventories, commitments, segment note
8-K 2026-07-30 Exhibit 99.1: nine-month cash flow statement, cash taxes paid, buybacks, dividends
get_price_history AAPL 1y: price, market backdrop, 10-year Treasury yield

rows.finding: Nine-month FY2026 revenue rose 16.1% to $364,357M and operating income 21.7% to $122,432M (33.6% margin) from 32.0% in FY2025, but the June 2026 quarter's 50.1% gross margin included approximately 2 percentage points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS, and R&D rose 32.5% to $34,035M.
rows.mechanism: Revenue growth is price and mix-led (iPhone +22.4% on third-party shipment growth in the low teens plus a favourable euro and renminbi swing), while cost of sales was reduced by a one-off Supreme Court-driven tariff refund; both flatter the margin without changing the underlying volume run-rate.
rows.benchmark: FY2023-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 4.2% and FY2025 operating margin of 32.0%; Microsoft FY2026 operating margin 46.8% and Alphabet FY2025 32.0%.
rows.weakens: The margin expansion is real in reported terms and broader than one quarter, and services gross margin also rose to 76.3%; a simple 'all one-off' dismissal would overstate the downside.
rows.implication: The FY2026 margin should be normalised down before it is used in any valuation, and R&D growing twice as fast as revenue is the leading indicator that the operating margin has peaked.
rows.confidence: high - all figures come from the primary statements; the non-recurring nature of the refunds is the company's own characterisation.
rows.follow_up: How much of the 22% iPhone revenue growth is price, mix and FX rather than units, and does the refund reverse in FY2027?

rows.finding: Trailing free cash flow is $136,683M, 1.06x net income, on capex of $10,041M (2.2% of sales); FY2025's 0.88x conversion is explained by the $15.8bn Irish State Aid settlement paid that year, and nine-month FY2026 working capital was a net $2.9bn drag rather than a source of cash.
rows.mechanism: Apple leases or outsources manufacturing capacity and pays suppliers on 98-day terms while collecting receivables in 24 days, so growth releases rather than absorbs capital; competitors that build data centres convert a third or less of profit into free cash.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft TTM free cash flow of $59,957M on net income of $142,631M (0.42x) and Alphabet $19,747M on $235,694M (0.08x), both burdened by AI capex.
rows.weakens: The 1.06x is flattered by a $8,316M receivables release and $5,671M of vendor receivables, and by $10,016M of other liabilities; a normalised year would convert closer to 0.95-1.00x.
rows.implication: Cash conversion is not a concern and Apple's free cash flow is roughly 1.7 times Microsoft's and Alphabet's combined, which is the strongest single argument for owning it in a capex-heavy technology market.
rows.confidence: high - cash flow statements are explicit and the State Aid note reconciles the FY2025 dip.
rows.follow_up: What is the maintenance capex floor, and how much of the FY2026 cash benefit from receivables and vendor receivables is a one-time collection cycle?

rows.finding: Inventories rose to $11,092M at 2026-06-27 from $5,718M at 2025-09-27 (+94%; +87% year on year), lifting days inventory to 16.9 from 9.4 while the cash conversion cycle stayed negative at -56.8 days and deferred revenue rose to $14.9bn, 64% of it current.
rows.mechanism: Apple is pre-buying components into a shortage and paying for them before they ship, which raises inventory days and absorbs cash precisely when component prices are rising; a negative cash cycle elsewhere covers the cost.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 DSO of 34.9, DIO of 9.4 and DPO of 115.4; Microsoft TTM DSO of 65.4 and DPO of 138.8.
rows.weakens: Inventory is still only $11.1bn against $109.4bn of quarterly revenue, so the absolute risk is small; a 6-day rise in inventory days is not yet a working-capital problem.
rows.implication: The negative cash cycle is intact, but the inventory build is the first balance-sheet signal that the memory shortage is now costing Apple cash, and it should be watched as the leading indicator of a gross-margin miss.
rows.confidence: medium - balances are disclosed, but the reason for the inventory build (memory pre-buy versus weak sell-through) is not disclosed.
rows.follow_up: Is the inventory build finished goods ahead of price increases or unsold channel stock, and what is the write-down risk if demand softens?

rows.finding: Net cash is $62,173M at 2026-06-27 (cash and marketable securities $146,517M less debt $84,344M), with term-debt maturities of $12,393M in 2026, $10,078M in 2027 and $9,300M in 2028, lease liabilities of $13.7bn, purchase obligations of $4,752M due in 2026 and $23.2bn of gross unrecognised tax benefits, of which $10.6bn would hit the tax rate.
rows.mechanism: Debt is cheap, long-dated and matched against a $146.5bn liquidity pool, so the company earns net interest income (+$670M in nine months) rather than paying it; the intangible addition is a use of that liquidity that bypassed both capex and the acquisition line.
rows.benchmark: Pristine peer sets: Microsoft's 18.2% goodwill and intangibles to assets and Alphabet's 5.6%.
rows.weakens: Gross intangibles rose $13,270M with no corresponding acquisition in investing cash flow, and the current portion is already $5,075M, so amortisation is beginning; the item is unexplained rather than adverse on its face.
rows.implication: Balance-sheet risk is not a constraint on the position; the intangible build is, because it is the one line that could turn into future amortisation that the current margin does not carry.
rows.confidence: high on the balance-sheet figures; low on what the intangibles represent, which the 10-Q does not disaggregate.
rows.follow_up: What are the $13.3bn of gross intangibles added in nine months, over what life are they amortised, and could the unrecognised tax benefits crystallise?

rows.finding: ROA is 36.1% and ROE 148.8% on the trailing twelve months, while the mechanically computed ROIC of 320.6% is an artefact of near-zero invested capital after $263.2bn of buybacks in FY2023-FY2025; on net operating assets of roughly $100bn the after-tax return is about 128%, and on total assets about 33%.
rows.mechanism: Buybacks shrink the equity and invested-capital denominators, so ROE and ROIC rise mechanically as the company returns capital; the economic return is the cash profit earned on operating assets, which is high but not 300%.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft TTM ROIC 35.2% and ROA 20.1%; Alphabet TTM ROIC 30.1% and ROA 30.6%; a cost of capital estimated at 9-10% from a 4.99% ten-year Treasury plus a 4.5-5.0% equity risk premium.
rows.weakens: The 128% and 33% are the analyst's restatements; the reported ratios are the ones most screens and index models use, and they overstate the true return by an order of magnitude.
rows.implication: Returns are far above any plausible cost of capital, so the case does not rest on capital efficiency; it rests on whether the margin level persists, which is a pricing question rather than a returns question.
rows.confidence: high on the inputs and direction; the cost-of-capital estimate is the analyst's, not a disclosed figure.
rows.follow_up: What is the incremental return on the new R&D and intangible spend, and does management report any AI-attributable revenue?

rows.finding: Apple bought back $82,226M of stock over the trailing twelve months and paid $15,640M of dividends, about 72% of free cash flow, retiring 1.6% of the diluted share count a year and lifting EPS growth (22.4%) above net income growth (20.0%) in nine months; the buyback has slowed from $70,579M to $62,094M year on year while R&D rose 32.5%.
rows.mechanism: A company trading above the inverse of its cost of capital converts buybacks into per-share engineering rather than value creation; the cash still leaves the balance sheet, but the return per dollar is below the risk-free alternative.
rows.benchmark: A 4.99% ten-year Treasury yield and a 2.7% trailing free-cash-flow yield; Microsoft's 0.8% buyback yield against Apple's 1.6%.
rows.weakens: Buybacks remain 72% covered by free cash flow and the company is net cash, so there is no solvency or leverage argument against them; the critique is about return per dollar, not affordability.
rows.implication: At roughly 40x trailing earnings the buyback retires shares at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.99% risk-free rate, so it supports the share price more than it compounds value — a point the position sizing should reflect.
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic; medium on the judgement that buybacks at this multiple are value-neutral rather than value-destructive.
rows.follow_up: Will the buyback be cut further to fund AI investment, and is any part of the $13.3bn intangible spend capitalised R&D that would otherwise have hit the operating margin?

plan.decision_question: What do the statements say about earnings quality, cash conversion, balance-sheet strength and capital allocation?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's statements show a business that turns nearly all of its profit into cash — $136.7bn of trailing free cash flow at 1.06x net income on capex of 2.2% of sales — but the fiscal 2026 margin of 49.1% gross and 33.6% operating includes at least 2 points of non-recurring tariff refunds and a $13.3bn intangible build the 10-Q does not explain, so the current margin should be treated as a peak to discount rather than a run-rate to capitalise.
plan.why_different: This is the only section that tests the numbers against each other — profit against cash, margin against the note that produced it, return against cost of capital — and the only one that can say the reported margin is not the economic margin.
plan.mechanism: Reported profit is converted to cash at 1.06x because capex is 2.2% of sales, receivables are collected in 24 days and payables are stretched to 98 days, giving a negative 57-day cash cycle that funds the business; the margin level, by contrast, is a price-times-mix outcome that a component-cost shock or a reversed tariff refund can move by 100-200bp without any change in volume.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2023-FY2025 statements as the base rate, Microsoft FY2026 and Alphabet FY2025 statements for margins, returns and cash conversion, Samsung's Q3 2026 operating margin as the component-cost comparator, and the 4.99% 10-year Treasury against Apple's ~2.5% buyback earnings yield.
plan.counter_evidence: Growth deceleration is the base case (FY2023-FY2025 revenue CAGR 4.2% against 16.1% in 9M FY2026); the 49.1% gross margin contains roughly 2 points of non-recurring tariff refunds and a $13.3bn unexplained intangible build; inventory is up 87% year on year as memory prices rise; and buybacks at roughly 40x earnings return 2.5% per dollar against a 4.99% risk-free rate.
plan.visual: Financial-statements table for FY2023 to TTM plus a returns and working-capital table with Microsoft and Alphabet as the peer column, and an info warning box on the margin quality.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, risks are manageable, well positioned, fortress balance sheet (unqualified), about/many/several with a number, cash machine

rows.finding: Global smartphone shipments fall 16.7% in 2026 to just over 1bn units — the steepest annual contraction recorded — while ASP rises 27.6% to $581 and total market value grows 6.3% to $613bn; memory costs are up nearly 300% YoY and exceed 65% of low-end bill of materials.
rows.mechanism: The AI-datacenter memory shortage raises bill-of-materials cost, wiping out the sub-$100 tier (173M units shipped in 2025) and forcing price increases; volume migrates to vendors with secured supply and premium mix, so the market's value grows while its unit base shrinks.
rows.benchmark: 2025: about 1.25-1.26bn units and roughly 1.5-2.3% unit growth, with a broadly flat ASP; 2026 is the first year value and volume move in opposite directions at this scale.
rows.weakens: IDC cut its own 2026 forecast from -13.9% to -16.7% in one quarter, so the magnitude is unreliable; Counterpoint put Q2 2026 shipments at -11% YoY against IDC's -7.4%, a 3.6pp tracker disagreement on the same quarter.
rows.implication: Size Apple's opportunity in value, not units: a revenue model built on unit growth would understate Apple and overstate volume Android vendors; price lower any assumption of a volume recovery before 2028.
rows.confidence: High on direction (value up, units down); medium on the magnitude of the 2026 decline.
rows.follow_up: When does memory pricing peak — IDC expects increases until at least 2028 — and does Apple's early supply lock extend beyond the iPhone 18 cycle?

rows.finding: Premium handsets ($600+ wholesale) reached a record 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026, up from 25% in H1 2025; Apple held 65% of premium units, with premium sales up 9% YoY, and Apple plus Samsung held 84% of the segment.
rows.mechanism: Premiumisation is the market's adjustment mechanism to higher component costs: trade-in, financing and buyback programmes let buyers absorb higher prices, concentrating profit in the two vendors with the deepest premium franchises.
rows.benchmark: Apple held 62% of premium units in H1 2025, so its share rose about 3pp in a year even as its absolute premium volume grew 9% against a low-single-digit premium market.
rows.weakens: Premium share is measured in units, not profit; Huawei is the third-largest premium brand globally and leads China, and the Counterpoint release was read as a search extract rather than opened in full.
rows.implication: At 65% of the premium pool, Apple's incremental growth has to come from price and services attach rather than from further share gains — the ceiling on share is a ceiling on mix-driven growth.
rows.confidence: Medium — single research house, extract only, unit not value basis.
rows.follow_up: What is Apple's share of premium segment gross profit, and how much of the premium pool is China, where Huawei is the leader?

rows.finding: Apple's Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27 (from $49.9bn), with Q3 FY2026 up 22%, after falling 4% in FY2025 and 8% in FY2024; Apple's China unit share rose to 18.1% in Q2 2026 from 13.9% a year earlier while China's total market fell 4.3%.
rows.mechanism: Apple and Huawei held prices while Android rivals raised theirs on memory costs, and Apple signalled second-half price increases, pulling iPhone 17 demand forward; renminbi strength added a translation tailwind. Share gain in a shrinking market, not market growth, drove the number.
rows.benchmark: China's market fell 4.2% to 134M units in H1 2026 and IDC expects the decline to widen to about 20% YoY in H2 2026, with recovery around 2028-29.
rows.weakens: Part of the gain is pull-forward and FX; if Android pricing normalises after the memory cycle, Apple's price-discipline advantage disappears. IDC's own outlook for H2 2026 China is markedly worse than H1.
rows.implication: Treat China as cyclical and price-driven rather than structurally lost — but do not extrapolate 30% growth; the sustainable read is share defended at 18%, not a new growth engine.
rows.confidence: High — company filings for revenue, IDC for share.
rows.follow_up: How much of the 30% is FX, how much is price, how much is units — and what happens to Apple's China share when Android prices stabilise?

rows.finding: Services reached $120.5bn on a trailing-twelve-month basis to 2026-06-27 (from $85.2bn in FY2023, about 12.3% a year) at a 76.3% gross margin in the nine months, against 36.8% product gross margin in FY2025; Apple's installed base passed 2.5bn active devices in the December 2025 quarter.
rows.mechanism: Services monetise an installed base that no longer grows quickly: about $48 of services revenue per active device a year, at roughly twice the gross margin of hardware, so a 12% services growth rate adds more gross profit than a 5% iPhone growth rate.
rows.benchmark: Global consumer in-app purchase spend was $167bn in 2025, up 10.6%; the App Store ecosystem facilitated over $1.4tn of developer billings and sales, more than 90% of it commission-free.
rows.weakens: The commission-bearing slice of that $1.4tn is not disclosed; Google search-licensing revenue is exposed to US remedies ordered on 2025-09-02, and EU take rates fall from October 2026 (5% outside the App Store, 20% on external payment links).
rows.implication: The valuation question is services durability, not services growth: a take-rate haircut on a 76%-margin stream is worth more per point than hardware share.
rows.confidence: High on the reported figures; medium on the durability of the take rate.
rows.follow_up: What share of services revenue is App Store commission, Google licensing and EU-exposed, and how much of the DOJ Google remedy is already reflected in guidance?

rows.finding: Apple's regional mix shifted toward Greater China in FY2026: nine-month revenue of $149.4bn Americas (+11%), $95.6bn Europe (+16%), $64.8bn Greater China (+30%), $24.4bn Japan (+10%) and $30.2bn rest of Asia-Pacific (+19%), versus FY2025 shares of 42.9% Americas, 26.7% Europe, 15.5% Greater China, 6.9% Japan and 8.1% rest of Asia-Pacific.
rows.mechanism: The two largest regions grow at low-to-mid teens while Greater China grows at 30%, so group growth of 16.2% in the nine months is unusually dependent on a market that is itself contracting in units.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 total revenue grew 6.4% with Greater China down 4%; Europe's FY2026 growth benefits from euro strength against the dollar.
rows.weakens: Europe's 16% includes a disclosed favourable FX effect and Greater China's includes renminbi strength, so constant-currency growth is lower than reported in both.
rows.implication: The Americas — 41% of nine-month revenue — is the swing factor for FY2027: a US replacement-cycle pause would matter more than another quarter of China share gains.
rows.confidence: High — filed regional net sales.
rows.follow_up: What is US carrier upgrade activity and iPhone replacement-cycle length in 2026, and how much of Americas growth is services versus iPhone?

rows.finding: India shipped 33.2M smartphones in Q2 2026, down 11.1% YoY, with the first half at 64.2M units — the lowest in five years — while ASP rose 14.4% to about INR 30,000 and Apple led the market by value.
rows.mechanism: The same memory shock that shrinks Indian volumes raises prices, and Apple's premium position converts the shift into value share even as the unit market contracts; India sits inside a rest-of-Asia-Pacific region that grew 19% in the nine months.
rows.benchmark: India's Q2 2026 decline of 11.1% is steeper than the global 7.4%, and its ASP is roughly a tenth of Apple's implied iPhone ASP.
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose India revenue; the country is a small part of the $30.2bn rest-of-Asia-Pacific line, and the value-share claim comes from trade-press reporting of IDC data.
rows.implication: India is optionality for the next decade, not a driver of FY2027 earnings — worth a diligence question, not a valuation adjustment today.
rows.confidence: Medium — IDC data via trade press, no company disclosure.
rows.follow_up: What is Apple's India revenue and unit share, and how much of iPhone assembly for the US market has moved to India?

plan.decision_question: How large is the profit pool in Apple's markets, how fast is it growing by product and region, and where does Apple's next growth come from?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's markets are shrinking in units and growing in value — global smartphone shipments fall 16.7% in 2026 while market value rises 6.3% to $613bn — and Apple already captures about 40% of that value through $245.5bn of iPhone revenue in the twelve months to 2026-06-27, so the next leg of growth must come from price, services attach and share gains in China and India rather than from a rising unit tide.
plan.why_different: This section sizes the pool and its growth by product and region and locates Apple's position in it; the competition section names rivals and their shares, the business-model section explains how Apple monetises the pool, and the financials section turns the pool into margins and cash. Market answers 'how big and how fast', not 'who wins' or 'how profitable'.
plan.mechanism: The AI-datacenter memory shortage raises handset bill-of-materials cost, collapses the sub-$100 tier, forces Android vendors to raise prices, and shifts volume and value toward premium vendors with secured supply; Apple's revenue therefore grows on a falling unit base, while services compound off a 2.5bn-device installed base whose growth has slowed to a crawl.
plan.comparison_set: Samsung and Xiaomi under the same memory shock in Q2 2026 (+8.1% and -26.4% units); Apple's own history — 2025 unit growth of 1.5-2.3% with flat ASP versus 2026 value growth of 6.3% with a 27.6% ASP jump; premium share of 25% in H1 2025 versus 29% in H1 2026.
plan.counter_evidence: IDC cut its 2026 forecast from -13.9% to -16.7% in one quarter and expects no replacement-cycle recovery before 2028-29; China may fall about 20% in H2 2026; Apple's FY2026 China and Europe growth includes disclosed FX tailwinds and pull-forward demand; services take rates face EU and US legal compression.
plan.visual: A two-method market size table (top-down from IDC market value and premium share, bottom-up from installed base times services revenue per device) followed by a five-region table of Apple's position, barriers and competitors.
plan.prohibited: huge market; strong demand; favorable tailwinds; well positioned; large addressable market; secular growth story; clear runway

rows.finding: The global handset pool is worth $613bn in 2026, +6.3%, on just over 1bn units (-16.7%) at a $581 ASP (+27.6%); iOS share rises almost 4 points to a record 23.6% while Android falls 24.3%.
rows.mechanism: Memory costs up over 300% remove the sub-$100 tier and force price increases, so value grows while units shrink and share concentrates in vendors with supply and premium mix.
rows.benchmark: 2025 units and ASP; IDC's prior forecast of -13.9% units one quarter earlier
rows.weakens: IDC cut the 2026 forecast by 2.8 points within one quarter and Counterpoint's Q2 is -11% versus IDC's -7.4%, so any single growth rate is indicative only.
rows.implication: Size Apple in value, not units: iPhone revenue is 40% of the $613bn pool on roughly a fifth of units. Price and mix, not a volume recovery, drive the next leg.
rows.confidence: high on direction and the $613bn value; medium on the exact 2026 unit decline
rows.follow_up: How much of 2026 iPhone growth is price rather than units, and how much demand was pulled forward ahead of Apple's own price rises?

rows.finding: Regional market sizes: Europe 35m units in Q2 2026 (-10% YoY, Apple and Samsung tied at 34%); Japan -1% YoY in Q2 2026 with no absolute units published; China 134m units in H1 2026 and -15.4% in Q3 2026; India 33.2m units in Q2 2026 (-11.1%); US 33.4m units in Q1 2026 (-3%).
rows.mechanism: Demand is contracting in every region but at different rates, and the premium mix shifts the revenue pool toward Apple even where its unit share is small.
rows.benchmark: Apple's filed segment revenue: Americas $178.4bn, Europe $111.0bn, Greater China $64.4bn, Japan $28.7bn, Rest of APAC $33.7bn in FY2025
rows.weakens: No regional revenue or ASP is published in the material opened, and the US figure is a secondary compilation of Omdia's paywalled tracker.
rows.implication: Use Apple's segment revenue as the company-level proxy for regional value where the trackers publish units only; the regional table can now give a size for every segment.
rows.confidence: medium on Europe, China and India; low on the US and Japan absolute size
rows.follow_up: What are regional market values and ASPs, and what share of each region's value does Apple hold?

rows.finding: Apple's own channel split is 40% direct and 60% indirect of FY2025 net sales; its customers include consumer, small and mid-sized business, education, enterprise and government; 12% of new US iPhone buyers came from Android in the March 2026 quarter and loyalty was 87%.
rows.mechanism: Indirect channels (carriers, resellers, wholesalers) carry most of Apple's revenue while upgrade demand from the installed base, not conversion, supplies most iPhone buyers.
rows.benchmark: CIRP's historical 11-15% Android switching range; 84% loyalty a year earlier
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose the carrier share of iPhone units, the enterprise or government share, or a trade-in split; CIRP is a US-only survey.
rows.implication: Growth depends on the carrier and retail channel and on installed-base upgrades; conversion from Android adds at most a few points of volume.
rows.confidence: high on the 40/60 split and the switching range; low on carrier, enterprise and government shares
rows.follow_up: How much iPhone volume runs through carriers versus Apple retail, and what share of US iPhone buyers are switchers versus upgraders in 2026?

rows.finding: Substitutes are arriving at the edge of the pool: Meta holds 68.7% of XR glasses, a category growing 35.3% in Q2 2026 and forecast +26.3% in 2026; OpenAI's screenless AI companion was reported on 2026-07-14 and remains unshipped; EU alternative app marketplaces and external links cut Apple's commission to 5% and 20% from 2026-10-01.
rows.mechanism: Glasses and AI devices attack the next upgrade and the assistant layer, while regulation attacks the commission on transactions, so substitution works on the value pool rather than on handset units first.
rows.benchmark: 2.5bn+ active Apple devices; a 76.3%-gross-margin services stream
rows.weakens: Glasses pair with a phone today and the OpenAI device has no ship date or price, so neither has taken measurable revenue yet.
rows.implication: Price the near-term risk as small; price the 2027-2028 risk to the upgrade cycle and the services take rate as real and rising.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: At what point do AI glasses or companion devices become a primary compute purchase rather than an iPhone accessory?

rows.finding: The premium tier ($600+ wholesale) reached a record 29% of unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier; Apple took 65% of it and Apple plus Samsung 84%; foldables grow 12.6% to 22.9m units in 2026 and Apple is forecast to ship over 17m foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, generating over $45.7bn.
rows.mechanism: The cost shock pushes the mix up-market, and Apple's premium franchise converts the shift into revenue and gross profit; the foldable entry adds a new high-ASP product line.
rows.benchmark: Premium share of 25% in H1 2025; Apple's current iPhone ASP implied by $245.5bn TTM revenue
rows.weakens: Premium share is measured in units, not value; Counterpoint does not publish the segment's revenue in the material opened.
rows.implication: The profit pool Apple competes for is the premium tier, where its share is 65%, not the 1bn-unit total where its share is about 22%.
rows.confidence: high on the share, medium on the value
rows.follow_up: What is the premium tier's revenue and gross profit, and how much of it is Apple's?

rows.finding: Counter-evidence: IDC cut its 2026 forecast from -13.9% to -16.7% within one quarter, China's market fell 15.4% in Q3 2026, and iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders were reported muted in September 2026.
rows.mechanism: Price-led growth pulls demand forward and leaves the following quarters exposed; a weakening China market undermines the share-gain story.
rows.benchmark: 9M FY2026 Greater China revenue +30%; Apple's China unit share 18.1% in Q2 2026
rows.weakens: The pre-order report is a single analyst note, and China's Q3 decline is a market-wide figure, not Apple-specific.
rows.implication: Do not extrapolate the current growth rate; wait for Q4 FY2026 results (2026-11-02) before treating the China recovery as durable.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: Did Apple's China share hold in Q3 2026 as the market fell 15.4%, and what did the iPhone 18 cycle do to upgrade rates?

rows.finding: Services revenue reached $120,478m TTM at a 76.3% gross margin in the nine months to 2026-06-27 against 36.8% for products in FY2025, or $48.19 per active device a year across more than 2.5bn devices; consumer in-app purchase spend was $167bn in 2025, +10.6%.
rows.mechanism: The installed base is the real market: each active device yields a recurring, high-margin services stream that grows faster than hardware revenue.
rows.benchmark: Products gross margin of 36.8% in FY2025
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose services revenue by category, so the commission-bearing and Google-licensing slices cannot be separated.
rows.implication: Services is the valuation pivot; its exposure to EU and US remedies is a direct risk to the multiple, not a side issue.
rows.confidence: high on the totals and margin, low on the category mix
rows.follow_up: What share of services revenue comes from App Store commissions and Google search licensing, and how much margin survives the EU and US remedies?
