plan.decision_question: Is Apple's silicon/OS/ecosystem advantage durable in the AI era, or is it falling behind?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's silicon and operating-system advantage is still real but no longer self-sufficient: the September 2026 cycle pairs a new A20 Pro and a first foldable with an assistant built on licensed Google Gemini, so the moat is durable in hardware integration and supply-chain scale and thinning at the intelligence layer where the next premium is being priced.
plan.why_different: This section judges the technology on measured performance, shipped dates and regulator-confirmed claims; it does not infer capability from marketing, and it separates hardware integration (defensible) from model capability (now licensed).
plan.mechanism: Vertical integration of silicon, OS and power management raises the fixed cost of matching an iPhone experience, which supports ASP and retention; licensing the foundation model converts Apple's largest capability gap into a variable cost that protects margin but removes differentiation and hands query data and model economics to a competitor that also competes in phones.
plan.comparison_set: Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 on benchmarks; Google in-house Gemini and Tensor; Samsung's licensing of Google models; Huawei's domestic vertical integration; Apple's own history of double-digit single-core leads and FY2025 wearables decline.
plan.counter_evidence: A 4.5% single-core lead is within noise of thermal and scheduler variation; memory and component cost inflation is compressing gross margin and forcing price rises on Mac and iPad; the foldable is 4.5% of output; Vision Pro and patent counts are undisclosed, so the innovation picture cannot be fully verified.
plan.visual: Performance metrics table (A19 Pro/A20 Pro versus Snapdragon) plus the technology comparison table across Apple, Qualcomm, Google, Samsung and Huawei.
plan.prohibited: No "huge market", "strong team", "high barriers to entry", "well positioned", "risks are manageable", no vague counts ("many patents", "about 5"), no sentences about how the section is written, no unlabelled company claims.

strategy.author: Product Analyst
queries: AAPL 10-K FY2025 Items 1, 3, 7 and 8: Services revenue and gross margin, Greater China, legal proceedings (DMA, DOJ, Epic), revenue recognition of App Store commissions
AAPL 10-Q Q3 FY2026 and 8-K 2026-07-30: segment revenue, services growth, R&D, capex, accelerated share repurchase
AAPL 8-K 2026-04-20: CEO transition to John Ternus effective 2026-09-01

European Commission DMA interoperability specification decisions and General Court gatekeeper ruling 2026

rows.finding: Services reached $109,158m in FY2025 (+13.5% from $96,169m) at a 75.4% gross margin versus 73.9% in FY2024, and $91,728m in the nine months to 2026-06-27 (+14%), with Q3 FY2026 services gross margin of 75.6%; Apple books only its commission on third-party App Store sales, on a net basis.
rows.mechanism: Each dollar of services revenue carries about 75 cents of gross profit, so services mix raises consolidated margin without requiring hardware share gains; because revenue is booked net, a commission cut shows up as lost revenue with almost no offsetting cost.
rows.benchmark: Total company gross margin of 46.9% in FY2025 and 50.1% in Q3 FY2026, so services carry roughly two extra points of margin for every point of mix shift.
rows.weakens: Services growth of 12-14% is now slower than total company growth of 16%, so services are no longer the fastest-growing line; advertising and cloud, not the App Store, are cited as the drivers.
rows.implication: The margin engine is intact and mix-favourable, so earnings can grow faster than revenue even if hardware units flatten; this is the strongest leg of the strategy.
rows.confidence: high: primary filings.
rows.follow_up: What share of services growth is advertising and cloud versus App Store commission, and how does that split change if commissions are removed?

rows.finding: The take rate is being removed by courts and regulators: on 2025-04-30 the California District Court barred Apple from imposing any commission on purchases made outside an app and referred it for possible criminal contempt; the European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 2025-04-23 and its Article 6(4) investigation remains open; the EU General Court upheld Apple's gatekeeper status in July 2026.
rows.mechanism: Legal removal of commissions transfers value from Apple to developers and consumers and pushes Apple toward monetising the installed base through advertising, subscriptions and device price, all of which are more contestable.
rows.benchmark: US and EU are the highest-revenue storefronts; the Commission can fine up to 10% of worldwide net sales under Article 6(4).
rows.weakens: Apple's compliance changes in the EU already introduced alternative fee structures, so part of the revenue may migrate rather than disappear; total services revenue has so far kept growing through the changes.
rows.implication: Price the App Store as a declining-margin asset and value services on advertising, cloud and subscriptions; any settlement or ruling that preserves a commission is upside.
rows.confidence: high: primary filing and Commission record.
rows.follow_up: When does the Ninth Circuit rule, and will the Commission's Article 6(4) decision impose a further fine or a structural remedy?

rows.finding: India assembled 23% of global iPhone output in 2025, up from 14% in 2024, and is projected to reach 28% in 2026 while China's share fell from 83% to 74%; Apple also secured components for about 80 million new-model phones for H2 2026 and plans more than 220 million units of 2026 production.
rows.mechanism: Dual-sourcing shifts tariff exposure and builds bargaining power with assemblers, at the cost of duplicated tooling, logistics and lower yields during ramp; scale buying of memory protects unit economics while competitors cut targets.
rows.benchmark: China's share was 83% in 2024 and India's 14%; the 2026 projection of 28% is an industry estimate, not an Apple disclosure.
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose assembly shares; the estimates come from a research firm and may lag actual line shifts, and India still depends on imported components.
rows.implication: The tariff hedge is real but partial: about three quarters of assembly remains in China, so a severe tariff or export-control shock is still a material risk rather than a tail event.
rows.confidence: medium: industry estimate, not company-disclosed.
rows.follow_up: What are the unit costs and yields of Indian assembly versus China, and how much of Indian output is sold domestically versus exported?

rows.finding: Apple launched iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and its first foldable, the iPhone Duo, on 2026-09-09 and will spread at least five new models across H2 2026-H1 2027; iPhone revenue rose 22% to $54,252m in Q3 FY2026 and Mac rose 29% to $10,352m while iPad fell 6% to $6,191m.
rows.mechanism: Staggering launches into two annual windows smooths factory loading and lets Apple price the Pro and foldable tiers above the base model, raising average selling price even where units are flat.
rows.benchmark: Apple planned about 10 million foldables for 2026, roughly 4.5% of its 220 million-plus output; Samsung has sold foldables since 2019.
rows.weakens: The splits come from third-party supply-chain reporting; Apple discloses no unit volumes, and memory-cost inflation could offset the mix benefit.
rows.implication: Product strategy is working commercially without needing a hit new category; the foldable is optionality and a marketing signal, not a growth driver.
rows.confidence: medium-high: multiple independent reports plus primary revenue data.
rows.follow_up: How much of iPhone revenue growth is units versus ASP, and what does the iPhone 18 base model launching in spring 2027 do to seasonality?

rows.finding: Apple entered $10.0bn of accelerated share repurchases in May 2026, pays a $0.27 quarterly dividend, spent $6,799m on property, plant and equipment in nine months (down from $9,473m) while R&D rose 33% to $34,035m, and held $146.5bn of cash and marketable securities against $82.3bn of term debt at 2026-06-27.
rows.mechanism: A capital-light AI strategy leaves free cash flow for buybacks, which lift EPS faster than net income; the risk is that under-investment in owned compute and models is being traded for short-term per-share growth.
rows.benchmark: PP&E payments are 1.9% of nine-month revenue, so the AI build is not a capital drag; net income grew 27% while EPS grew 29%, showing about 1.6 points of buyback contribution.
rows.weakens: Buybacks flatter EPS while gross intangibles rose from $24,950m to $38,220m in nine months, so some cash is going into acquired or licensed intangibles whose nature is not detailed in the retrieved text.
rows.implication: Capital allocation supports per-share compounding without leverage risk; a large AI acquisition is the main way this could change, and management has not signalled one.
rows.confidence: high: primary filings.
rows.follow_up: Does Apple intend a large AI-related acquisition, and what would it do to the buyback pace?

rows.finding: Greater China revenue rose 22% to $18,816m in Q3 FY2026 and 30% to $64,839m in nine months after falling 4% in FY2025 and 8% in FY2024; Apple's China shipments fell 4.3% in Q3 2026 but its share rose to 17.8% from 15.8% as the market fell 15.4%, while Huawei grew 17.3% to 21.1%.
rows.mechanism: Premium mix and pricing lift revenue per unit faster than units fall, so revenue grows while the addressable market contracts; that works until price elasticity or Huawei's premium push breaks it.
rows.benchmark: IDC put China's Q3 2026 smartphone market down 15.4% year on year, with Huawei at 21.1% and Apple at 17.8%.
rows.weakens: The negative for the bull case is the shrinking market itself; a single quarter of share gain does not reverse three years of revenue decline through FY2025.
rows.implication: China is currently a revenue tailwind but a unit headwind: growth is coming from mix and pricing in a shrinking market, which is more fragile than volume growth.
rows.confidence: high on reported figures, medium on causality.
rows.follow_up: Can Apple hold share in China if Huawei's domestic supply chain keeps improving, and what is the iPhone 18 cycle's China sell-through?

rows.finding: John Ternus, previously Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering, became CEO on 2026-09-01 with Tim Cook moving to Executive Chair; the September 2026 launch was the first under Ternus.
rows.mechanism: A hardware-engineering CEO reinforces the integration model and product cadence, while a chair who built the services and China relationships retains influence over the political and regulatory agenda.
rows.benchmark: Apple's last CEO transition was 2011; both Cook and Ternus come from operations and hardware engineering, so the integration doctrine is likely to persist.
rows.weakens: A product engineer at the top may under-weight the regulatory and services negotiations that now determine the take rate; the division of labour between CEO and Executive Chair is not disclosed.
rows.implication: Continuity is the base case, which is reassuring for execution but leaves the strategic questions - AI ownership, regulatory concessions - unresolved by a leadership change.
rows.confidence: high: primary filing.
rows.follow_up: Does the new CEO change capital allocation, services pricing or regulatory posture, and who now owns government affairs and AI strategy?

plan.decision_question: Does Apple's strategy - services growth, AI, India manufacturing and health - create durable growth, or defend a maturing franchise?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's strategy is a defence that is working: services at roughly 75% gross margin, a premium multi-launch product cadence and Indian assembly are turning a maturing hardware franchise into a higher-margin, less tariff-exposed annuity, but each leg now depends on regulators in Brussels and Washington and on a competitor's models, so the plan protects cash generation rather than restoring growth.
plan.why_different: This section tests whether dated commitments are being met and whether resources fit the plan; it judges execution and capital allocation rather than product performance or market size.
plan.mechanism: Mix shift into 75%-gross-margin services and premium hardware raises profitability even when units stagnate; Indian assembly and memory pre-purchasing reduce tariff and supply shocks; capital-light AI keeps cash flowing to buybacks - but regulator-mandated removal of commissions and a licensed model layer put a ceiling on how much of the value Apple can keep.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2023-FY2025 trajectory (Greater China revenue falling 8% then 4%, wearables falling 4%); Samsung and Huawei in China; hyperscalers' capitalised AI build versus Apple's opex-funded approach; the base rate for platforms under DMA-style rules, where commission revenue migrates to device price and advertising.
plan.counter_evidence: Every growth leg is contested: US courts and the European Commission are removing App Store commissions, services growth of 12-14% is slower than the mid-teens total-company growth it once led (FY2025 Services +13.5% versus FY2026 total +16%), memory costs are rising, China units are shrinking, the foldable is about 4.5% of output, and the AI layer is licensed from a competitor.
plan.visual: Milestone table with dated commitments and their status (foldable and iPhone 18 shipped, India 28% target, DMA Article 6(4) decision, Ninth Circuit appeal, Ternus first full year).
plan.prohibited: No "huge market", "strong team", "high barriers to entry", "clear business model", "fierce competition", "risks are manageable", "well positioned"; no vague counts; no sentences about how the section is written; no unlabelled company claims.

rows.finding: The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 2025-04-23 and ordered it to end anti-steering restrictions within 60 days; a separate Article 6(4) case on developer contract terms remains open, with a statutory maximum of 10% of worldwide net sales (about USD 41.6bn on FY2025 net sales of USD 416.2bn).
rows.mechanism: DMA enforcement attacks the steering rules that protect App Store take rates; the fine is a rounding error, but the cease-and-desist and pending Article 6(4) decision set the template for lower commissions on link-out and alternative distribution.
rows.benchmark: Alphabet was fined EUR 430m (Google Play) and EUR 460m (Search) under the DMA in July 2026, after its EUR 4.1bn Android fine was upheld in 2022 and confirmed on final appeal in July 2026. DMA fines are calibrated in the hundreds of millions, far below the 10% cap.
rows.weakens: Apple has appealed the 2025 decision; Article 6(4) has been open since June 2024 with no final decision disclosed; Apple's compliance changes may preserve part of the economics through new fee structures.
rows.implication: Do not underwrite a large fine; underwrite a slow, permanent compression of EU App Store commission revenue and price it as a Services-margin haircut rather than a one-off charge.
rows.confidence: High on the facts; medium on the revenue effect because Apple does not disclose App Store revenue or take rates.
rows.follow_up: What effective commission will Apple earn on EU link-out purchases after the 2025 decision and any Article 6(4) remedy?

rows.finding: Services produced USD 109.2bn of FY2025 net sales and USD 82.3bn of gross profit at a 75.4% gross margin, 61.9% of Apple's USD 195.2bn total gross profit; App Store third-party sales are booked net, so commissions flow almost entirely into this pool.
rows.mechanism: Because Apple recognises only its commission on third-party app sales, a lower take rate or a shift to external payment hits Services revenue and gross profit almost one-for-one, with little offsetting cost of sales.
rows.benchmark: Services gross margin is 75.4% versus 36.8% for Products (USD 307.0bn sales, USD 194.1bn cost of sales), so a dollar of lost App Store commission removes about twice the gross profit of a dollar of lost hardware sales.
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose App Store revenue, commission revenue or regional take rates, so the sensitivity is an upper bound on the App Store-specific effect.
rows.implication: Regulatory remedies are a margin-mix problem: a 10% cut in Services gross profit would remove about USD 8.2bn, or 6.2% of FY2025 operating income, material even if no fine is ever imposed.
rows.confidence: High on disclosed figures; low on the App Store share.
rows.follow_up: What share of Services revenue and gross profit is App Store commission revenue, by region?

rows.finding: The DOJ and 15 states plus DC sued Apple for monopolization on 2024-03-21 in the District of New Jersey seeking equitable relief; the motion to dismiss was denied and by July 2026 the parties were in early settlement talks, with fact discovery running to late May 2027. In Epic v. Apple the court found contempt on 2025-04-30 and barred fees on out-of-app purchases; the Ninth Circuit on 2025-12-11 allowed some link-out commission and the Supreme Court granted cert on the contempt standard on 2026-06-30.
rows.mechanism: US remedies target the same anti-steering rule in Apple's largest App Store market; a ban on link-out commissions removes the fee without a statute, faster than the DMA process.
rows.benchmark: In the Google search case the D.C. District Court entered a final judgment in December 2025 restricting distribution deals; the parallel Apple exposure is the undisclosed Google search-distribution revenue that flows through Services.
rows.weakens: DOJ seeks no damages; Apple has already changed US anti-steering rules; the Ninth Circuit accepted that Apple can charge some commission; a settlement could remove the tail risk.
rows.implication: US remedy risk is the largest single regulatory threat to Services margin, but the 2027+ timeline and settlement talks make it a 2027-2029 earnings issue, not a 2026 one.
rows.confidence: High on docket facts; medium on cash effect.
rows.follow_up: What commission has Apple actually collected on US link-out purchases since the 2025 injunction, and what would a Supreme Court ruling on contempt change?

rows.finding: The UK CMA designated Apple with strategic market status on 2025-10-22 and by 2026-10-20 was consulting on steering and NFC access conduct requirements; Korea's KMCC fined Apple KRW 20.81bn (about USD 15.5m) on 2026-10-28 and ordered payment-link and commission changes within three months; Japan's MSCA took effect 2025-12-18 with Apple designated in March 2025; 48 Chinese developers complained to SAMR on 2026-06-23.
rows.mechanism: Each regime copies the same anti-steering and core-service logic, so DMA compliance diffuses at near-zero marginal cost while fines stay modest; the risk is cumulative take-rate erosion rather than one penalty.
rows.benchmark: Korea ruled that a 26% fee on third-party billing was an evasion of the 30% norm, setting a de facto ceiling on compliant commission levels across jurisdictions.
rows.weakens: The UK has not fined Apple, Japan is dialogue-based, China has only a complaint, and Korea's fine is about 0.004% of Apple's revenue.
rows.implication: Enforcement diversification raises the probability that the global effective take rate converges down toward the mid-teens, a structural Services margin headwind.
rows.confidence: High on the records; medium on convergence speed.
rows.follow_up: Will the CMA's first conduct requirements cap commissions or only mandate access and steering?

rows.finding: France's Autorité de la concurrence fined Apple EUR 150m on 2025-03-31 for abusing dominance through the implementation of App Tracking Transparency, finding the consent framework neither necessary nor proportionate and harmful to small publishers.
rows.mechanism: Privacy features are treated as access rules when implemented by a dominant platform, so Apple's privacy differentiation creates antitrust exposure as well as brand value.
rows.benchmark: Meta was fined EUR 200m under the DMA on 2025-04-23 over its pay-or-consent model; EU regulators now treat consent design as a competition issue.
rows.weakens: EUR 150m is about 0.04% of FY2025 sales; Apple can adjust consent flows.
rows.implication: Privacy and ATT risk is a recurring compliance cost and a constraint on advertising-adjacent services, not a one-off.
rows.confidence: High.
rows.follow_up: Has Apple changed ATT consent flows in France, and does the decision create damages claims from publishers?

rows.finding: Apple's 2025 greenhouse-gas emissions were more than 60% below 2015 and roughly flat versus 2024, against a 75% reduction target for 2030 that must be met before carbon removals balance the remainder.
rows.mechanism: The remaining gap sits in supplier energy and product use, where Apple's leverage is contractual; the cost is real but small relative to USD 133.1bn of FY2025 operating income.
rows.benchmark: Apple's 75%-before-removals target is stricter than a pure offset strategy, but independent review flags the removal-dependent residual as unverified.
rows.weakens: Apple has not disclosed the volume or cost of carbon removals, and emissions were flat in 2025 despite growth.
rows.implication: Climate is a brand and compliance issue, not a cash-flow driver; the investable question is whether green claims attract EU litigation or regulatory challenge.
rows.confidence: Medium.
rows.follow_up: How many tonnes of carbon removals has Apple contracted, at what cost, and with what third-party assurance?

rows.finding: Apple's manufacturing is concentrated with outsourcing partners primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, and its 10-K flags supplier industrial-accident risk; Apple files an annual Form SD conflict-minerals report (latest 2026-05-28).
rows.mechanism: Labour risk transmits through supply disruption and brand damage rather than direct fines; India's PLI has reduced concentration, with cumulative iPhone exports passing USD 50bn by December 2025.
rows.benchmark: India's iPhone exports reached a record INR 2 lakh crore (about USD 23bn) in FY2026, the PLI's final year, making Apple the country's largest branded exporter; this is subsidy-supported capacity rather than a proven structural cost advantage.
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose facility-level audit results or accident rates in SEC filings, so the risk cannot be quantified from public records.
rows.implication: Supply-chain labour is a tail risk rather than a priced recurring cost; the India ramp lowers China concentration but adds new regulatory and quality risk.
rows.confidence: Medium.
rows.follow_up: What are the lost-time injury and audit non-compliance rates at Apple's largest assembly suppliers in China and India?

rows.finding: Apple has one class of stock, an independent chair and eight directors, with no material related-party transactions disclosed; Tim Cook's 2025 target pay was USD 59m and 92% of votes cast supported say-on-pay in 2025; a China Entanglement Audit shareholder proposal was rejected on 2026-02-24. The EU State Aid case ended with USD 15.8bn payable to Ireland and a USD 10.2bn net FY2024 tax charge; the US Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple is claiming refunds.
rows.mechanism: Governance is not the discount driver; the binding policy variables are tax (already crystallised) and trade (refundable but volatile), while the political shareholder proposal signals China exposure as a governance theme.
rows.benchmark: The State Aid case ran from 2016 to the ECJ's 2024-09-10 confirmation and ended in cash settlement; the 2026 IEEPA ruling reversed tariff cost after about a year, showing trade costs are reversible while tax precedent is not.
rows.weakens: Apple's FY2025 effective tax rate fell to 15.6% from 24.1% in FY2024 because the prior year carried the one-time State Aid charge, so the headline overstates the ongoing tax burden.
rows.implication: Treat State Aid as sunk and tariffs as reversible noise around gross margin; watch Section 232 semiconductor and Section 301 actions, which remain live after the IEEPA ruling.
rows.confidence: High.
rows.follow_up: What is the annual cost of Section 232 and Section 301 tariffs net of refunds, and what is the Google search-distribution revenue at risk?

plan.decision_question: Which ESG, regulatory and policy factors materially change Apple's cash flows, margin or valuation, and how should an investor price them?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's ESG exposure is not a carbon or governance problem but a platform-regulation problem: enforcement in five jurisdictions is aimed at the 75.4%-gross-margin Services pool, where fines to date are immaterial (EUR 500m in the EU, EUR 150m in France, USD 15.5m in Korea) but remedies on link-outs and alternative distribution can permanently compress the highest-margin revenue stream.
plan.why_different: The ESG section is the only place where regulation and policy are treated as cash-flow variables rather than checklists: it prices the enforcement mechanism, maps the jurisdictions and separates one-off fines from structural remedies, feeding the financial, strategy and risk sections.
plan.mechanism: Platform regulation attacks the commission rules that protect App Store take rates; because third-party app sales are booked net, a lower take rate hits Services gross profit almost one-for-one. Fines are small relative to USD 416.2bn of sales, but conduct remedies are permanent. Trade policy moves hardware cost and supply geography, and tax disputes are already cash-settled.
plan.comparison_set: Alphabet (DMA fines of EUR 430m for Google Play and EUR 460m for Search in July 2026; EUR 4.1bn Android fine upheld in 2022 and confirmed in July 2026; USD 1.0bn charge) and Meta (EUR 200m DMA fine in April 2025) as the peer enforcement base rate; Samsung as the India PLI comparator; Apple's own FY2019-FY2025 record.
plan.counter_evidence: Fines are below 0.2% of sales; enforcement timelines slip (DOJ discovery to May 2027; DMA Article 6(4) unresolved since June 2024); the Ninth Circuit allowed Apple to charge some link-out commission; Apple's compliance changes may preserve economics through new fees; App Store revenue is not disclosed and may be a smaller share of Services than the market assumes; environmental and labour risks are not financially material on current disclosure.
plan.visual: Regulatory record table (regulator, record, date, status) plus a Services gross-profit sensitivity table showing the effect of 5%, 10% and 20% commission-pool cuts.
plan.prohibited: ESG is strong; committed to sustainability; well positioned; manageable; high barriers to entry; fierce competition; clear business model; about; many; recently; any sentence describing how the section is written.

rows.mechanism: Privacy features are treated as access rules when implemented by a dominant platform, so Apple's privacy differentiation creates antitrust exposure as well as brand value.
rows.benchmark: Meta was fined EUR 200m under the DMA on 2025-04-23 over its pay-or-consent model; EU regulators now treat consent design as a competition issue.
rows.weakens: EUR 150m is about 0.04% of FY2025 sales; Apple can adjust consent flows.
rows.implication: Privacy and ATT risk is a recurring compliance cost and a constraint on advertising-adjacent services, not a one-off.
rows.confidence: High.
rows.follow_up: Has Apple changed ATT consent flows in France, and does the decision create damages claims from publishers?

rows.finding: Apple's 2025 greenhouse-gas emissions were more than 60% below 2015 and roughly flat versus 2024, against a 75% reduction target for 2030 that must be met before carbon removals balance the remainder.
rows.mechanism: The remaining gap sits in supplier energy and product use, where Apple's leverage is contractual; the cost is real but small relative to USD 133.1bn of FY2025 operating income.
rows.benchmark: Apple's 75%-before-removals target is stricter than a pure offset strategy, but independent review flags the removal-dependent residual as unverified.
rows.weakens: Apple has not disclosed the volume or cost of carbon removals, and emissions were flat in 2025 despite growth.
rows.implication: Climate is a brand and compliance issue, not a cash-flow driver; the investable question is whether green claims attract EU litigation or regulatory challenge.
rows.confidence: Medium.
rows.follow_up: How many tonnes of carbon removals has Apple contracted, at what cost, and with what third-party assurance?

rows.finding: Apple's manufacturing is concentrated with outsourcing partners primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, and its 10-K flags supplier industrial-accident risk; Apple files an annual Form SD conflict-minerals report (latest 2026-05-28).
rows.mechanism: Labour risk transmits through supply disruption and brand damage rather than direct fines; India's PLI has reduced concentration, with cumulative iPhone exports passing USD 50bn by December 2025.
rows.benchmark: India's iPhone exports reached a record INR 2 lakh crore (about USD 23bn) in FY2026, the PLI's final year, making Apple the country's largest branded exporter; this is subsidy-supported capacity rather than a proven structural cost advantage.
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose facility-level audit results or accident rates in SEC filings, so the risk cannot be quantified from public records.
rows.implication: Supply-chain labour is a tail risk rather than a priced recurring cost; the India ramp lowers China concentration but adds new regulatory and quality risk.
rows.confidence: Medium.
rows.follow_up: What are the lost-time injury and audit non-compliance rates at Apple's largest assembly suppliers in China and India?

rows.finding: Apple has one class of stock, an independent chair and eight directors, with no material related-party transactions disclosed; Tim Cook's 2025 target pay was USD 59m and 92% of votes cast supported say-on-pay in 2025; a China Entanglement Audit shareholder proposal was rejected on 2026-02-24. The EU State Aid case ended with USD 15.8bn payable to Ireland and a USD 10.2bn net FY2024 tax charge; the US Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple is claiming refunds.
rows.mechanism: Governance is not the discount driver; the binding policy variables are tax (already crystallised) and trade (refundable but volatile), while the political shareholder proposal signals China exposure as a governance theme.
rows.benchmark: The State Aid case ran from 2016 to the ECJ's 2024-09-10 confirmation and ended in cash settlement; the 2026 IEEPA ruling reversed tariff cost after about a year, showing trade costs are reversible while tax precedent is not.
rows.weakens: Apple's FY2025 effective tax rate fell to 15.6% from 24.1% in FY2024 because the prior year carried the one-time State Aid charge, so the headline overstates the ongoing tax burden.
rows.implication: Treat State Aid as sunk and tariffs as reversible noise around gross margin; watch Section 232 semiconductor and Section 301 actions, which remain live after the IEEPA ruling.
rows.confidence: High.
rows.follow_up: What is the annual cost of Section 232 and Section 301 tariffs net of refunds, and what is the Google search-distribution revenue at risk?

plan.decision_question: Which ESG, regulatory and policy factors materially change Apple's cash flows, margin or valuation, and how should an investor price them?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's ESG exposure is not a carbon or governance problem but a platform-regulation problem: enforcement in five jurisdictions is aimed at the 75.4%-gross-margin Services pool, where fines to date are immaterial (EUR 500m in the EU, EUR 150m in France, USD 15.5m in Korea) but remedies on link-outs and alternative distribution can permanently compress the highest-margin revenue stream.
plan.why_different: The ESG section is the only place where regulation and policy are treated as cash-flow variables rather than checklists: it prices the enforcement mechanism, maps the jurisdictions and separates one-off fines from structural remedies, feeding the financial, strategy and risk sections.
plan.mechanism: Platform regulation attacks the commission rules that protect App Store take rates; because third-party app sales are booked net, a lower take rate hits Services gross profit almost one-for-one. Fines are small relative to USD 416.2bn of sales, but conduct remedies are permanent. Trade policy moves hardware cost and supply geography, and tax disputes are already cash-settled.
plan.comparison_set: Alphabet (DMA fines of EUR 430m for Google Play and EUR 460m for Search in July 2026; EUR 4.1bn Android fine upheld in 2022 and confirmed in July 2026; USD 1.0bn charge) and Meta (EUR 200m DMA fine in April 2025) as the peer enforcement base rate; Samsung as the India PLI comparator; Apple's own FY2019-FY2025 record.
plan.counter_evidence: Fines are below 0.2% of sales; enforcement timelines slip (DOJ discovery to May 2027; DMA Article 6(4) unresolved since June 2024); the Ninth Circuit allowed Apple to charge some link-out commission; Apple's compliance changes may preserve economics through new fees; App Store revenue is not disclosed and may be a smaller share of Services than the market assumes; environmental and labour risks are not financially material on current disclosure.
plan.visual: Regulatory record table (regulator, record, date, status) plus a Services gross-profit sensitivity table showing the effect of 5%, 10% and 20% commission-pool cuts.
plan.prohibited: ESG is strong; committed to sustainability; well positioned; manageable; high barriers to entry; fierce competition; clear business model; about; many; recently; any sentence describing how the section is written.

risk.author: Red Team Analyst
queries: read_sec_filing AAPL 10-Q item 1, keywords amortization, intangible, useful life — current portion of intangibles and purchase obligations
web_search: Google Apple default search payments remedy 2026 non-exclusive one year appeal DC Circuit
web_search: Mehta remedy order Google payments Apple non-exclusive one-year agreements choice screen ruling
web_search: Google paid Apple $20 billion a year default search agreement trial evidence
web_search: iPhone 18 Pro preorder demand first weekend 2026 wait times AI features upgrade
web_search: DRAM contract prices 2026 triple smartphone makers cost memory content per handset TrendForce
web_fetch TrendForce 2026-05-14 press release on 2Q26 mobile DRAM contract prices
web_search: Apple App Store commission revenue estimate 2025 billion analyst services gross profit share
web_search: Apple services Google search payment share of gross profit estimate 2026 analyst

rows.finding: Mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% QoQ for LPDDR5X and 70-75% for LPDDR4X in 2Q26 after several quarters of steep increases, and average handset DRAM content still rises to 8.5GB in 2026; Apple's July 2026 10-Q states component costs may materially hurt gross margin and revenue.
rows.mechanism: Cost per handset compounds while price increases to offset it suppress the units Apple needs; 100bp of gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, about $0.30 of EPS.
rows.benchmark: 9M FY2026 gross margin of 49.1% against 46.9% in FY2025, of which about 2pp of the June quarter was a one-off tariff refund, so 48% ex-refund is the level to defend.
rows.weakens: The scenario assumption that a 48% gross margin holds through FY2027 on price and mix alone.
rows.implication: Underwrite FY2027 at 47% gross margin, which removes about $0.90 of EPS against the $9.56 consensus, and rebase the entry band accordingly.
rows.confidence: high on the cost data and the filing language, medium on the elasticity
rows.follow_up: What is the December-2026 quarter gross margin on a like-for-like basis once the tariff refund is out?

rows.finding: Google's payment to be Safari's default has been reported at about $20bn a year since the 2022 trial record, equivalent to 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109,158M and 12.9% of trailing operating income of $154,859M; the US remedy kept payments lawful but banned exclusivity and moved contracts to annual renegotiation, and Google filed its defence of the Safari agreement by 2026-05-22.
rows.mechanism: Near-100% incremental-margin revenue is reset every year by a counterparty whose exclusivity premium has been removed by court order, while the remedy itself is under cross-appeal.
rows.benchmark: 12.9% of trailing operating income against a bear-case multiple of 26x and apple's own 40.0x trailing multiple.
rows.weakens: The claim that platform regulation is a sentiment issue rather than an earnings event, and the base-case EPS of $9.56 which carries the payment in full.
rows.implication: Do not capitalise the payment in the multiple; a 50% cut costs $0.56 of EPS and 5.9% of FY2027 consensus, and the base value at 34x falls to about $287.
rows.confidence: medium: the amount is a press estimate and Apple discloses neither the sum nor its margin
rows.follow_up: At what price does the payment renew for 2027, and does the DC Circuit restore or remove any of it?

rows.finding: About $149bn of the $1.4trn App Store ecosystem is commission-bearing digital goods; Apple's EU terms from August 2026 charge 5% on transactions completed outside the store and 20% on external payment links from 2026-10-01, against a 30% headline rate and a 15% US proposal for external purchases.
rows.mechanism: A take rate falls on a fixed commerce pool, so each 1,000bp removed from half the pool is about $7.5bn of near-pure-margin revenue, roughly $0.42 of EPS.
rows.benchmark: The 15-26% band the scenario assumes versus the 5-20% terms Apple has already published in the EU.
rows.weakens: The GTM claim that Services growth is a function of distribution reach rather than of a take rate now set by regulators.
rows.implication: Services EPS risk of about -4.4% is additive to the Google payment risk, not an alternative to it.
rows.confidence: medium: the pool is a third-party estimate and Apple discloses no App Store revenue
rows.follow_up: What share of third-party billings moves to external links in the first two quarters under the October 2026 terms?

rows.finding: The current portion of intangible assets, net rose to $5,075M from $2,208M, implying roughly $2.9bn more amortisation within twelve months; gross intangibles rose $13,270M to $38,220M in nine months with no acquisition line, while other purchase obligations rose $14.5bn to $29.3bn.
rows.mechanism: A licensed capability is capitalised and amortised into operating expense while its cash settlement sits in purchase obligations, so the charge and the cash arrive in different periods.
rows.benchmark: 55bp of FY2027 revenue, about $0.16 of EPS or 1.7% of consensus; $4.8bn a year if the obligations are paid over three years, 3.5% of trailing free cash flow.
rows.weakens: The claim that 1.06x free-cash-flow conversion is a clean measure of owner earnings.
rows.implication: Model the charge explicitly: if the $13,270M had been cash in the period, conversion was 0.96x, and the discounted value falls further.
rows.confidence: high on direction, medium on the useful life which Apple does not disclose
rows.follow_up: What are the intangibles, over what lives are they amortised and who is the counterparty?

rows.finding: The iPhone 18 Pro entered at $1,199 and initial pre-order wait times were described as lukewarm, with GF Securities' Jeff Pu trimming production estimates in the week of 2026-09-15; IDC expects 2026 shipments to fall 16.7% while ASP rises 27.6% to $581.
rows.mechanism: Pass-through of memory cost requires price, and price suppresses units, so revenue and margin compete for the same lever; an 8% fall in iPhone units removes about $0.50 of EPS.
rows.benchmark: Prior cycles sold out in the first pre-order weekend, and the June 2026 quarter grew iPhone revenue 22.4%.
rows.weakens: The bull case's AI-driven replacement cycle and the base case's 10.6% September-quarter revenue growth.
rows.implication: Wait one clean cycle before entry; the December-2026 quarter, not the 2026-11-02 print, is the read.
rows.confidence: medium: one analyst and one launch weekend
rows.follow_up: Are wait times short because of supply, or because demand at $1,199 is thin?

rows.finding: At $348.91 the shares trade at 40.0x trailing earnings and 37.3x free cash flow; on the valuation's own cash flows and 3.5% terminal growth the price is fair at a WACC near 6.8%, an equity risk premium of about 1.6% over a 4.99% Treasury at a 1.1 beta.
rows.mechanism: The multiple is the reciprocal of a spread between required return and growth, so a 40x price either assumes about 7% perpetual growth or a required return below 7%.
rows.benchmark: FY2022-FY2025 year-end multiples of 24.6x, 27.9x, 37.5x and 34.2x, and a 21.3x median for Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta excluding Samsung's 12.9x.
rows.weakens: The peer-median value of $158 and the two-stage DCF of $183 as fair-value anchors, both of which sit below any multiple a premium franchise trades at.
rows.implication: Keep the no-margin-of-safety verdict but rest it on the reverse DCF rather than on the peer median or the point DCF.
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on the cash-flow path
rows.follow_up: What equity risk premium does the committee require, and does the ten-year yield hold below 5%?

rows.finding: No insider bought a share in the twelve months to 2026-10-29 while $208.0m was sold, 43 of 46 transactions under pre-set plans; repurchases fell 12.0% to $62,094M in nine months from $70,579M a year earlier.
rows.mechanism: Management's own transactions are a revealed price test: the company slowed buying at 40x and no executive added at $300-$345.
rows.benchmark: A 2.5% earnings yield at the price against a 4.99% ten-year Treasury, and a buyback internal rate of return of about 10.5-12.5% only if 8-10% EPS growth persists.
rows.weakens: The claim that the buyback is value-destructive because 2.5% is below 4.99%: the correct test is price against intrinsic value, not a yield against a coupon.
rows.implication: Treat the buyback as support rather than an engine, and read the May 2027 authorisation as the test of intent.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Does the 2027 authorisation shrink, and does any director buy at these prices?

plan.decision_question: Does the watchlist-only, zero-position conclusion survive a 40% bear weight and a bear EPS of $8.00, and what entry price does that imply?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's risk is not a broken franchise but three repricings arriving together — the memory inside its phones, the two services cash flows it does not disclose, and the discount rate — and the valuation prices only the third.
plan.why_different: Only this section sizes the two undisclosed Services cash flows (the reported $20bn Google payment and the $149bn commission-bearing App Store pool) against the memory cost line, recomputes the probability weights from that arithmetic and rebases the entry band; the other sections describe the risks this one prices.
plan.mechanism: Memory cost per handset rises faster than price can rise without suppressing units, because Apple's revenue growth is price-led; simultaneously the App Store take rate and the Google default payment are annual, litigated and reset toward mid-teens, and both land on a Services line earning 76% gross margin. Margin, revenue and multiple therefore compress from three independent causes in the same eighteen months.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2022-FY2025 year-end multiples of 24.6x to 37.5x, the FY2024-to-FY2023 de-rating from 37.5x to 27.9x, the three US peers at a 21.3x median excluding Samsung, and the 4.99% ten-year Treasury against a 2.68% free-cash-flow yield.
plan.counter_evidence: Muted iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders and a $1,199 entry price disprove the AI replacement cycle the bull case needs as well as the margin-holds assumption, but if the December-2026 quarter holds gross margin near 48% ex-refund and Services grows above 12%, the bear case fails and the multiple is defensible at a lower WACC than modelled.
plan.visual: Risk matrix with probability, impact, timing, signpost and mitigation, backed by a stress table of EPS and multiple combinations and a danger card for the Google payment.
plan.prohibited: risks are manageable; well positioned; fierce competition; high barriers to entry; clear business model; about N; many patents; experienced team; any statement about how the report or section is written.

scoring.author: Lead Analyst
queries: Market regime data call 2026-10-30: S&P 500 7,720.39, +12.8% YTD and 1.6% below its high; VIX 17.20 at the 52nd percentile; 10-year Treasury 4.99%; IG spread 86bp; XLK -3.0% over one month against SPY +0.7% (S8, S9, S10, S39, S17, S25).
web_search: S&P 500 forward P/E 18.59x on 2026-10-29 against Apple's 36.5x FY2027E - Apple trades at roughly twice the index multiple (S153).
web_search and web_fetch: Apple 7.25% of SPY, three stocks 21.70% of SPY, top ten 39.27%; Apple +23.06% YTD to 2026-10-06 (S97).
web_search: Apple maximum drawdown history - all-time 81.8% in 2000; 52-week range $243.42-$351.73 (44.5% spread) and five-year closing low $125.02 from the register (S7, S160).
web_search and web_fetch: Microsoft 1999-2012 as the base rate for high-multiple quality franchises losing half the capital while cash flow tripled (S154).
web_search: Apple P/E 45.25x in 2005 to 12.46x in 2014 - own-history de-rating range for the sensitivity table (S156).

rows.finding: Valuation scores 2 of 10: 40.0x trailing earnings, 32.5x EV/EBIT and 36.5x FY2027E against a four-peer median of 18.1x and an S&P 500 forward multiple of 18.59x; the two-stage DCF returns $183 and the probability-weighted outcome is $300, -14.0%.
rows.mechanism: The required return is 9.5% and the cash yield is 2.68%, so the holder depends on multiple and growth that the price has already capitalised.
rows.benchmark: Peer median 18.1x; Apple's own FY2022-FY2025 year-end range 24.6x-37.5x; S&P 500 forward 18.59x.
rows.weakens: At an 8.0% required return the same cash flows support $259-$330, so the score is sensitive to the discount rate rather than to the business.
rows.implication: Valuation is the binding constraint and carries the largest weight in the score table; it is also the only dimension that can improve without new operating evidence.
rows.confidence: high on the multiple, medium on fair value.
rows.follow_up: What ten-year yield would make 40x defensible on a 4.5% equity-risk premium?

rows.finding: Business quality scores 9: nine-month FY2026 revenue of $364,357M at a 49.1% gross margin and 33.6% operating margin, with trailing free cash flow of $136,683M at 1.06x net income on capex of 2.2% of sales.
rows.mechanism: Asset-light hardware plus a 76%-margin services annuity converts a quarter of revenue into gross profit and nearly all of it into cash.
rows.benchmark: Capex of $10,041M against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet, with free cash flow 1.71 times the two combined.
rows.weakens: The 49.1% margin carries about 2 points of one-off tariff refunds and $13,270M of gross intangibles added in nine months, so the quality is flattered at the margin.
rows.implication: Quality justifies a premium multiple; it does not set the size of the premium.
rows.confidence: high.
rows.follow_up: What is the underlying FY2026 gross margin excluding refunds and intangible amortisation?

rows.finding: Growth scores 5: FY2026 revenue grows 14.8% on consensus but global shipments fall 16.7% while ASPs rise 27.6%, and FY2027 EPS growth decelerates to 8.1%.
rows.mechanism: The unit market is shrinking; growth comes from price, mix and services attach, each with a ceiling and each exposed to memory pricing.
rows.benchmark: Premium tier 29% of units in H1 2026 from 25%; Apple 65% of the $600+ tier; China second-half market expected down 20% year on year.
rows.weakens: June-quarter revenue rose 16.4% with double-digit growth in every segment, so the deceleration is a forecast rather than an observed trend.
rows.implication: A growth score of 5 keeps the composite below the level that would justify paying a growth multiple.
rows.confidence: medium.
rows.follow_up: Does the December-2026 quarter deliver unit growth or only price?

rows.finding: Margin durability scores 6: the 10-Q warns memory and storage costs may materially hurt gross margin, mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% quarter on quarter for LPDDR5X in Q2 2026, and management called memory a '100-year flood'.
rows.mechanism: Every 100bp of gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, $0.30 of EPS and 3.1% of base-case net income; a 300bp miss removes $0.90, 9.4% of consensus EPS.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 gross margin 46.9% vs 49.1% in nine months of FY2026, of which about 2 points are tariff refunds.
rows.weakens: The iPhone 18 Pro launched at $1,199 and held premium share, so price is passing some of the cost through.
rows.implication: The margin is a cyclical high rather than a new plateau, which caps the score and anchors the bear case.
rows.confidence: medium-high.
rows.follow_up: What is the December-quarter gross margin like-for-like?

rows.finding: Management and capital allocation scores 6: $82,226M of trailing buybacks at 40.0x earnings retire stock at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.99% Treasury, repurchases fell 12.0% in nine months, and no insider bought a share in twelve months against $208.0m sold.
rows.mechanism: Buybacks at a multiple above intrinsic value transfer value from continuing holders to sellers; the reduction in pace shows management is price-aware but has no alternative deployment at scale.
rows.benchmark: $438.6bn of buybacks and $75.0bn of dividends paid from operating cash flow from FY2021 to FY2026.
rows.weakens: Dividends and buybacks are still funded entirely from operations and net cash is $62,173M, so there is no financial distress risk.
rows.implication: Capital allocation no longer adds to per-share value at this price, so it cannot be used to justify the multiple.
rows.confidence: high on the facts, medium on the judgement.
rows.follow_up: What size and price discipline will the May 2027 authorisation carry?

rows.finding: Regulatory risk scores 4: the Google search-distribution payment is reported at $20bn a year, 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue and 12.9% of trailing operating income, and is undisclosed by Apple; the EU Article 6(4) case carries a cap at 10% of worldwide sales and the EU's new fee card took effect 2026-10-01.
rows.mechanism: The two highest-margin services cash flows are being repriced by courts and regulators rather than by competitors, and the payment now renews annually on non-exclusive terms under cross-appeal.
rows.benchmark: The €500m DMA fine of 2025-04-23 was 0.2% of FY2025 sales; a 10% cut to Services gross profit is $8.2bn, 6.2% of operating income.
rows.weakens: The US remedy preserved the payments and no court has ordered structural separation, so the most damaging outcome remains a probability rather than a fact.
rows.implication: Remedies, not fines, are the earnings risk; the score stays at 4 until Services sub-segment disclosure or a final remedy sizes the exposure.
rows.confidence: medium.
rows.follow_up: What share of Services gross profit is App Store commission plus the Google payment?

rows.finding: Position sizing: the Kelly fraction is negative (-1.6) because the probability-weighted return is -14.0% with a 0.44 upside-to-downside ratio, so the position is zero; the maximum loss to the bear case is -35.8%, and the market regime is risk-on at the index level but rotating out of technology.
rows.mechanism: Kelly maximises log wealth only when expected return is positive; a negative expectation makes the optimal bet zero regardless of the size of the franchise.
rows.benchmark: Bull 20% at +15.8%, base 40% at -6.9%, bear 40% at -35.8%; VIX 17.20, 10-year 4.99%, XLK -3.0% over one month vs SPY +0.7%.
rows.weakens: A 2.68% free-cash-flow yield growing 8% a year beats the 4.99% Treasury only if the multiple holds, which the market regime does not support at a 36.5x forward multiple.
rows.implication: Watchlist only, zero position, with a conditional starter at $273-$309 and a cap of 3-5% of the fund for a long-only portfolio.
rows.confidence: high on the sign of the expected return, medium on its magnitude.
rows.follow_up: What position size would the fund take at $300 with the bear drivers unchanged?

plan.decision_question: What is the weighted score of Apple on quality, growth, margin, management, regulation and price, and what position does that score support for a long-only fund at $348.91?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple scores 5.7 out of 10: a 9 for business quality and an 8 for its moat are outweighed by a 2 for valuation and a 4 for regulatory risk, which supports a watchlist rating with a zero position and a conditional entry at $273-$309.
plan.why_different: This section is the only place where the report commits to a number, a position size and the conditions that change them.
plan.mechanism: The composite is dominated by the 20% valuation weight and the 10% regulatory weight; quality dimensions cannot lift the score above the level that justifies a position while the expected return is negative.
plan.comparison_set: Four-peer median 18.1x, S&P 500 forward 18.59x, Apple's own FY2022-FY2025 year-end multiples, and the Microsoft 1999-2012 lost-decade base rate.
plan.counter_evidence: If the required return is 8.0% rather than 9.5%, the same cash flows support $259-$330 and the valuation score would rise to 4, taking the composite to about 6.1 - still below the level needed to add but no longer a clear avoid.
plan.visual: The weighted score table with the composite read from it, plus the ranked sensitivity table.
plan.prohibited: 'huge market', 'strong team', 'clear moat', 'well positioned', 'risks are manageable', 'high barriers to entry'

thesis.author: Lead Analyst
queries: Market regime data call 2026-10-30: S&P 500 7,720.39 (+12.8% YTD, 1.6% below the 52-week high), VIX 17.20 (52nd percentile), 10-year Treasury 4.99%, 2s10s +37bp, IG spread 86bp, XLK +7.4% over three months vs SPY +3.7% (S8, S9, S10, S37, S39, S17, S25).

web_search and web_fetch: Cisco 2000 peak of $80.06 on 2000-03-27, market capitalisation above $500bn, first exceeded on 2025-12-10 after 25 years; revenue growth 66% in 2000 vs 7.5% recently (S155).
web_search: Apple P/E history - 45.25x in 2005 to a low near 12.46x in 2014 while earnings grew (S156).

rows.finding: Microsoft's free cash flow per share rose 200% from $1.15 in 1999 to $3.45 in 2012 while the share price fell 54% from $58.38 to $26.71; $100 invested at end-1999 was worth $51 at end-2012 with dividends reinvested.
rows.mechanism: A 51x P/FCF entry multiple contained the entire fundamental return: the multiple fell to 8x, so thirteen years of cash-flow growth produced a negative total return.
rows.benchmark: Apple at 40.0x trailing earnings, 37.3x P/FCF and 36.5x FY2027E, with consensus EPS growth of 8.1% for FY2027 and 10.3% revenue growth.
rows.weakens: Microsoft in 1999 was a slower-growing, PC-licence business with no services annuity; Apple's 76%-margin Services and 2.5bn-device base are structurally better, and its 2026 revenue grew 14.8% against Microsoft's single digits.
rows.implication: An entry multiple that discounts a decade of growth can convert a great business into a lost decade for the buyer; the watchlist decision must be driven by the multiple, not by quality.
rows.confidence: medium - the arithmetic is public and exact, but the business comparison is imperfect.
rows.follow_up: What EPS growth rate, sustained for five years, would make 40x a fair entry multiple on a 9.5% required return?

rows.finding: Cisco set a split-adjusted record of $80.06 on 2000-03-27 and did not exceed it until 2025-12-10; revenue was still growing 7.5% in its most recent quarter against 66% in 2000.
rows.mechanism: A hardware leader at a peak multiple de-rated even as its revenue kept compounding, because the growth rate, not the growth itself, set the multiple.
rows.benchmark: Apple's 40.0x is below Cisco's 2000 peak on most measures, but Apple's revenue growth is decelerating to 10.3% in FY2027 from 14.8% in FY2026.
rows.weakens: Cisco's gross margin and recurring revenue were far below Apple's, and Apple's buyback retires 1.6% of shares a year, which Cisco did not do at scale.
rows.implication: A 25-year round trip is the tail the base and bear cases are pricing; it argues for a trim discipline tied to the multiple rather than a permanent hold at any price.
rows.confidence: medium - dates and prices are exact; the analogy is directional.
rows.follow_up: Does Apple's buyback and Services annuity shorten the recovery time from a de-rating compared with Cisco's?

rows.finding: Apple's own P/E fell from 45.25x in 2005 to about 12.46x in 2014 while earnings grew strongly.
rows.mechanism: Earnings growth outran the share price for years; the multiple absorbed the growth rather than the price delivering it.
rows.benchmark: Today's 40.0x against Apple's own FY2022-FY2025 year-end range of 24.6x to 37.5x.
rows.weakens: Apple in 2005-2014 was a one-product hardware company before Services reached 25% of revenue; the current mix justifies a higher multiple than 12x.
rows.implication: Apple has traded at low-teens multiples within its own history, so a 26x bear-case multiple is a observed level, not a stress assumption.
rows.confidence: medium - source is a secondary compilation of filed P/E history.
rows.follow_up: Which segment mix and growth rate historically coincided with Apple's lowest multiples?

rows.finding: The 2026 acceleration is borrowed: global shipments fall 16.7% while ASP rises 27.6%, so revenue growth comes from price and mix, and the June-quarter 50.1% gross margin includes about 2 points of one-off tariff refunds.
rows.mechanism: Memory costs are forcing Android vendors to raise prices or exit the sub-$100 tier, handing Apple premium share; when memory normalises, the mix benefit reverses and the underlying margin is 48.1%, not 50.1%.
rows.benchmark: Premium tier 29% of units in H1 2026 from 25%; Apple 65% of the $600+ tier; consensus FY2027 EPS growth of 8.1% against FY2026's 18.5%.
rows.weakens: Apple raised iPhone 18 Pro prices to $1,199 and held premium share, so some of the mix gain may be durable pricing power rather than a cyclical windfall.
rows.implication: The base case must be built on 48% gross margin and 8% EPS growth, not on the FY2026 print; the bull case needs evidence of a new engine, which no filing provides.
rows.confidence: high - shipment, ASP and margin data are dated and sourced.
rows.follow_up: Does the December-2026 quarter hold gross margin near 48% ex-refund with unit growth?

rows.finding: The probability-weighted outcome is $300 a share, -14.0% from $348.91, on bull 20% at $404, base 40% at $325 and bear 40% at $224.
rows.mechanism: The bear's drivers are dated events already in motion (memory contracts, EU terms live 2026-10-01, the Google remedy on annual terms); the bull's driver, an AI replacement cycle, has no unit evidence yet.
rows.benchmark: Consensus 12-month target $332.39 from 43 analysts, 4.7% below the close; Sell plus Strong Sell ratings up from one to six between May and October 2026.
rows.weakens: At an 8.0% required return the reverse DCF needs only 5.3% perpetual growth, which Apple has already cleared, and 8.1% EPS growth plus the buyback and dividend is an 8.4% annual return with no re-rating.
rows.implication: A negative expected return at the current price makes the decision watchlist only, zero position, with a buy band at 30-34x risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS.
rows.confidence: medium - the probabilities are judgements, the price levels are computed.
rows.follow_up: What would the FY2026 fourth-quarter print on 2026-11-02 have to show to move the base case to $350 or more?

rows.finding: Apple is 7.25% of SPY and the three largest stocks are 21.70% of it, the highest three-stock concentration in the index's history; only 25% of S&P 500 stocks were above their 50-day average on 2026-10-06.
rows.mechanism: Passive flows amplify both directions when a stock is 7% of the benchmark, and thin breadth means the index's record rests on the same three companies.
rows.benchmark: The mid-1980s peak of 13.4% for IBM, AT&T and ExxonMobil combined.
rows.weakens: The three leaders are highly profitable, with net margins of 26.9% at Apple, 40.3% at Microsoft and 55.6% at NVIDIA, unlike the 2000 concentration.
rows.implication: Index weight supports the multiple on the way up and accelerates any de-rating; a long-only fund already owns Apple through its benchmark, so an active position must clear a higher bar.
rows.confidence: high - weights and breadth are dated market data.
rows.follow_up: How much Apple does Meridian already hold through index exposure?

gate: 1+ primary or near-primary source checked where available
2+ numeric facts/proxies or explicit missing-data note
source IDs mapped to source register

plan.decision_question: Is Apple worth owning at $348.91 for a long-only fund, and at what price or milestone does the case turn from watchlist to buy?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple is a superior cash compounder whose shares at $348.91 already capitalise a second growth engine no filing evidences, so the stock belongs on the watchlist at zero position until the price reaches $273-$309 or a clean margin-and-services print removes the bear drivers.
plan.why_different: The other sections describe the business and its price; this section converts them into probabilities, an entry band and the evidence that would falsify the caution.
plan.mechanism: The multiple, not the business, sets the return: 40.0x trailing earnings on 8.1% FY2027 EPS growth means the multiple must hold for the holder to earn the required return, while memory cost and the two services cash flows are being repriced by suppliers and courts.
plan.comparison_set: Microsoft 1999-2012 (FCF/share +200%, price -54%), Cisco 2000-2025 (25 years to regain the peak), Apple 2005-2014 (45.25x to 12.46x); peer median 18.1x, S&P 500 forward 18.59x, consensus target $332.39.
plan.counter_evidence: At an 8.0% required return the reverse DCF needs only 5.3% perpetual growth, already cleared; 8.1% EPS growth plus a 1.6% buyback and a 0.31% dividend is an 8.4% annual return with no re-rating, which is an acceptable long-only outcome.
plan.visual: The scenarios component (Bull 20%, Base 40%, Bear 40%) and the ranked key-assumptions table.
plan.prohibited: 'huge market', 'strong team', 'clear moat', 'well positioned', 'risks are manageable', 'about 5', 'many patents'

user_data_requests.database: Samsung Electronics investor relations and a market-data terminal (e.g. Bloomberg, FactSet, Refinitiv)
user_data_requests.query: Samsung Electronics (KRX: 005930) trailing-twelve-month EV/EBIT, EV/Sales, EV/EBITDA and free-cash-flow yield as of 2026-10-29, in KRW, with the enterprise value components used.
user_data_requests.why: Samsung is the fourth named peer, and only its P/E (12.9x) could be verified. Its other multiples are missing from the SEC XBRL screen because it does not file US GAAP statements, so the four-peer median in the valuation table is carried on three peers for EV/EBIT and EV/Sales. Adding Samsung would lower the peer median further and widen Apple's measured premium.
user_data_requests.how: Samsung publishes quarterly earnings releases and a valuation page on its IR site; a terminal screen for 005930.KS would give the TTM figures directly. Either source is sufficient.

user_data_requests.database: Transaction databases (Capital IQ, Dealogic, Mergermarket) or the acquirers' own deal announcements
user_data_requests.query: Announced EV/revenue, EV/EBIT and EV/EBITDA multiples paid in Microsoft/Activision Blizzard (2022), Dell/EMC (2016) and Broadcom/VMware (2023), with the target's LTM financials used.
user_data_requests.why: The precedent-exits table in the exit section has deal values but no multiples, so it establishes only that no transaction approaches Apple's $5.03T size, not what a strategic buyer has been willing to pay per dollar of earnings. That weakens the section's claim about the price an acquirer would hypothetically pay and is the main limitation on its confidence.
user_data_requests.how: Each acquirer's merger press release or proxy/prospectus states the consideration and the target's trailing financials; a deal database screen would return the multiples in one pass.

user_data_requests.database: US federal court records — PACER (Epic Games v. Apple, N.D. Cal. 4:20-cv-05640; United States v. Apple, D.N.J. 2:24-cv-04055)
user_data_requests.query: Trial exhibits and filings showing App Store commission revenue, effective take rate and App Store operating margin by region (Apple's internal App Store P&L, commission schedules and link-out fee analysis), plus the DOJ's proposed remedies and any settlement terms in the New Jersey monopolization case.
user_data_requests.why: Apple does not disclose App Store revenue, commission revenue or take rates, so the report can only bound the Services-margin exposure from total Services gross profit (USD 82.3bn in FY2025). The court exhibits would convert the 5-20% sensitivity into a cash estimate and show whether remedies remove a small or a large share of Services profit, which is the difference between a Hold and a Reduce on valuation grounds.
user_data_requests.how: Log in to PACER (pacer.uscourts.gov, per-page fee) and download the Epic v. Apple exhibit list and the DOJ v. Apple case docket, or provide the public trial exhibits from the Epic case (Docs. 407-1 and related) that contain Apple's App Store financial data.
