cover.business_summary: Apple Inc. designs and sells iPhone, Mac, iPad and wearables and monetises a base of more than 2.5 billion active devices through Services such as the App Store, iCloud, advertising and payments.

report: rewrite plan: 2 items unresolved after a failed QA loop

cover.tagline: A great franchise at a price that already assumes a second growth engine
cover.business_summary: Apple Inc. designs and sells iPhone, Mac, iPad and wearables and monetises a base of more than 2.5 billion active devices through the App Store, subscriptions and other services, generating $364,357M of revenue in the nine months to 2026-06-27.
cover.industry: Consumer technology — hardware and digital services

top_three: Section 12: rebuild the scenario table and sensitivity on the 20/40/40 weights and the $273-$309 band, so the report states one probability-weighted value ($300, -14.0%) instead of $314 in one section and $300 in four.

Sections 11, 14 and the executive summary: show how $9.10 of risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS is derived and stop the entry band at or below the $300 probability-weighted value, so a buy at the top of the band is not a negative-expectation trade on the report's own distribution.

Section 8 and 6: deduct the $17.7bn of contracted intangible purchases alongside stock-based compensation in the owner-cash-flow build (value falls to roughly $160), and rebuild the LTV:CAC ratio on a consistent four-year basis — the two numbers a committee will test first.

1.name: Completeness sweep
1.notes: Depth and breadth are above the standard: all fifteen sections sit between 8,096 and 8,995 characters, well past the 2,500 floor and inside the 9,000 ceiling, with six or more analytical paragraphs, eight or more figures, four or more source IDs and a Source column on every table of figures; the executive summary is 6,594 characters against a 900 floor and carries all five components. Legal-entity, cap-table, education, career, patent, product, market, competitor, pricing, unit-economics, statements, valuation, milestone, partner, risk-matrix, ESG and regulatory tables are all present as the template requires; there is no VIE, no second share class and no controlling shareholder, and the report says so rather than inventing structure. Company-only claims are labelled in the executive summary table and in sections 3 and 10. Sections 1, 2, 3 and 14 state their open questions explicitly, which is what the standard asks. Section 8 and 12 both handle the listed-company case (no rounds to trace) by substituting a capital-formation table and a trading history, which is the right adaptation.

2.name: Claim verification
2.notes: Claims that pass the independence test: revenue, margins, cash flow, buybacks, debt, maturities, purchase obligations, inventory and intangibles all trace to filings (S5, S6, S47); price, moving averages, volume and the 52-week range to timestamped market data (S7); the EU fine to the Commission's own press release (S134) and the decision (S133); the General Court, UK CMA, Korean and French actions to regulator pages; the memory-price move to TrendForce (S148). The Google payment is correctly presented as an unverified press figure (S147) and not as a disclosure, and section 10 says so in terms. The Gemini arrangement is labelled partially verified with fee and term undisclosed, and Greater China's cause is labelled a management explanation — both correct N3 handling. The App Store ecosystem figure is labelled company framing and reduced to the $149bn commission-bearing slice (S150), which is the right treatment. Patent and FDA citations are primary. Nothing in the register is OCR-derived, so there is no transcription risk beyond the $20bn press figure.

3.name: Missing competitors
3.notes: Geographic coverage is better than most reports in this category: China, India, Japan, Korea, Europe and the US each have a named competitor and a share, and the report does not commit the usual error of listing only US rivals — Huawei's 22.6% China share and its inability to convert outside China is the sharpest single competitive judgement in the report. The strongest missing-competitor challenge I would put to the owner in committee is not a company but a structure: Apple's rival in Services is the open web and alternative payment, not another app store, and the report's own 5%/20% EU fee card is the evidence that the substitute already works.

4.name: Product/market fit
4.notes: Questions I would ask the owner in committee. (1) Selling: Apple's hardest sale is not capability but the price ladder — the iPhone 18 Pro at $1,199 enters a memory-cost cycle with lukewarm pre-orders (S151), so what evidence is there that the installed base will pay the increment rather than hold devices one more year? The upgrade cycle length is the single unmeasured variable and Apple does not disclose it. (2) Budget owner: on consumer hardware the buyer and the payer are the same person, so the real gate is the carrier's trade-in subsidy and the instalment plan; in enterprise and government the buyer is an IT procurement function where Apple's share is not disclosed anywhere in the report. (3) Sales cycle: consumer is same-day, enterprise is a refresh cycle; the report never says which share of revenue is which, and that gap matters because the enterprise tail is what makes a hardware decline slow rather than sharp. (4) Why adoption is not faster: the installed base grew 6.4% against 16.1% revenue growth — the report explains this as monetisation per device, which is right, but it does not ask whether a base growing at 6.4% can carry 8-10% revenue growth once the price lever runs out. (5) Lost deals: the Huawei case in China is the documented loss and the report covers it well; the undocumented losses — India below $400, Europe mid-market — are asserted from share data rather than from buyer evidence. None of these is a Critical gap for a Watchlist verdict, but they are what a partner would press on if the recommendation moved to a buy.

5.name: Number stress-test
5.notes: Stress arithmetic. Gross margin: 504 x 1% = $5.04bn; after tax $4.25bn; /14.6bn shares = $0.29-0.30 EPS. A 300bp miss removes $0.87-0.90, 9.4% of the $9.56 consensus, taking base value at 34x from $325 to $294 and at 26x to $225. Google payment: $20bn x 0.844 / 14.6 = $1.16 a share; half is $0.58, so a 50% cut takes FY2027 EPS to $8.98 and 34x value to $305, and a full loss to $8.40 and $286. Services: a 1,000bp cut on half of the $149bn commission-bearing pool is $7.45bn of gross profit, $0.43 a share. All three together with a 300bp margin miss give $7.67 and $261 at 34x, a 25% downside on a base multiple — that is the compound bear the report should show. Peer-set sensitivity: applying 21.3x (three US peers) to TTM EPS gives $186 and 18.1x gives $158, so the conclusion does not depend on including Samsung; the own-history 31.1x average gives $271; every multiple method lands below $300 and none above $348.91. Reverse DCF: at 9.5% the required ten-year FCF compound is 15%, at 8.0% the perpetual rate is 5.3%, and the fair WACC at 3.5% terminal growth is 6.8% — a 1.6% equity risk premium at 1.1 beta, which no long-only mandate underwrites. Thirty per cent worse on the bear case (EPS $6.02) gives $157 at 26x and still no solvency stress on $62,173M of net cash. The thesis survives every adverse stress by construction, because it is a no-position call; what it is not robust to is the opposite tail — a ten-year yield below 4% with the multiple held at 40x, which the report identifies and quantifies at $330-$404 and which is why the rating is Watchlist rather than Avoid.

items.issue: The regional table gives market size or growth for Greater China and India only; the United States/Americas, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia-Pacific all read "regional value not disclosed", so four of five regions have no denominator for Apple's revenue and share. The section standard requires market size, growth rate, barriers and competitors per region, and the international split is the one the report itself calls decisive (59.0% of nine-month revenue is non-US).
items.action: Add regional smartphone market value and growth (IDC or Counterpoint regional tables, 2025 full year and 2026 H1) for Europe, the Americas, Japan and Asia-Pacific, and state Apple's value share in each. Where a tracker publishes units only, give units and ASP and derive value, marking it as derived.
items.evidence_request: What were 2025 and H1 2026 smartphone market value and unit growth for the Americas, Europe, Japan and Asia-Pacific excluding China, and Apple's share of each, from IDC or Counterpoint regional data?

items.issue: Three of the section's five named executives read "Not disclosed" for education and are given tenure without chronology: Sabih Khan (Apple 1995-2025 in two rows), Kevan Parekh (CFO since 2025, no prior employers) and Jennifer Newstead (no prior role). "Not disclosed" is a claim about the public record, and Apple's leadership pages, appointment 8-Ks and press releases routinely carry degree, institution and prior employer for senior appointments. The team assessment matrix also carries ordinal scores (8/10, 9/10, 7.5/10) with no stated scale or basis, which is the kind of unsourced scoring the rest of the report avoids.
items.action: Search Apple's leadership pages, the 2025-01 CFO appointment release and the 2025-12-04 general counsel release for degrees, institutions, years and prior employers; replace "not disclosed" only where the search genuinely returns nothing, and say which sources were checked. Either give the matrix a stated rubric (what a 9 means) or drop the numeric scores and keep the qualitative read.
items.evidence_request: What education and prior employers do Apple's leadership page and the Parekh and Newstead appointment releases disclose?

items.issue: The version's own check still reads failed on two granularity findings while both sections demonstrably contain the data the finding asks for: team carries counted achievements (2.5bn active devices, Services +28% to $109,158m, eight FY2025 launches) and technology_product carries two patent numbers (US 12,164,344 and US2025/0120026A1). A version whose check reads failed cannot be delivered even though the substance is present.
items.action: Reformat the cells the check reads (a Count column with integers in the achievements matrix; patent numbers written in the exact granted/application pattern in the patent table) and re-save so the check clears; if the pattern is still not matched, record the finding as a check artefact with the evidence quoted, rather than leaving the report at passed=false.

items.issue: The governance paragraph says Apple has "an independent chair in Art Levinson and eight directors"; section 2 says nine directors aged 51-77 and the timeline says Levinson became lead independent director on 2026-09-01. After Ternus joins as a director the count is nine, and Levinson's title is lead independent director.
items.action: Reconcile the director count and Levinson's title with section 2's board paragraph.

items.issue: The KPI table values the company at $5.02trn "at $343.36", a price taken from a 2026-10-27 insider sale, while every other section uses the $348.91 close of 2026-10-29 and a $5,092.1B capitalisation. The price carries no date in the table, so the two market values look like a contradiction.
items.action: Use the 2026-10-29 close and $5,092.1B in the KPI row, or date the $343.36 row explicitly as the 2026-10-27 insider-sale price.

items.issue: The SOM row is nine-month revenue annualised ($485,809m), which is total company revenue, not a serviceable obtainable share of the market; the row above it already sizes SAM.
items.action: Relabel the row as run-rate revenue (a cross-check on SAM capture) or compute SOM as a share of the $613bn pool.

items.issue: The silicon comparison is not like-for-like and the patent record has a hole. The section's shipping flagship is the A20 Pro (announced 2026-09-09) but the only benchmark it cites (4,019) is the A19 Pro, the previous generation, against Qualcomm's current Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5; a 4.5% single-core gap on one run from a single outlet (S117) is inside run-to-run variance, which the red team already flagged. Separately, the patent table reads "Granted — date not disclosed" for US 12,164,344: a granted US patent's issue date and assignee are on the face of the grant, so the retrieved source (S121) is the application publication and a second source is needed.
items.action: Benchmark the A20 Pro against Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 on the same test build and report both a single-core and a multi-core/sustained-throttling figure from a second independent outlet; if no A20 Pro score exists, say so and state that the 4.5% lead is a last-generation comparison, not a current one. Retrieve US 12,164,344 from a patent database and add the grant date and assignee, or write "grant date not retrieved" instead of "not disclosed".
items.evidence_request: What Geekbench 6 single- and multi-core scores has the A20 Pro recorded, and what is the grant date and assignee of record on US 12,164,344?

items.issue: Two passages narrate the report's own revision history, which the writing standard bans: section 11 says "The weights changed from the original 25/45/30, and it is the report's most important correction" and section 10 says "I keep the recommendation and change the weights: bear from 30% to 40%, bull from 25% to 20%". A reader cannot see the earlier draft, so the sentences describe the drafting process instead of the evidence, and they are the only places in the report where internal process leaks into the text.
items.action: Rewrite both passages as findings rather than revisions: state the 20/40/40 weighting with the three dated drivers behind it, and the band at $273-$309 with its multiple arithmetic, without referring to an earlier draft or to what was changed.

items.issue: "+28% to $109.2bn" in the executive summary and "Services grown 28% to $109.2bn between FY2023 and FY2025" in section 2 read as one year's growth for a reader who has just been told FY2025 Services were $109,158m; the underlying figures are +28.1% over two years and +13.5% in FY2025, and section 9 states 13.5%.
items.action: Write "$109,158m, up 28% over FY2023-FY2025 and 13.5% in FY2025" in the executive summary and "Services grew 13.5% in FY2025 and 28% over two years" in section 2.

items.issue: The S&P 500 forward multiple of 18.59x, which anchors the valuation comparison in sections 11 and 14, comes from a single aggregator page (S153, medium confidence, 2026-10-29) rather than an index-provider or exchange figure.
items.action: Add the date of the source to the sentence, or replace it with the index forward multiple from an exchange or index-provider page.

items.issue: The State Aid Decision is quantified two ways: a $10.7bn fall in the FY2025 provision (section 1) and a $10.2bn net FY2024 charge (sections 7 and 13). Both can be true of different lines, but the report never says which is the cash outflow and which the charge. Separately, China figures are quoted for H1 2026 (section 4), Q2 2026 (section 5) and Q3 2026 (section 9) without always naming the quarter, so Apple's China share reads as 17.8%, 18.1% and 22.6%-versus-18.1% in different places.
items.action: State the State Aid amounts by period in one sentence, and label the China figures with their quarter and base (units or value) wherever they appear.

items.issue: The iPhone Duo's existence, ship date and $1,199 entry price rest on Apple's newsroom and supply-chain reporting (S114, S116, S113); the section 9 milestone table records "Shipped", and the executive summary's company-claims table labels the Siri AI and iPhone 18 feature claims as untested but not the Duo's shipment or price.
items.action: Add the status label to the Duo row and milestone, e.g. "shipped per Apple; no independent sell-through or activation data".

items.issue: The competitive set is thorough inside the handset and PC categories but stops at the boundary of the business the report says is most exposed. The App Store's economics face a substitute the table omits: alternative distribution and web payment inside the EU under the DMA, where Apple already charges 5% and 20% instead of 30%, and Epic Games' store as the named challenger. The wearables row lists Huawei, Xiaomi, Samsung and Garmin but not Meta, whose smart glasses are the fastest-growing wearable and the one that competes for the same face real estate as the iPhone. The AI row names OpenAI as an assistant challenger but not as a hardware entrant, which is the form in which the rented-assistant gap becomes a revenue threat.
items.action: Add four rows and a short paragraph: Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses as the wearable that takes the face rather than the wrist; Epic Games and the EU alternative marketplaces as the substitute for the App Store's commission inside the store Apple owns; OpenAI's device programme as the adjacent entrant with the assistant Apple rents; and Tencent's mini-programme ecosystem as the substitute that makes an App Store unnecessary in China. Give share, funding and the specific mechanism for each, and say which of them the section judges immaterial and why.
items.evidence_request: What unit volumes and share does Meta hold in smart glasses, how much iOS commerce runs through alternative marketplaces in the EU since 2026-10, and has OpenAI disclosed a device timeline or hardware partner?

items.issue: Two actors sit outside the table. Chinese memory makers CXMT and YMTC are negotiating with Apple for China sales (section 9) and would, if qualified, relieve the cost shock the whole competitive argument depends on; and WeChat's mini-programme ecosystem is the substitute that has already made a native App Store partly unnecessary for Chinese developers.
items.action: Add CXMT and YMTC to the cost-side competitive map (they are named as suppliers in section 9), and add a sentence on Chinese super-app distribution.

items.issue: The report is unusually clear on why revenue grows faster than the installed base, but it says almost nothing about the selling mechanism or the lost deals. The buyer, the channel and the loss reasons are spread thin: section 1 gives the 40% direct / 60% indirect split and nothing more; no section states who authorises an upgrade decision in enterprise or government, how the carrier subsidy and trade-in mechanic prices the upgrade, or what a buyer who rejected the iPhone bought instead and at what price. Section 5 explains share shifts at market level but not at the point of sale.
items.action: Add one paragraph on distribution and the loss pattern: the carrier and retail channel, the trade-in mechanic in the US, the enterprise and government channel (undisclosed share), and what is documented about buyers who chose Android instead — India below $400, China above $600 against Huawei. Where data is missing, name the source that would settle it (IDC channel splits, carrier trade-in disclosures, Apple's own enterprise case studies).
items.evidence_request: How much of iPhone volume runs through carrier channels versus Apple retail, what share of US iPhone buyers are switchers versus upgraders in 2026, and what does Apple's enterprise and government business represent?

items.issue: Section 12 still runs the pre-reweighting distribution: its scenario table carries weights of 25/45/30, a probability-weighted value of $314 and a -9.9% expected return, and it sets the entry band at $287-$325 on $9.56 of FY2027 EPS. Sections 10, 11 and 14 and the executive summary all use 20/40/40, $300 and -14.0%, with a $273-$309 band on $9.10. The report therefore states two different expected returns for its central decision, and the stale one makes the shares look 4.1 percentage points less unattractive.
items.action: Rebuild section 12's scenario and sensitivity table on 20/40/40 so the probability-weighted outcome is $300 (-14.0%, $294 on bear EPS of $8.00), and replace the $287-$325 entry band with the $273-$309 band the rest of the report uses. Add one sentence reconciling the trim rule above $400 with the $309 ceiling, because at $309 the entry case and the trim case must not overlap.

items.issue: The entry band's top is above the report's own expected value: $309 is 3% above the $300 probability-weighted outcome, and the band is set on $9.10 of "risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS" whose derivation appears nowhere — 30-34x on the $9.56 consensus gives $287-$325, so a 4.6% haircut to EPS was applied and then compounded with a multiple that the same section calls a ceiling rather than a target. Buying at $309 would carry a negative expected return on the report's own distribution, which undercuts the discipline the section is arguing for.
items.action: Show the derivation of $9.10 (which haircuts are netted, at what weight) and set the top of the band at or below the probability-weighted value, or state explicitly why a 30-34x multiple on a risk-adjusted EPS is a better entry rule than the scenario expectation. Apply the same band and the same EPS in sections 11, 14 and the executive summary.

items.issue: LTV per device is computed over a four-year life ($312, $381) and divided by a single year of allocated SG&A ($11.0, $11.9) to claim 28:1 and 32:1; on a consistent four-year basis the ratio is roughly 7:1 and 8:1. SG&A also bundles corporate cost, not acquisition cost, so the figure is not a CAC. The section then uses 32:1 to argue the model is "closer to a subscription business than to a hardware assembler", which is the one inference the arithmetic cannot carry.
items.action: Either rebuild LTV on the same four-year basis as acquisition cost (annual SG&A x 4, or a one-time channel and marketing cost per device) and restate the ratio, or drop the ratio and keep the waterfall, which is sound.

items.issue: The DCF's owner cash flow deducts $13.7B of stock-based compensation as a real cost but not the $17.7B annualised of contracted intangible purchases ($13,270M of gross intangibles added in nine months, $5,075M already current) that the risk section itself says flatters the $183 value. One adjustment is made and its larger twin is not, so the valuation applies an asymmetric test to itself; the missing deduction would cut the value by roughly 12%, to about $160.
items.action: Deduct the intangible purchases (or the amortisation that represents them) in the owner-cash-flow build, restate the base value and state the range. The conclusion strengthens, so the change costs the report nothing.

Adoption is not faster because the installed base grows 6.4% while revenue grows 16.1%, so growth is monetisation per device rather than new users (business model), and because the foldable and AI features are being priced above the tier that would expand the base. # Apple Inc.: Investment research report
Rating: Watchlist
Composite score: 5.7
Data as of: 2026-10-30

## 5分钟速读 Executive Briefing

Apple closed at a record $348.91 on 2026-10-29, a market capitalisation of $5,092.1B and an enterprise value of $5,029.9B, 5.0% above its 50-day average and 17.8% above its 200-day. The shares have returned 28.6% over twelve months against 13.2% for the S&P 500, and essentially the whole gain arrived after April 2026, so the move since the 2026-07-31 third-quarter results extends an already extended re-rating. The market backdrop is risk-on but narrow: the S&P 500 is at 7,720.39, +12.8% year to date and 1.6% below its high, the VIX is 17.20 at the 52nd percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99% with the 2s10s curve at +37bp. Technology is being rotated out even as the index sits near a record — the sector ETF is 3.0% lower over one month against the S&P 500's +0.7% — and Apple is 7.25% of SPY, so passive flows cut both ways [S7, S8, S9, S10, S17, S97].

The report's answer is Watchlist with a zero position. Apple passes the tests that describe a great business and fails the one that describes a good purchase: the need is real, the capability is defensible and the economics scale, but at $348.91 the price already capitalises a second growth engine that no filing evidences. Consensus agrees on quality — 43 analysts carry a $332.39 average target, 4.7% below the close, and Sell plus Strong Sell ratings rose from one to six between May and October 2026 — so the difference is not about the franchise but about the multiple, and on quality the thesis is consensus. Our view is that the 2026 acceleration came from hardware mix, Android retreat under memory costs and 2 points of tariff refunds rather than from a new cycle; the probability-weighted outcome is $300, -14.0%, on a 20/40/40 distribution [S93, S6].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Watchlist | Zero position at $348.91; conditional starter at $273-$300 | 5.7 | Medium | 12-24 months | S93, S6 |

The strongest positives are cash generation, the services annuity and the balance sheet: free cash flow exceeds the two largest peers' combined, net cash is intact, and Services earns the highest gross margin in the group. The most important risks are repricing events already dated: memory costs that management calls a hundred-year flood, an App Store take rate being set by courts rather than by competitors, and a Google payment on annual non-exclusive terms under appeal. The bear case is a multiple event rather than a solvency event, which is why the position is zero rather than short. Follow-up diligence is specific: the FY2026 annual report's intangible note due with the fourth-quarter results, the December-quarter gross margin excluding refunds, and Services sub-segment disclosure.

## 公司概览 Company Overview

Apple at 2026-10-30 is an iPhone business with a services margin bolted on — 53.9% of nine-month FY2026 revenue comes from iPhone while 76.3%-gross-margin Services supply a quarter of sales — and that shape, not the $62.2bn of net cash, is what the next twelve months test. Apple Inc. is a California corporation whose shares trade on Nasdaq under AAPL in US dollars, with one class of common stock: 50,400,000 thousand shares authorised at $0.00001 par and 14,608,963 thousand outstanding at 2026-06-27, down from 14,773,260 thousand at 2025-09-27. Ownership is index-dominated: Vanguard held 9.63% and BlackRock 7.10% of the 14,697,926,000 shares outstanding at 2026-01-02, while all directors and executive officers together held 9,079,765 shares, or 0.062%, and Tim Cook held 3,280,295. There is no controlling shareholder, no VIE and no second voting class, so structural governance risk is low and policy risk arrives through regulators, not a controller [S6, S52].

The entity map is a jurisdiction map, not an intellectual-property map: Exhibit 21 names 19 subsidiaries, omits the rest as insignificant and states no entity's function. Four are Irish, the largest foreign cluster, and the tax note records that the FY2025 provision fell $10.7bn year on year because of the State Aid Decision, leaving an effective rate of 15.6% in FY2025 and 17.6% in nine months of FY2026. Cash and marketable securities of $146.5bn against $84.3bn of debt — $2.0bn commercial paper, $11.0bn current and $71.3bn non-current term debt — left $62.2bn of net cash at 2026-06-27 against $33.7bn nine months earlier, with inventories doubled to $11,092m. Apple returned $73.9bn in nine months ($62.1bn of repurchases, $11.8bn of dividends), equal to 63% of $117.0bn of operating cash flow, and spent $6.8bn on capital expenditure. Buybacks were $8.5bn below the prior-year period and the share count fell only 1.1%, so per-share compounding is a support rather than the engine. The implication for an investor is that the case is carried by mix and margin, not by the balance sheet: net cash is 1.2% of the $5.02trn market value implied by $343.36, the price of an insider sale executed on 2026-10-27, and it cushions nothing in a de-rating. The press valued it at $4.6trn on 2026-08-31 [S6, S5].

The weak points are supply, policy and price, not demand. Management states that component constraints and rising costs for advanced semiconductors, NAND and DRAM "may materially negatively impact" revenue, cost and gross margin, and expects the trend to intensify. Q3 FY2026 gross margin of 50.1% and EPS of $2.02 included roughly 2 percentage points and $0.11 from tariff refunds after the US Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20; the 2026-01-14 Section 232 results added nothing on Apple products, but Section 301 measures have since been imposed. In Europe the Commission fined Apple €500m for breaching the DMA's anti-steering rule in 2025 and Apple changed its EU App Store fees in August 2026. Against Microsoft, which funded $139.5bn of FY2026 investing outflows from $182.9bn of operating cash flow for AI capacity, Apple converts operating cash into buybacks and almost none into owned compute: coherent for an installed-base franchise, fragile if AI becomes the upgrade reason. Confidence is high on the figures (filings through 2026-06-27) and medium on the mix judgement; FY2026 results are not due until 2026-11-02. Open questions: whether Services outgrows iPhone in FY2027, how much of Q3 margin was the refund, what sits behind the $14.5bn rise in other purchase obligations to $29.3bn, and whether Greater China holds if the renminbi weakens [S47, S84, S50].

## 创始人与核心团队 Founding Team & Key Personnel

Apple's capital-allocation record is exceptional and its 2025-2026 product execution is not: the company returned $73.9bn, 63% of operating cash flow, in nine months while growing revenue 16%, but that growth needed a 33% rise in R&D and a $13.3bn build in gross intangibles, and the CEO, COO, CFO and general counsel all changed inside twenty months. John Ternus, 50 when appointed, became chief executive and a director on 2026-09-01; Tim Cook, 65, moved to executive chair after fifteen years as CEO; Sabih Khan, 58, has been chief operating officer since 2025-07-25 and joined Apple in August 1995; Kevan Parekh has been chief financial officer since January 2025; Jennifer Newstead became general counsel on 2026-03-01. The six named executive officers in the 2026 proxy include no AI or machine-learning title, so the function's leadership is not disclosed through Section 16 or proxy channels [S54, S52].

The succession is continuity by design, and that is the point to price. Ternus holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Pennsylvania and worked at Virtual Research Systems before joining Apple's product design team in 2001; the company credits him with the iPad and AirPods introductions. Apple has done this before: Cook, an Auburn industrial engineer with a Duke MBA, was promoted from within in 2011 and leaves an installed base above 2.5 billion active devices in more than 200 countries, Services that grew 13.5% in FY2025 and 28% over two years to $109,158m, and 8 hardware launches in FY2025. Independent reporting describes a well-liked product engineer expected to make "small touches" rather than a disruptive break, against a record including Vision Pro, delayed Siri and a criticised Liquid Glass redesign. Continuity protects the cash engine; it supplies no evidence of a new product cycle [S112, S111, S5, S87].

Capital allocation is where this team earns its premium. In nine months of FY2026 Apple returned $73.9bn — $62.1bn of repurchases and $11.8bn of dividends — equal to 63% of $117.0bn of operating cash flow, while spending $6.8bn, or 1.9% of revenue, on capital expenditure; FY2025 was $89.3bn of repurchases plus $15.4bn of dividends. Microsoft funded $139.5bn of FY2026 investing outflows from $182.9bn of operating cash flow, lifting capital spending $51.4bn for AI. Apple's returns on capital are high because it owns almost no compute [S6, S5, S50].

The spending pattern says the company knows it is behind. Research and development went from $29,915m in FY2023 to $31,370m in FY2024 and $34,550m in FY2025, then reached $34,035m in nine months of FY2026, up 33% year on year and 9.3% of revenue, attributed to AI infrastructure and headcount. In the same nine months gross intangible assets rose to $38,220m from $24,950m and other purchase obligations to $29.3bn from $14.8bn. The filing discloses neither the licensing counterparty nor the exclusivity, and operating margin held at 33.6% only because gross margin rose 2.3 percentage points. A commitment of that size is a permanent transfer of margin to an unnamed party and belongs in the valuation work as an assumption [S6, S5].

Pay and board composition reinforce the status quo. Cook's 2025 target equity was $50m with 75% performance-based, his base salary has not changed since 2016, his target pay sits in the 80th to 90th percentile of the primary peer group, and 2021-granted performance RSUs vested at 187% of target on 2024-10-01, or 477,301 shares, on relative total shareholder return against the S&P 500; he has already met the age-65, ten-year condition for retirement vesting. After the transition the board has nine directors aged 51 to 77, with Wanda Austin (2024) the only new independent since 2021. Relative-TSR scorecards pay for beating the index, reachable through buybacks and margin management without a new product cycle, and oversight of the AI transition sits with a board of finance, consumer-brand and aerospace backgrounds [S52, S54].

Insider behaviour gives no support to the price. Over the twelve months to 2026-10-29 there were 46 sale transactions of 687,127 shares for $208.0m, 43 under Rule 10b5-1 plans, and no purchases; Art Levinson sold $86.7m, Cook $80.4m, O'Brien $23.1m and Ternus $8.5m on 2026-10-02. Plans mute the sales; the signal is no discretionary purchase. The counter-case is about product rather than people: independent reporting describes an unresolved AI gap versus OpenAI and a memory shortage squeezing margins, while the filings show 16% revenue growth and 22% iPhone growth, so the team is executing the current cycle well and the next one is unproven. Four checks matter: Ternus's pay metrics, the executive who owns AI, the licensing counterparty, and whether the board adds an operating AI director [S41, S87].

## 技术与产品 Technology & Product

Apple's silicon and operating-system advantage is still real, but it is no longer self-sufficient. In the September 2026 cycle Apple shipped a 2nm A20 Pro processor, its first foldable iPhone and a rebuilt "Siri AI", and the assistant at the centre of the launch runs on Google's Gemini models under a multi-year agreement announced 2026-01-12 [S115]. The moat is durable where Apple controls the whole stack — processor, OS, power management, hinge, sensors, factory loading — and thin at the intelligence layer, where the next premium is being priced.

### Silicon: the lead is measurable again, and narrower than it looks

Apple designs the processor, the operating system and the power-management logic together, and that co-design, not transistor count, is what puts desktop-class single-thread performance inside a phone power envelope. The A20 Pro, announced 2026-09-09, is Apple's first 2nm phone chip, on TSMC's N2 node: a 6-core CPU with two performance cores at up to 4.93GHz, a 7-core GPU, a dual 16-core Neural Engine rated at 44 TOPS FP16 and Apple's own C2 5G modem [S157]. On Geekbench 6, one outlet measured 4,707 single-core and 12,598 multi-core on its iPhone 18 Pro Max against 3,588 and 10,207 for Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in an iQOO 15 — a 31% single-core and 23% multi-core lead [S157]. The 4.5% gap quoted in earlier coverage was an A19 Pro comparison inside run-to-run variance; on the shipping generation the difference is large enough to measure, and it rests as much on the node as on design.

### Sustained performance is the stronger claim, and it is not pure silicon

Peak scores flatter a chip; the 20-loop stress test in the table shows what a buyer gets after ten minutes. The A20 Pro held 80% of its best score, 8,793 falling to 7,032, while the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 fell to 25%, 6,867 to 1,715; a second outlet measured graphics stability of 79.4% against 65.2% a year earlier, and on Geekbench AI 1.7 a Qualcomm-powered Galaxy S26 Ultra scored higher than the iPhone 18 Pro, so the second neural engine did not buy AI throughput leadership [S158]. Apple's vapour chamber is three times larger and memory no longer sits on the die, so part of that gap is chassis and pairing Apple's largest phone with a thinner Android device overstates the silicon margin. Qualcomm's next part, in the table, closes the single-core gap to about 11% before retail testing.

### The intelligence layer is rented, not owned

The most consequential technical fact about Apple is a contract: the next generation of Apple Foundation Models is based on Gemini models and Google cloud technology. Apple calls this hybrid — on-device processing for privacy, licensed models for capability — and it shipped "all-new Siri AI" with the flagship iPhone. Research spending rose faster than sales while capital expenditure stayed a small fraction of revenue, so capability is bought as an operating cost rather than built on owned compute. Model quality, query data and the pace of improvement sit with a competitor that also sells phones; the Geekbench AI gap is that dependency in miniature.

**Apple converted its largest technology gap into a recurring cost rather than closing it.**

The next Apple Foundation Models are built on Google's Gemini under a non-exclusive multi-year licence, so the assistant's ceiling is set by a competitor while integration, privacy and distribution are what Apple keeps.

## 市场与行业分析 Market & Industry Analysis

**Apple's markets are shrinking in units and growing in value, and Apple already owns the value.** Global shipments fall 16.7% in 2026 to just over 1 billion units, the steepest IDC has recorded, while the average selling price rises 27.6% to $581 and market value grows 6.3% to a record $613 billion. iOS shipments fall 1.3% and its share rises almost four points to a record 23.6%; Android falls 24.3%. At the market's average price Apple's 22% unit share would be worth $134.9 billion; its iPhone revenue of $245,540 million in the twelve months to 2026-06-27 is 1.8 times that, or 40% of the value on a fifth of the units. [S60, S79, S6]

The bottom-up method reaches the same place. Apple reported more than 2.5 billion active devices in the December 2025 quarter. Services revenue of $120,478 million implies a 12.3% CAGR from $85,200 million in FY2023 and $48.19 per active device a year, earned at a 76.3% gross margin in the nine months to 2026-06-27 against 36.8% for products. In-app purchase spend was $167 billion in 2025, up 10.6%. Growth now comes from revenue per device already sold, not from the handset sold. [S58, S6, S83]

Why now is a cost event, not a demand event. Memory prices are up over 300% year on year and exceed 65% of the bill of materials at the low end, erasing the sub-$100 tier that absorbed 173 million units in 2025 and fell almost 60% in the second quarter of 2026. Apple grew units 14.9% and Samsung 8.1% in a quarter when the market fell 7.4%, while Xiaomi fell 26.4%; Counterpoint has the same quarter at -11%, so one quarter is indicative only. The premium tier absorbed the shock: devices above $600 reached a record 29% of unit sales in the first half of 2026 from 25%, Apple took 65% of them and Apple with Samsung 84%. [S60, S77]

Geography and policy move the number more than product mix. Nine-month FY2026 revenue grew 30% in Greater China to $64,839 million, 16% in Europe, 11% in the Americas, 10% in Japan and 19% in the rest of Asia-Pacific. China's market fell 4.2% in the first half of 2026 and 15.4% in the third quarter, so Apple's gain was share, not tide: its unit share rose to 18.1% from 13.9% as it held prices, and Huawei still led at 22.6%. India shipped 33.2 million units in the second quarter of 2026, down 11.1%, with average prices up 14.4% and Apple leading by value; in the United States, where iOS carries 58.35% of mobile web traffic, growth runs through carrier upgrades. Policy then sets the boundaries: Section 232 semiconductor findings on 2026-01-14 imposed no tariff on Apple's products, the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20, and Section 301 duties remain open; Europe's restructured App Store terms impose a 5% commission outside the App Store and 20% on external payment links from 2026-10-01; China's subsidies behind 2025 demand faded in the second quarter and "618" sales fell close to 15%; Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act drove iOS changes in December 2025. Subsidy-created demand is now subsidy-dependent; trade-in-driven demand has held. [S6, S80, S81, S96, S122, S142]

Distribution explains the loss pattern. Apple's FY2025 net sales split 40% direct and 60% indirect, so carriers, resellers and wholesalers carry most revenue, and its customers include consumer, small and mid-sized business, education, enterprise and government. In the US, 12% of new iPhone buyers came from Android in the March 2026 quarter and 87% of iPhone owners repurchased in the first quarter, so growth is upgrade-driven; carrier instalment plans and trade-in are the mechanic, and IDC credits interest-free financing in the US and UK for premium resilience. The buyer who rejects an iPhone buys a mid-tier Android in India, where average prices rose 14.4% and Apple leads only by value, and Huawei above $600 in China, where it leads at 22.6%. Apple does not disclose the carrier share of iPhone units, the enterprise and government share, or trade-in volumes; IDC channel splits and carrier disclosures would settle them. [S5, S166, S161, S165]

**Two sizing methods converge: Apple competes in a value pool it already dominates, not a volume pool it can outgrow.**

Top-down, the handset pool is worth $613 billion in 2026 on just over 1 billion units, and Apple's $245.5 billion of iPhone revenue equals 40.0% of it on a 22% unit share. Bottom-up, more than 2.5 billion active devices at $48.19 of services each produce the $120.5 billion services base, and the app-store spend feeding it grew 10.6% in 2025. [S60, S77, S58, S6, S83]

The judgement is narrower than a growth story. Apple's revenue can compound while its unit market shrinks because price, mix and services attach do the work, and that mechanism holds while memory costs stay high. What is not durable is the current rate: Greater China's acceleration rests on price discipline that works only while rivals raise prices, on renminbi strength and on demand pulled forward ahead of Apple's own increases. IDC cut its 2026 forecast within a quarter and China's third-quarter contraction is the clearest counter-evidence. Confidence in direction is high; confidence in magnitude is lower because the trackers disagree and regional value is unpublished. Three gaps would change the picture — the commission-bearing App Store slice, services revenue by category, and India revenue, which sits inside the Europe segment. The diligence questions are how much of the next four quarters is price rather than units, whether China's share holds as the market falls, and what services margin survives the EU terms.

## 竞争格局 Competitive Landscape

**Apple wins the value pool and only holds the unit pool, and the competitor that matters most is Samsung.** In Q2 2026 Apple's global smartphone market share rose 3.9 points to 20.2% and units 14.9% in a market that fell 7.4%, while it held 65% of $600-plus unit sales in the first half and 84% of that tier with Samsung. In PCs it is fourth at 9.9% and in wrist-worn devices second at 17%; its annual report concedes "a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets". The position is concentrated in one tier whose most dangerous attacker makes the memory Apple buys. [S79, S77, S90, S5]

iPhone competition is now a contest of supply and balance sheets rather than features. Samsung grew units 8.1% and leads at 22.7%; Xiaomi fell 26.4%, OPPO 17.1% and vivo 19.6% as memory exceeded 65% of low-end bill of materials. Apple's counter is scale and early supply commitments; IDC has it on track for a record 22% annual share in 2026. Counterpoint has Samsung at 24% on an 11% smaller market. iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders were reported muted in September 2026. Samsung's memory division sits on the winning side of the cost shock squeezing Xiaomi and OPPO, so it can fund handset price competition longer than any Android rival — that, not product superiority, makes it the most dangerous competitor. [S79, S78, S151]

Inside China the constraint has a name. Huawei leads with 22.6% of a market that fell 4.3% in the second quarter of 2026, growing 19.4%, while Apple rose to 18.1% from 13.9% and grew 24.4%, taking share from OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi and Honor, which fell 9.5% to 21.7%. Huawei is the only rival to beat Apple in a large premium market, on 2025 revenue of CNY880.9 billion; IDC expects HarmonyOS to nearly triple to 51 million units in 2026. Without Google Mobile Services it cannot convert that position outside China, so the threat is a ceiling on Apple's China premium share, not a global assault. Apple's China revenue grew 30% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 because it held prices as Android vendors raised theirs; that advantage ends when they stop. [S80, S82, S60, S6]

PCs and wearables show what happens without a premium monopoly. Mac shipments grew about 10% in a quarter when the PC market fell 4.9% to 68.2 million units, yet Apple is fourth at 9.9% behind Lenovo, HP and Dell, with Mac at 8.1% of FY2025 revenue ($33,708 million). In wrist-worn devices Huawei leads at 20.2%, Apple and Xiaomi are tied at 17%, and Samsung fell 20.7% to 5.8%: cheap Chinese hardware takes the unit lead while Apple keeps the profit through attach and price. Neither line moves the group: Mac and wearables were $69.4 billion of FY2025 revenue against iPhone's $209.6 billion. [S90, S88, S5]

Services faces substitutes and rule-makers at once. Google Play substitutes on Android while Microsoft and Meta compete for advertising and subscriptions: EU terms from 2026-10-01 charge 5% outside the App Store and 20% on external payment links; US remedies ordered on 2025-09-02 left Google's search payments intact on appeal. Three substitutes attack the pool without selling a phone. Meta's glasses hold 68.7% of an XR category that grew 35.3% in Q2 2026 and is forecast to grow 26.3% in 2026 and 40.5% in 2027; today they pair with an iPhone, but Android XR devices arrive later in 2026. Epic and the EU alternative marketplaces permitted under the DMA and the US Epic injunction take commission: Apple proposed 15% on external purchases on 2026-08-14, and the case is at the Supreme Court as No. 25-1311. OpenAI's screenless AI companion, reported 2026-07-14 and unshipped, targets the assistant layer Apple licenses from Google for about $1 billion a year. The 76.3%-gross-margin services stream is Apple's most valuable revenue and its most exposed. [S81, S147, S136, S13, S162, S64, S65, S164]

## 商业模式 Business Model

Apple taxes a 2.5-billion-device installed base twice — once at a 39.9% product gross margin when a device is sold, then for its life at a 76.3% services margin — but in fiscal 2026 the growth came from the hardware leg that memory suppliers are now repricing, not the software leg that regulators are repricing, so the durable half of the model is the smaller half of the growth. The investor implication is that earnings durability has to be underwritten as a hardware cycle with a services annuity attached, not the other way round [S5, S6].

### The mix rotated back to hardware, and that is where the profit came from

In the nine months to 2026-06-27 Apple booked $364,357M of net sales, up 16.1% year on year: iPhone $196,515M (+22.4%), Services $91,728M (+14.1%), Mac $27,137M (+8.6%), iPad $21,700M (+3.0%) and Wearables, Home and Accessories $27,277M (+2.3%). Full-year FY2025 was $416,161M (+6.4%), with iPhone at 50.4% of sales and Services at 26.2%, against a FY2023 mix of 52.3% and 22.2%. Greater China grew 30.0% to $64,839M, Europe 16.1% and the Americas 11.4%. Apple discloses gross margin only for Products and Services, so no iPhone-level margin exists; but of the $31,922M increase in nine-month gross profit, $22,629M — 71% — came from Products, a reversal of FY2025, when Services supplied 77.6% of the $14,518M gross-profit increase [S5, S6, S47]. The driver is a device upgrade cycle with Pro-model mix plus a favourable euro and renminbi swing, not a step-change in the base: the company reported more than 2.5 billion active devices in the December 2025 quarter, up 150 million year on year, or 6.4%, against 16.1% revenue growth. iPhone concentration rose to 53.9% of sales from 50.4%, the number to watch if the upgrade cycle rolls over.

### Services is a toll on the base, and the toll rate is now set outside the company

Services is the structurally superior asset: a 76.3% gross margin in 9M FY2026, up from 75.4% in FY2025 and 70.8% in FY2023, on revenue recognised net of the developers' share. On the disclosed base it is $48.9 of services revenue per active device per year, against $43.7 in FY2025, while device count grew 6.4%, so most of services growth is monetisation per device — advertising, cloud, App Store — rather than more devices. The margin is not a free parameter. Apple's EU rate card from 2026-10-01 cuts the base App Store commission to 26% from the 30% standard, adds a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed outside the App Store, and sets 20% for in-app alternative payments and 15% for link-outs; in the US Apple has proposed 5-15% on purchases through external links after a 2025 contempt finding, and the Department of Justice's Section 2 case from 2024-03-21 is unresolved while the two sides reportedly discuss settlement [S56, S62]. Each point off the commission moves third-party developer revenue out of a 76%-margin line, so the effect lands on the highest-margin slice of Services rather than spread across it.

These are averages: an iPhone buyer generates more services revenue than an iPad buyer, and the average hides the concentration that matters.

**Claim: the hardware leg is doing the growth and the services leg is doing the margin, and both are being repriced at the same time.**

- Products produced 71% of the $31,922M nine-month gross-profit increase ($22,629M) even though Services carries the 76.3% margin (Source: S6).
- The EU rate card effective 2026-10-01 sets a 26% base App Store commission and 5% for distribution outside the App Store, against the 30% standard Apple charged before the DMA (Source: S56, S65).
- Samsung Electronics earned a 55.0% operating margin in Q3 2026 on record memory earnings, the mirror image of the component-cost pressure Apple says will intensify (Source: S59).
- Apple's capital-light model keeps cash intact: $10,041M of trailing capex against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet, while R&D rose 32.5% in nine months (Source: S11, S13).

### Capital allocation is part of the model, not an afterthought

The model funds itself from a negative cash cycle: payables of 98 days against receivables of 24 days and inventory of 17 days give a cash conversion cycle of -56.8 days, and that is what pays for the buyback. Over the trailing twelve months Apple repurchased $82,226M of stock and paid $15,640M of dividends, retiring 1.6% of diluted shares a year and lifting nine-month EPS growth to 22.4% against 20.0% net income growth. The direction of travel in FY2026 is the signal: buybacks fell from $70,579M to $62,094M year on year while R&D rose 32.5% and gross intangible assets rose $13,270M, which the 10-Q does not disaggregate and for which there is no acquisition line in investing cash flow [S47, S11, S13]. Apple is redirecting cash from share retirement into capability it buys or licenses rather than builds — which protects free cash flow but diverts the per-share compounding engine, and the amortisation will land in future operating expense.

### What breaks the economics

The strongest counter-evidence is not that services is legally exposed; it is that both legs are exposed at once. IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026 while the industry ASP rises 27.6% to $581, and Counterpoint measured Apple's Q2 2026 shipments up 13% on an ASP up 17%: Apple is winning share in a market shrinking in units and inflating in price, which works only while demand is inelastic [S59, S60]. Apple's own 10-Q says memory and storage costs will intensify and that price increases may not offset them. If hardware gross margin gives back the 300bp it gained in nine months, and the App Store commission settles at 15-26% rather than 30%, the model still earns a 30%-plus operating margin on a fixed cost base — the economics do not break, they normalise. The open questions that would move confidence are iPhone unit volume, which Apple no longer discloses; the EU share of Services revenue, which Apple does not break out; and whether the $13.3bn intangible addition is amortised over three years — $4.4bn a year of extra expense — or over ten.

## 财务分析 Financial Analysis

Apple's statements show a business that converts almost all of its profit into cash on capex that is trivial for a company of its size, but the fiscal 2026 margin rests on a tariff refund the company itself calls one-off and on an intangible build the 10-Q does not explain, so the current margin is a peak to discount rather than a run-rate to capitalise.

### Growth re-accelerated, and the tax line explains two years of noise

Nine-month FY2026 revenue rose 16.1% to $364,357M and operating income 21.7% to $122,432M, lifting the operating margin to 33.6% from 32.0% in FY2025 and 29.8% in FY2023. That acceleration sits beside a FY2023-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 4.2%, so it is a cycle, not a trend. Two accounting items explain most of the reported profit volatility either side of it: the $10.2bn one-time State Aid charge in FY2024 pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% and cut net income to $93,736M, while the June 2026 quarter's 50.1% gross margin included 2 percentage points of tariff refunds, the company's own approximation, and $0.11 of the $2.02 diluted EPS. Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, so there is no non-GAAP reconciliation to police; the reported line is the only line, and the normalisation is the reader's job. What is not accounting is the cost trend: R&D rose 32.5% to $34,035M in nine months and stock-based compensation was 2.9% of revenue, so the operating margin is being defended with pricing and mix rather than operating leverage [S5, S6, S47].

### Cash conversion is better than the FY2025 ratio suggests

FY2025's 0.88x free-cash-flow conversion is the one ratio a screen will flag, and it is an artefact. The $15.8bn Irish State Aid settlement was still in escrow at 2024-09-28 and was paid during FY2025, so cash taxes for the nine months to 2025-06-28 were $37,332M against $26,555M a year later; adjust for it and FY2025 conversion is 1.0x. In nine months to 2026-06-27, operating cash flow of $116,996M exceeded net income by $15,532M and working capital was a net $2.9bn drag rather than a source of cash, with an $8,316M receivables release and $5,671M of vendor receivables offset by a $16,266M build in other assets and a $5,461M inventory build. The structural reason conversion is high is the negative cash cycle — receivables 24.5 days, payables 98.3 days — and the structural reason it beats peers is capex: $10,041M trailing against $135,921M at Microsoft and $159,804M at Alphabet, which leaves Apple's free cash flow at 1.71 times the two combined [S47, S5, S11, S13].

### The balance sheet is a net-cash position with one unexplained line

At 2026-06-27 Apple held $146,517M of cash and marketable securities against $84,344M of debt, for net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M at the FY2025 year-end. Term-debt maturities are $12,393M in 2026, $10,078M in 2027 and $9,300M in 2028, covered by maturities in the securities portfolio, and the company earns net interest income (+$670M in nine months), so coverage does not bind. Commitments are modest: $4,752M of unconditional purchase obligations due in 2026, lease liabilities of $13.7bn, deferred revenue of $14.9bn (64% current) and $23.2bn of gross unrecognised tax benefits, of which $10.6bn would hit the tax rate if recognised. The line that needs explaining is intangibles: gross intangibles rose $13,270M to $38,220M in nine months with $5,075M already current, and there is no acquisition line in investing cash flow, so this is licensed or purchased capability rather than a bought business, and its amortisation is not yet in the margin. The diligence question that follows: what are those intangibles, over what life are they amortised, and does the expense arrive in FY2027 [S6, S5]?

### Returns are extraordinary, but the reported ROIC is arithmetic, not economics

Return on assets is 36.1% on the trailing twelve months and return on equity 148.8%, both far above Microsoft's 20.1% and 30.6% and lifted by a shrinking equity base. The computed ROIC of 320.6% is meaningless: buybacks of $263,210M in FY2023-FY2025 shrank invested capital to near zero, so the denominator, not the numerator, produces the number. On $100.4bn of net operating assets the after-tax return is 128%, and on total assets 33% — a wide premium to an estimated 9-10% cost of capital built on a 4.99% ten-year Treasury yield, and the honest statement is that Apple earns $128.1bn of after-tax operating profit on $100.4bn of operating capital. Against Microsoft's 35.2% and Alphabet's 30.1% TTM ROIC the comparison is not like-for-like, because those two now carry the data-centre capital Apple does not; that is the trade an investor is making — higher returns on lighter capital, in exchange for depending on partners for AI capacity. The capital-allocation version of the same point: trailing buybacks of $82,226M plus $15,640M of dividends absorbed 72% of free cash flow and retired 1.6% of diluted shares, lifting nine-month EPS growth to 22.4% against 20.0% net income growth; but at $348.91 on 2026-10-29, or 40.0 times trailing EPS, each buyback dollar retires stock at a 2.5% earnings yield while the ten-year Treasury yields 4.99%, so it is per-share engineering with a below-risk-free return, covered 1.4 times by free cash flow and already slowing — $62,094M in nine months against $70,579M [S7, S10, S11, S13, S47].

### Base, upside and downside: gross margin is the variable that moves the outcome

On a base case of $504bn of FY2027 revenue (+6% on an estimated FY2026 of $475bn), a 48.0% gross margin and 15.6% operating expense, operating income is $163.3bn (32.4%) and EPS $9.30; an upside case of 10% revenue growth with a 49.5% margin gives $10.24, and a downside of a 2% revenue decline with a 45.0% margin gives $7.58. Every 100bp on gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, 3.1% of base-case net income; 100bp on the tax rate is $1.6bn, 1.2%. Gross margin dominates, and it is the line management has already flagged: memory and storage costs that price increases "may not" offset. That is the variable to underwrite — whether Apple can hold a 48% margin when Samsung is earning 55% on the components inside its phones [S59, S60].

The fiscal 2026 margin is not a clean run-rate: 2 percentage points of the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin came from tariff refunds the company calls a one-off, inventories rose 94% to $11,092M from the FY2025 year-end close, and $13,270M of gross intangibles were added with no acquisition in investing cash flow and no note disaggregating them (Source: S6, S47). Amortisation of that build is the most likely source of an FY2027 operating-margin surprise that no current line item shows.

## 发展方向与战略 Development Strategy

Apple's strategy is a defence that is working, but it is a defence. Services at a 75.4% gross margin, a premium multi-launch product cadence and Indian assembly are turning a maturing hardware franchise into a higher-margin, less tariff-exposed annuity — while the two forces that set the ceiling, competition law in Brussels and Washington and the cost of renting intelligence from Google, are outside management's control [S115]. The plan protects cash generation; it does not restore growth.

### Services carry the margin, and the law is repricing them

Services reached $109,158m in FY2025, up 13.5% from $96,169m, at a 75.4% gross margin against 73.9% a year earlier, and grew 14% to $91,728m in the nine months to 2026-06-27 with a 75.6% margin in the June quarter. Because Apple books only its commission on third-party App Store sales, on a net basis, a dollar of services revenue carries 75 cents of gross profit against a consolidated gross margin of 46.9% in FY2025 and 50.1% in Q3 FY2026, so every point of mix shift raises group profitability without a single extra iPhone sold. That engine is now being repriced by courts and regulators rather than by competitors. On 2025-04-30 the California District Court found Apple in violation of the 2021 Epic injunction and barred it from imposing any commission on purchases made outside an app, referring the matter to the U.S. Attorney for possible criminal contempt, with the Ninth Circuit hearing Apple's expedited appeal in October 2025; in Europe the Commission fined Apple €500m on 2025-04-23 and its Article 6(4) investigation into Apple's contract terms remains open, carrying potential fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales; and the Department of Justice's antitrust suit, filed on 2024-03-21, seeks equitable relief over the same conduct [S5]. Because Apple has already introduced alternative fee structures and external purchase links in the EU, some revenue migrates rather than vanishing, but the direction is one-way: from commission, which scales with third-party commerce and costs nothing, to advertising, subscriptions and device price, which Apple must earn back every year.

### Manufacturing diversification is real but partial

India assembled 23% of global iPhone output in 2025, up from 14% in 2024, and is projected to reach 28% in 2026, while China's share fell from 83% to 74% [S119, S6]. That is the fastest supply-chain shift in Apple's history and it is being paid for twice: duplicated tooling and lower ramp yields on one side, dependence on Chinese components on the other, since Indian final assembly still imports much of what it screws together. Scale is the offset. Apple secured components for 80 million new-model phones for the second half of 2026 and plans more than 220 million units of production in 2026, which lets it pre-buy memory while Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo cut targets below 100 million units each, and inventories rose to $11,092m from $5,718m in nine months. Tariff policy remains live: the U.S. Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple has applied for refunds, while Section 301 duties and the Section 232 semiconductor investigation continue.

### China: revenue up, units down, share up

Greater China revenue rose 22% to $18,816m in Q3 FY2026 and 30% to $64,839m in nine months, after falling 4% in FY2025 and 8% in FY2024. The unit picture is different: China's smartphone market fell 15.4% year on year in Q3 2026, Apple's shipments fell 4.3%, its share rose to 17.8% from 15.8%, and Huawei grew 17.3% to 21.1% [S5, S122]. Apple is therefore monetising a shrinking market through mix and price rather than winning volume — defensible while the installed base upgrades to Pro and foldable models, fragile if Huawei's domestic supply chain keeps improving or price elasticity bites. The "China share loss" bear case was right about the trend through FY2025 and wrong about 2026 so far.

### Capital allocation is the strategy's quiet centre

Apple spent $6,799m on property, plant and equipment in nine months, 1.9% of revenue, while raising R&D 33% to $34,035m: the AI build is an operating cost, not a capital programme. That leaves cash for shareholders — $10.0bn of accelerated share repurchases entered in May 2026 and a $0.27 quarterly dividend — against $146.5bn of cash and marketable securities and $82.3bn of term debt at 2026-06-27. Net income rose 27% and diluted EPS 29% in the June quarter, so buybacks added 1.6 points of per-share growth [S6, S47]. The risk is not leverage but under-investment: buying capability from Google protects the margin while leaving Apple without owned compute or models, and gross intangibles rising from $24,950m to $38,220m in nine months suggests more value is being purchased than built.

### Resources fit the plan, with one exception

The organisation changed at the top on 2026-09-01, when John Ternus moved from Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering to CEO and Tim Cook became Executive Chair. A hardware engineer running a hardware-led strategy is continuity, and the first launch under him came in on schedule [S54]. The exception is political capital: the decisions that matter most over the next three years — the DMA Article 6(4) remedy, the Ninth Circuit appeal and the DOJ case — are legal negotiations in which a product engineer has less experience than the chair he replaced.

### What must be true within twelve months

Four tests decide whether this is a durable annuity or a melting ice cube. Gross margin must hold near the mid-forties once the tariff refund washes out of the comparison while memory costs rise; the December 2026 quarter is the first clean read. Services growth must stay in double digits with advertising and cloud replacing any commission lost to the Epic order and the DMA — a mix the company has not had to prove for a full year. The iPhone Duo must sell into its planned volume, a claim that rests on Apple's announcement and supply-chain reporting rather than a document verified here, so the volume figure is a target and not a result. And no adverse final remedy should land in Brussels or at the Ninth Circuit that removes commission revenue retroactively. The signposts are concrete: the December-quarter margin, the advertising-versus-App-Store split in the FY2026 10-K, any disclosed size for the Gemini contract, IDC's China share for Q4 2026 and the Article 6(4) decision.

For a long-only watchlist the conclusion is that Apple's strategy earns ownership of the cash flow rather than payment for growth: the services annuity justifies a premium multiple while growth holds in double digits, the buyback compounds per-share value, and the plan creates no new growth engine before 2028. What the record cannot settle is the economics of the AI arrangement — the fee, the term and whether Apple retains query data — and the value of the health and finance adjacencies, neither of which is broken out; Apple discloses no services sub-segment revenue, so the durability of the margin engine has to be inferred from aggregate growth. Confidence in the direction of the strategy is high and in its durability medium, because the plan is well funded and well executed but its two binding constraints are a regulator and a competitor.

## 风险评估 Risk Assessment

Apple's risk is not a broken franchise but three repricings arriving together — the memory inside its phones, the two services cash flows it does not disclose, and the discount rate — and the valuation prices only the third. Nine-month FY2026 revenue of $364,357M and a 49.1% gross margin describe a cyclical high, when a 40.0x trailing multiple has least room. The probability-weighted outcome is $300 on a 20/40/40 bull/base/bear split, because three dated drivers are already in motion: memory contracts repricing handsets, the EU commission terms live since 2026-10-01, and the Google default payment on annual, non-exclusive terms under cross-appeal. The bull's AI-driven replacement cycle has no unit evidence to set against them. The entry band is $273-$300 — 30x to 33x the $9.10 blended FY2027 EPS (60% × $9.56 + 40% × $8.42), capped at the $300 expected value because 34x on $9.10, $309, is above it. Memory is the likeliest driver, at 65% probability: mobile DRAM contract prices rose 78-83% quarter on quarter for LPDDR5X and 70-75% for LPDDR4X in the second quarter of 2026, average DRAM content still rises to 8.5GB a handset in 2026, and the July 2026 10-Q says component costs may materially negatively impact gross margin and revenue. Every 100bp of gross margin is $5.0bn of operating income, $0.30 of EPS and 3.1% of base-case net income, so a 300bp miss costs $0.90, or 9.4% of the $9.56 consensus. The pass-through test is already running: the iPhone 18 Pro opened at $1,199 and pre-order wait times were "lukewarm", with GF Securities' Jeff Pu cutting production estimates in the week of 2026-09-15. Price defends the margin and price suppresses the units, so the two levers cannot both work at full strength; a December-2026 quarter below 47% gross margin like-for-like settles it. [S6, S81, S147, S148, S151]

### Services is named but not sized

Google's payment to be Safari's default has been reported at $20bn a year since the 2022 trial record; Apple discloses neither sum nor margin, so the figure is unverified by the company. At $20bn it is 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109,158M and 12.9% of trailing operating income of $154,859M. The US remedy kept the payments lawful, banned exclusivity and moved contracts to annual renegotiation; Google filed its defence of the Safari agreement by 2026-05-22 and the remedy is under cross-appeal. Half of it is $0.56 of EPS, 5.9% of consensus. The App Store: $149bn of the $1.4trn ecosystem is commission-bearing digital goods, and Apple's EU terms from August 2026 charge 5% on transactions outside the store and 20% on external payment links from 2026-10-01, against a 15% US proposal. A 1,000bp cut on half that pool is another $0.42. Together $0.98 — 10.3% of $9.56, the whole of the bear case's EPS haircut before memory, China or the renminbi. [S147, S150, S81]

### The bear case is too narrow, not too harsh

It applies a defensible multiple to a haircut two services items exhaust, leaving nothing for the cost shock already contracted. Refinancing is the stress that does not bind on $62,173M of net cash. A 30% free-cash-flow cut takes the discounted value to $111 a share, which no committee should believe for a franchise earning 76% margins on a quarter of revenue; the honest form of that stress is EPS minus 17% at 26x, or $206. Policy is priced the same way rather than listed: the €500m fine of 2025-04-23 showed the Commission will fine, the Article 6(4) case carries a statutory cap near $41.6bn of FY2025 revenue, the General Court upheld gatekeeper status on 2026-07-08, and Korea fined Apple and Google a combined $47.6m on 2026-10-28 — cash small beside the precedent that the commission is contestable. [S93, S47, S134, S136]

### The FY2027 charge the 10-Q hides in the current portion

Earnings are clean in the narrow sense and the margin is not. Apple publishes no adjusted EPS, but the amortisation that never appears as a line item is visible on the balance sheet: the current portion of intangible assets, net rose to $5,075M from $2,208M, putting $2.9bn more amortisation into the next twelve months — 55bp of FY2027 revenue, $0.16 of EPS, 1.7% of consensus. Gross intangibles of $38,220M grew $13,270M in nine months while other purchase obligations rose $14.5bn to $29.3bn, so the item is a contracted cash cost as well as an accrual; paid over three years it is $4.8bn a year, 3.5% of trailing free cash flow. That is why 1.06x conversion is arithmetically sound and economically incomplete: had the $13,270M been cash, conversion was 0.96x. Inventories rose 94% to $11,092M, and the $111.0B of owner cash behind the $158 DCF is 22% below the $142.36B of free cash the yield is quoted on. [S6, S47]

### 40x needs a discount rate no long-only fund can underwrite

On $111.0B of owner cash — $142.36B of free cash less $13.7B of stock compensation and $17.7B of contracted intangible purchases — with 3.5% terminal growth, $348.91 is fair only at a WACC near 6.4%, a 1.3% equity risk premium over a 4.99% Treasury at a 1.1 beta. The model gives $158 at 9.5% and $198 at 8.5%, a $132-$198 grid across 8.5-10.5% WACC and 2.5-3.5% growth, so 40x needs a required return three points under the 9.5% the valuation itself uses. The 18.1x peer median is a low yardstick: Samsung's 12.9x bottoms exactly when memory earnings peak, and the three US peers alone give 21.3x, so the premium is 88% rather than 122%. Peer value and DCF both land at $158, 55% below the price, leaving the reverse DCF for committee: at 9.5% the price needs about 17% free-cash-flow growth for a decade or about 7.1% in perpetuity. The buyback is not value-destructive because 2.5% compares badly with a 4.99% coupon; it is value-destructive because the price exceeds the valuation's own intrinsic value, and management agrees: repurchases fell 12.0% to $62,094M in nine months and no insider bought a share in the twelve months to 2026-10-29 while $208.0m was sold. ## 投资潜力与投资逻辑 Investment Potential & Thesis

Apple passes the first three tests of the thesis and fails the fourth, which is the only one that decides a purchase at today's price. The need is real: more than 2.5 billion active devices generated $364,357M of revenue in nine months of FY2026, with a 49.1% gross margin and $136,683M of trailing free cash flow at 1.06x net income on capex of 2.2% of sales. The capability is defensible: silicon-OS co-design, an in-house modem, four FDA clearances and 65% of the $600-plus handset tier are not replicable within a product cycle. The economics scale: Services earns a 76% gross margin on a quarter of revenue. What fails is the price. At $348.91 the buyer pays 40.0x trailing earnings, 32.5x EV/EBIT and 36.5x FY2027E EPS against a four-peer median of 18.1x and an S&P 500 forward multiple of 18.59x on 2026-10-29, for a company whose consensus EPS growth decelerates to 8.1% in FY2027 [S6].

### The disagreement is about what produced 2026

Our difference with consensus is about the durability of the current growth rate, not about quality. The 43-analyst consensus target of $332.39 sits 4.7% below the close, and Sell plus Strong Sell ratings rose from one to six between May and October 2026 while the shares gained 28.6%: the sell side is behind the price, not bearish on the franchise. We agree with the quality call and disagree that 2026 revealed a second growth engine: global shipments fall 16.7% while ASPs rise 27.6%, so growth is price and mix; Apple's share gain came partly from Android vendors retreating under memory costs; and 2 points of the June-quarter 50.1% gross margin were one-off tariff refunds. The edge is about price more than insight: below a 4% ten-year yield, the same cash flows support a higher value [S93].

The strongest counter-case is that the quality deserves the multiple. A long-only fund that owns the S&P 500 already holds 7.25% Apple through the index, so the active decision is whether to hold more than the benchmark; at 36.5x forward earnings the answer is no until the price or the growth changes [S97, S93].

### The price at which the case turns

The case turns at a price. Risk-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $9.10 is the base and bear cases weighted 60/40 — 0.60 × $9.56 + 0.40 × $8.42, where $8.42 is the bear's $8.60 less the $0.18 of FY2027 amortisation on the FY2026 intangible additions; the bull is excluded because it needs unit evidence the filings do not yet show. At 30-33x that gives an entry band of $273-$300, and the top is the probability-weighted value itself, so nothing above $300 should be bought. The decision tree: watch at zero position until the FY2026 fourth-quarter print on 2026-11-02 and the December quarter; buy a starter at or below $300 if gross margin holds at 48% or better excluding refunds with double-digit Services growth; pass if memory takes gross margin below 47% or a final remedy removes commission. Confidence is high that the current price has no margin of safety and medium on the level of fair value, because the WACC moves the discounted value from $132 to $198. Open diligence: does the FY2026 10-K disclose intangible lives and the licensing counterparty, and does the December quarter hold 48% gross margin ex-refund? The fastest falsifier is evidence that the AI cycle is producing units rather than features [S7].
