## ESG评估 ESG Assessment

Apple's ESG exposure is a platform-regulation problem, not a carbon or governance one: seven jurisdictions target the 75.4%-gross-margin Services pool — $109.2bn of FY2025 sales and $82.3bn of gross profit, 42.2% of the total — while fines to date (€500m EU, €150m France, $15.5m Korea) are less than 0.2% of $416.2bn of net sales and the remedies can permanently lower the highest-margin revenue Apple has. [S5, S134, S137, S136]

### The EU has established the principle; the size is still open

On 2025-04-23 the European Commission fined Apple €500m for breaching the DMA's anti-steering obligation and ordered the restrictions removed within 60 days; a separate Article 6(4) case on developer contract terms, opened 2024-06-24, remains unresolved with a statutory ceiling of 10% of worldwide net sales ($41.6bn). The fine is a rounding error, but the principle is durable: the General Court rejected Apple's challenge to its gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08. The cash question is the EU link-out commission. [S6, S134, S135]

### The US is the largest and slowest remedy risk

The DOJ and 15 states plus DC sued Apple for monopolization on 2024-03-21 in New Jersey seeking equitable relief; the motion to dismiss failed and by July 2026 the parties were in early settlement talks, with discovery to late May 2027 and no trial date. In Epic v. Apple the district court found contempt on 2025-04-30 and barred fees on out-of-app purchases; the Ninth Circuit on 2025-12-11 allowed some link-out commission and the Supreme Court agreed to review the contempt standard on 2026-06-30. Google search remedies finalised in December 2025 also threaten distribution payments inside Services, of undisclosed size. [S6, S62, S138]

### Enforcement is fragmenting; privacy is now an antitrust issue

The UK CMA designated Apple with strategic market status on 2025-10-22 and by 2026-10-20 was consulting on steering and NFC conduct requirements. Korea's communications regulator fined Apple KRW 20.81bn ($15.5m) on 2026-10-28 and ordered payment links and revised commissions, ruling a 26% fee on third-party billing evaded the 30% norm. Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act took effect on 2025-12-18, and 48 Chinese developers complained to SAMR on 2026-06-23. France's competition authority fined Apple €150m on 2025-03-31 over App Tracking Transparency, treating a privacy feature as abuse of dominance. The pattern is convergence of the global take rate toward the mid-teens, not one catastrophic penalty. [S132, S136, S140, S139, S141, S137]

### Environmental, labour and governance risks are not the discount drivers

Apple's 2025 emissions were more than 60% below 2015 and flat versus 2024, against a 2030 target of a 75% cut before carbon removals balance the remainder; removal volumes and costs are undisclosed, so the claim is only partially verified. Manufacturing remains concentrated in China, India and Vietnam, and the 10-K flags supplier industrial-accident risk; India's production-linked incentive has shifted capacity — cumulative iPhone exports passed $50bn by December 2025 and reached ₹2 lakh crore in FY2026 — but this is subsidy-supported diversification, not a structural cost advantage. Governance is cleaner than the sector: one share class, an independent chair in Art Levinson and eight directors; the 2026 proxy discloses no material related-party transactions beyond a former operating chief's family member earning above $120,000, and Tim Cook's 2025 target pay was $59m with 92% support on the 2025 say-on-pay vote. The live issues are succession (Cook is 65) and political exposure: shareholders rejected a "China Entanglement Audit" proposal on 2026-02-24. There is no dual-class discount. [S144, S145, S146, S143, S5, S52, S100]

### Policy is two different risks: sunk tax and reversible trade

The policy matrix separates sunk tax from reversible trade. State Aid is finished cash — the ECJ confirmed the Commission's 2016 decision on 2024-09-10 — a precedent risk, not an open liability. Tariffs are the opposite: the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and Apple is claiming refunds, the Section 232 semiconductor review imposed no tariffs on Apple's products on 2026-01-14, but Section 301 actions remain live. Price trade policy as gross-margin volatility, not permanent impairment. [S6]

### What the investor should price

Separate the fine from the remedy. Fines to date are immaterial, and even a maximum DMA fine would be a single charge. The durable exposure is the commission pool: the matrix shows what a cut in Services gross profit would do to operating income. That argues for a haircut to Services earnings, not for avoiding the stock. Confidence is medium because Apple does not disclose App Store revenue or take rates, and the DOJ and EU timetables have slipped repeatedly.

### Diligence questions

Five questions would change the assessment: what share of Services revenue and gross profit is App Store commission revenue by region; what commission Apple collects on US and EU link-outs; whether Article 6(4) brings periodic penalties or structural separation; the annual value of Google search-distribution payments; and the contracted volume and cost of carbon removals behind Apple 2030. The first two sit outside the public filing set; a PACER data request has been filed. If App Store commission revenue is below a tenth of Services gross profit, regulation is a sentiment issue; if a quarter or more, an earnings issue.

### The recommendation and what changes it

The rating is Watchlist with a zero position, a 12-24 month horizon and medium evidence confidence. It changes in three directions. ### Position sizing and the regime

Three actions come before any purchase.
